# Implementation Requirement Teardown

This scratchpad reverse-engineers requirements from the current implementation. The code is treated as an implementation of an unavailable PRD; the existence of a code path is evidence of an implied requirement, not evidence that the requirement is still valid.

No product code is changed or deleted during this exercise.

## Working objective

This repository is an Omi clone used as bootstrap scaffolding for a different macOS product. Optimize for the shortest credible path to shipping and operating that Mac app:

- question every behavior implemented by the inherited code rather than treating Omi's product decisions as requirements;
- keep useful, already-working Mac behavior when it serves the new product;
- make private product data local-authoritative by default and remove unnecessary cloud copies, synchronization, reconciliation, and cross-device projections;
- minimize hosted infrastructure, especially per-user compute, vector stores, duplicated databases, and background control planes;
- retain hosted compute only when a separately approved behavior actually requires it, such as the cloud-STT fallback or transient Gemini analysis;
- use the existing implementation as battle-tested scaffolding when localizing retained behavior instead of casually replacing it with a weaker redesign;
- treat the Windows product and every Windows-only build, test, release, generated-client, and documentation surface as outside this macOS audit: do not inspect, modify, or delete them, and behave as though they do not exist unless the user explicitly reopens that scope;

## Review method

For each implemented subsystem:

1. State the requirement implied by the implementation.
2. Trace the current production path from its real callers.
3. Identify which user-facing behavior depends on it.
4. Decide whether that behavior is required.
5. If it is not required, define the complete deletion boundary without deleting anything yet.
6. Separate similarly named systems so deleting one does not accidentally remove another.
7. Maintain a dependency graph and an explicit unresolved frontier. Reviewing one branch may expose sibling branches; those siblings stay visible until separately resolved.
8. A `keep local` decision preserves the agreed user-visible behavior behind a real local authority. It does not authorize a degraded fallback, stub, or deletion of adjacent behavior merely because the current implementation is cloud-backed. Any product simplification must be decided explicitly; only remote storage, synchronization, and cloud-only coordination disappear automatically.
9. After parallel ledger edits, run `python3 bootstrap-scaffold/validate-requirements-ledger.py`; closure requires one numerically indexed reviewed row and exactly one final `### Decision` section per IR, with no missing, duplicate, or stale-open graph entry.

Decisions are `keep`, `delete candidate`, or `unresolved`.

## Verified baseline

- Current HEAD is `f293b62603145af15ce230a230f88017dce95f4a`, aligned with `origin/main` at the start of this exercise.
- `ScreenActivitySyncService.swift` was deleted in that commit because the shared-backend copy of Rewind screen activity was not required.
- Local Rewind persistence, OCR indexing, embeddings, and local retrieval were retained.
- `FORK.md`, the attached backlog, and upstream product principles are not requirement authorities for this exercise.

## IR-009 - Windows excluded from the macOS audit; unused shared Rust crate

### Exact scope boundary

This exercise is only about shipping the macOS product. `desktop/windows/**` is a separate Electron product, but its requirements are not being accepted, rejected, simplified, or deleted here. The Windows app and every Windows-only source, test, dependency, generated client, workflow, release lane, installer, document, failure-class entry, and repository check must be treated as though it does not exist for this audit.

That means a later macOS cleanup must not use an adjacent Windows implementation as a reason to preserve something, and it must not edit or remove Windows merely because the Mac no longer needs a shared backend behavior. Windows can be reconsidered only if the user explicitly reopens its scope.

### Verified shared-Rust status

`desktop/shared-rust` is different: it was presented as a platform-neutral `omi-desktop-core` crate, but the live checkout proves it has no consumer:

- its three source files define fallback-label helpers, Gemini provider/model-tier policy, and one EqSwift export;
- neither the macOS Swift/Node product nor the Windows product imports or links the crate;
- no build or CI workflow compiles the Desktop Cargo workspace;
- the only live repository references are `desktop/Cargo.toml`, its generated `desktop/Cargo.lock`, and `FORK.md`, which already states that neither app builds it; and
- several of its model-tier/provider policies duplicate or conflict with model-system decisions already made in this audit.

### Decision

`ignore Windows completely; delete only the verified-unused shared Rust zombie`

Confirmed: do not inspect, question, modify, or delete `desktop/windows/**` or any Windows-only build, test, release, generated-client, documentation, or repository surface. Do not perform Windows cleanup as a consequence of macOS decisions.

Delete `desktop/shared-rust/**`, `desktop/Cargo.toml`, and `desktop/Cargo.lock` when implementation begins because that standalone workspace has no surviving consumer or behavior. This deletion does not touch the macOS Swift app, its local Node/Pi runtime, the Python backend, any retained Rust SDK elsewhere in the repository, or any Windows file.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-938 - External task integrations and automatic export

### Exact current behavior

The canonical Python backend mounts `task_integrations.router` even though IR-025 makes the Mac's GRDB `action_items` table the sole authority for ordinary tasks. The router and `utils/task_integrations_ops.py` implement OAuth, token refresh, provider-specific discovery, stored connection/default state, and task creation for Todoist, Asana, Google Tasks, and ClickUp. The provider callbacks return Omi deep links, and environment configuration supplies each provider's client ID and secret.

`utils/task_sync.py` then makes this more than an on-demand API. New backend action items and conversation-extracted action items automatically export to the user's default integration. Accepted task and workstream candidates take a second durable path: their transactions write `candidate_integration_outbox`, `candidate_service.py` claims/completes/retries its leased dispatch through `auto_sync_action_item`, and `POST /v1/candidates/integrations/drain` schedules pending work. A Firestore composite index, registry entry, generated client, focused lifecycle/router tests, and the `task_candidate_lifecycle` workflow invariant keep that integration-only queue executable.

A separate Apple Reminders branch marks `sync_requested`, sends a mobile push so another client can create reminders, and exposes bidirectional `GET /v1/action-items/pending-sync` plus `PATCH /v1/action-items/sync-batch` routes. Their request/response models and Firestore helpers read and write `sync_requested`, `exported`, `export_date`, `export_platform`, and `apple_reminder_id`. Firestore user records separately retain integration credentials, defaults, list/project selections, and connection metadata. The Mac has generated bindings but no handwritten retained caller that needs this hosted product.

This is not local task CRUD, local Task Assistant extraction, task creation by Chat/PTT, or the native notification/reminder behavior that stays inside this product. It is outbound synchronization of product tasks into external task systems and depends on cloud task authority and mobile/Omi behavior already rejected elsewhere.

### Decision

`delete the complete external task-integration and export product`

Confirmed: remove `task_integrations.router` and registration; provider OAuth URL, callback, token-exchange/refresh, discovery and task-write endpoints; Todoist, Asana, Google Tasks, and ClickUp clients, credentials, settings, stored tokens/defaults/list/project metadata, generated non-Windows bindings, tests, docs, metrics, and deployment configuration; `task_integrations_ops.py`; automatic single/batch export hooks from action-item, task-intelligence, and conversation processing; and the integration-only candidate dispatch machinery. The latter includes `candidate_integration_outbox` writes from task/workstream acceptance, its claim/complete/list lease helpers and exports, `candidate_service` dispatch/drain code, `/v1/candidates/integrations/drain`, its Firestore index plus registry entry, generated binding, focused candidate/workstream/router tests, and the integration-dispatch clause in the `task_candidate_lifecycle` workflow invariant. Preserve candidate creation/acceptance itself after removing that side effect.

Also remove the complete Apple Reminders export path. That path includes its mobile-push builder/sender, `batch_set_sync_requested`, `get_pending_apple_reminders_sync`, `batch_sync_update_action_items`, `/v1/action-items/pending-sync`, `/v1/action-items/sync-batch`, `SyncBatch*`/`PendingSyncResponse` models, the five export/sync fields where no other retained caller remains, route-policy/generated-client entries, mobile-lifecycle and focused unit tests, and current docs.

Preserve ordinary local tasks, local Task Assistant extraction, local recurrence/edit/complete/delete behavior, and retained Chat/PTT/proactive producers writing the authoritative GRDB store. Do not replace the deleted providers with a generic integration framework or silently add a native Apple Reminders integration. A future local/native export is a new product decision with its own authority and consent boundary.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-939 - Vendored universal libwebp release libraries

### Exact current behavior

Ordinary typed screen capture is live and depends on libwebp: `ScreenCaptureManager.captureScreenData()` encodes the current display as WebP through the `CWebP` system-library target, and typed Chat, floating-bar attachments, capture tools, artifact storage, and MIME detection consume that format. Local development obtains libwebp through Homebrew/pkg-config and bundles/signs the dylibs from that installation.

`desktop/macos/vendor/libwebp/` additionally contains libwebp 1.5.0 `libwebp.7.dylib` and `libsharpyuv.0.dylib`. Both are universal Mach-O binaries with `x86_64` and `arm64` slices. Their recorded SHA-256 values are `3515af9fc46957cbd3f879ee36b9bbc0283cf6e2bbd51032a943ec8a9e64b2ff` and `5a92b18c7deee56b134d1079712e41e77d151584c20e894a3a9c176e9f9ed119`. The accompanying README documents the original absent `codemagic.yaml` consumer: a universal release needs these cached binaries because the runner's Homebrew build is arm64-only, with a from-source universal rebuild as fallback.

The current checkout cannot prove a live root Codemagic consumer because that inherited file is missing and IR-892 assigns creation of the owned release definition to S-29. Deleting the cache now would not simplify the live WebP feature; it would merely force S-29 to rediscover or rebuild a small, already-documented universal dependency.

### Decision

`retain and re-own the universal libwebp cache with the Mac release system`

Confirmed: keep the two universal dylibs and the reproducible build instructions as an S-29 release input. The owned Codemagic/release definition must verify the expected version/checksums, both architectures, `@rpath` install names, minimum supported macOS version, signing, and the from-source fallback before copying them into a universal candidate. Update Omi names and missing-file claims when that owned consumer lands; do not treat a README as sufficient release wiring.

Preserve `CWebP`, ordinary typed WebP screen capture, local Homebrew/pkg-config development behavior, artifact MIME handling, and signed-bundle library rewriting. Do not convert typed capture to PTT's separate JPEG path or delete live screen understanding to remove two release artifacts.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-710 - Managed model for explicit-memory normalization

### Corrected current boundary

The earlier draft of this requirement attributed the complete promotion decision to `memory_l2`. Direct code tracing shows that the canonical pipeline splits two jobs:

```text
explicit user Add/Edit -> memory_l2 normalization
evidence-backed Short-term candidate -> memory_conflict consolidation (IR-730)
```

This correction does not reverse the selected provider or local-authority decision. It states precisely what the retained `memory_l2` call does.

### Exact current pattern

The required-processing path calls `get_llm("memory_l2")` for explicit user/API/MCP/plugin memory submissions. All three current model profiles resolve that feature to the same route:

```text
provider: OpenAI
model:    gpt-4.1-mini
```

The model receives the submitted text plus bounded provenance and authoritative source attribution. It must preserve every material detail while returning a concise, structured assertion: normalized content, subject identity, predicate, arguments, sensitivity labels, and rationale. It is not allowed to reject or silently downgrade an explicit user instruction to remember something.

Production code validates the structure and subject boundary, attaches an auditable processing receipt, and makes the result eligible for the later lifecycle decision. Provider, parsing, or validation failure changes no memory content and remains retryable.

IR-815 deletes the hosted job and IR-260 moves lifecycle authority to the Mac. The same-pattern adaptation is:

```text
Mac local lifecycle runner
  -> selects an explicit local Add/Edit awaiting normalization
  -> sends its bounded text, provenance and source attribution
  -> Python calls OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini and returns the structured normalization
  -> Mac validates against the current local revision and commits to GRDB, or retries later
```

The Mac does not receive or store an OpenAI API key. The Python backend does not become memory authority and does not persist a cloud memory copy. Memory text leaves the Mac only for this transient managed-model request and must stay out of raw logs and durable backend storage.

IR-608 removes the separate LLM gateway, so the canonical Python backend calls the provider directly. IR-609 removes premium/max/BYOK route switching, so this becomes one explicit workload route rather than three duplicated profiles.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the current OpenAI pattern.** Pin explicit-memory normalization to managed OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini, preserve the existing prompt, structured validation, and retry behavior, and move only state ownership/commit to the Mac.
2. **Move normalization to Gemini.** Rework the existing structured-output path and validate a new provider even though the current memory workload does not switch to Gemini in any profile.
3. **Run this model fully on-device.** Add and validate another local semantic model workload with its own download, resource, compatibility, and quality lifecycle.

### Recommendation

`keep the existing OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini memory_l2 normalization pattern and adapt its ownership boundary`

This is the smallest same-pattern adaptation. We keep the model and proven normalization/validation behavior; only the Mac becomes the source of input truth and owner of the final state change. Changing to Gemini or a new local model would add a separate quality migration without solving an architectural problem.

### Question

Should explicit local Add/Edit memories keep the current managed OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini normalization pattern, with the Mac owning when it runs and whether the returned proposal is committed?

### Decision

`keep the existing OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini memory_l2 normalization pattern and adapt its ownership boundary`

Confirmed after correcting the code-path description: pin explicit-memory normalization to managed OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini. Preserve the existing instruction to retain every material user-authored detail; bounded text/provenance/source packet; structured content, subject, predicate, argument, sensitivity and rationale output; subject and schema validation; auditable receipt; retryable provider/parse/validation failures; and no-mutation-on-failure behavior.

Move pending-item selection, current-revision validation, retries, receipt storage and the normalized local write to the Mac's lifecycle runner and authoritative GRDB store. Send only the bounded explicit assertion packet through the authenticated canonical Python backend for transient inference. The backend calls OpenAI directly under IR-608, returns the proposal, stores no cloud memory copy, and keeps raw memory content out of logs and durable backend state. The separate evidence-backed promote/archive/review/reject and duplicate/replace/merge/keep-both decision is retained under IR-730. Do not place an OpenAI key on the Mac, introduce Gemini provider migration, add an on-device replacement model, or restore premium/max/BYOK switching.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-711 - Hidden Premium/Max tier for retained Mac Gemini workloads

### Requirement implied by the model configuration

> The Mac must persist one global `premium` or `max` model-quality tier and silently change several retained Gemini workloads together.

This is separate from realtime PTT's user-visible Auto/Gemini/OpenAI provider choice. It applies to ordinary Gemini calls used by retained local-product features.

### Exact current behavior

`ModelQoS.activeTier` reads `modelQoS_activeTier` from UserDefaults and defaults to `premium`. The tiers currently resolve as follows:

| Retained workload | `premium` default | hidden `max` value |
|---|---|---|
| Focus, automatic screenshot memory extraction, AI User Profile synthesis, and PTT context vocabulary | `gemini-2.5-flash` | `gemini-2.5-pro` |
| automatic task extraction | `gemini-2.5-flash` | `gemini-2.5-pro` |
| periodic Insight generation | `gemini-2.5-flash` | `gemini-2.5-pro` |
| event-driven Live Suggestions | `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | `gemini-2.5-flash` |
| local embeddings | `gemini-embedding-001` | unchanged |

No production source writes `ModelQoS.activeTier`, exposes the tier in Settings, or selects it from a paid plan. Only tests write it. Therefore normal customers always follow the `premium` column unless the private UserDefaults key is manually injected.

The authenticated Python Gemini proxy still allowlists `gemini-2.5-pro`. If Pro is somehow requested, it silently rewrites Pro to Flash after 30 daily Gemini calls in the ordinary server tier, or after 300 calls when an unrelated `OMI_MODEL_TIER=max` environment value is set. No surviving production code sets the Mac tier from that server value, so the two hidden tier controls are not one coherent product policy.

### Concrete choices

1. **Pin the current reachable defaults.** Keep Gemini Flash for Focus/Memory/Profile/PTT vocabulary/Task/Insight, Flash-Lite with the existing Flash fallback for Live Suggestions, and the existing embedding model. Delete only the Mac's `ModelTier`, its UserDefaults key, Max branches, description, and exclusive tests. Leave the separately reachable Python-proxy Pro capability for its own audit.
2. **Keep the hidden tier unchanged.** Retain dormant UserDefaults and environment controls that can independently alter model quality without a product owner or visible setting.
3. **Expose a model-quality setting.** Add a new customer-facing or plan-driven Premium/Max product and define its billing, quota, disclosure, and cross-device behavior.

### Recommendation

`pin every retained Mac Gemini workload to its current reachable default and delete only the proven-dead Mac tier selector`

This preserves what customers actually receive today and follows IR-609's one-explicit-route-per-workload rule. It does not change prompts, cadence, local authority, result handling, or the retained Gemini proxy. Repository-wide tracing proves that only tests write `ModelQoS.activeTier`; production code only reads the default-derived workload constants. The Python proxy's authenticated Pro route is not deleted here because it remains directly reachable even though no in-tree product caller selects it.

### Question

Should we keep the current real behavior—Flash for the retained proactive workloads, Flash-Lite for Live Suggestions, and the existing embedding model—and delete only the verified-dead Mac Premium/Max selector?

### Decision

`delete only the verified-dead Mac Premium/Max selector; keep every live model caller and separately reachable proxy capability`

Confirmed with the user's dead-code condition: remove `ModelTier`, the private `modelQoS_activeTier` UserDefaults getter/setter and change notification, tier-dependent `switch` branches, `tierDescription`, and tests that exist only to activate or describe the unreachable Max state. Replace the surviving `ModelQoS.Gemini` accessors with fixed current-default values: Flash for proactive/Task/Insight workloads, Flash-Lite plus the existing Flash fallback for Live Suggestions, and the unchanged embedding model.

Do not delete the live `ModelQoS` namespace or its retained callers. Do not change prompts, cadence, proxy transport, local persistence, fallback behavior, realtime PTT provider selection, or embeddings. The unused shared-Rust tier disappears separately with the already-approved unused crate deletion under IR-009. Preserve the Python proxy's authenticated `gemini-2.5-pro` allowlist and Pro-to-Flash downgrade behavior for a separate reachability/compatibility decision because a crafted authenticated request can still invoke it.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-712 - Vertex AI and Gemini AI Studio paths behind the retained proxy

### What this is in plain English

> The Mac's retained Gemini features need our authenticated Python backend to reach the same Google Gemini models through either Vertex AI or Gemini AI Studio, depending on controlled server configuration and credential availability.

Vertex AI and Gemini AI Studio are not two different assistant products here. They are two Google-operated access paths to the same retained Gemini model names. This is also separate from realtime PTT's Gemini-versus-OpenAI provider choice.

### Exact current behavior

Every retained Mac Gemini call first reaches the canonical Python backend. The proxy authenticates the Firebase user, rejects an expired trial, applies shared Redis request limits, restricts model/action/body/output shape, strips unsupported request controls, and forwards the request without creating a durable server copy of the prompt, screenshot, or embedding text.

The upstream selection is:

```text
if customer Gemini BYOK exists
  -> Gemini AI Studio with the customer's key
else if GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT is configured and a Google service token succeeds
  -> Vertex AI with platform identity
else
  -> Gemini AI Studio with our server-side GEMINI_API_KEY
```

IR-062 already deletes the first branch because customer BYOK is not part of this product. The other two branches are platform-owned managed compute. The checked-in production desktop-backend workflow explicitly installs our Gemini API key, so the AI Studio route is deployable. Vertex remains executable whenever the runtime carries `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and usable Google credentials. Local development intentionally supports the server-side API-key path.

The two Google APIs have slightly different embedding request/response shapes, and the proxy already adapts them so the Mac sees one stable contract. If Vertex credential acquisition throws, current code falls back to the platform AI Studio key. An ordinary non-success response returned by Vertex is passed back to the Mac; it does not replay the same content through Studio.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the existing two-route managed pattern.** Use Vertex when explicitly configured and credentialed; retain our AI Studio key for local development and credential-acquisition fallback. Remove only customer-BYOK selection and keep the Mac unaware of the upstream route.
2. **Use AI Studio only.** Delete Vertex identity, endpoint selection, and embedding transforms. This is simpler code but removes an already implemented platform-identity route.
3. **Use Vertex only.** Delete the API-key route, making local development and a Vertex credential failure fail closed unless every environment obtains Google platform identity.

### Recommendation

`keep Vertex plus platform-owned AI Studio fallback exactly as the managed proxy pattern; delete only customer BYOK routing`

Neither platform-owned route is dead. Keeping both preserves the current production/development options without exposing provider infrastructure to customers or duplicating local state. The Mac still makes one authenticated proxy call and receives one response; only our backend chooses the Google access path.

### Question

Should the retained Gemini proxy keep Vertex when explicitly configured plus our server-owned AI Studio path for local development and Vertex credential fallback, while removing only the already-rejected customer-BYOK branch?

### Decision

`keep Vertex plus platform-owned AI Studio fallback exactly as the managed proxy pattern; delete only customer BYOK routing`

Confirmed: retain one authenticated Mac-facing Gemini proxy contract with both platform-owned Google upstream routes. When the runtime explicitly provides a Google Cloud project and obtains platform credentials, use Vertex AI; otherwise use our server-side Gemini AI Studio key, including local development and the existing Vertex credential-acquisition fallback. Preserve the current request/response adaptation that hides the two Google API shapes from the Mac, including embedding conversion.

Remove only the customer-key branch and `get_byok_key("gemini")` selection under IR-062. Customers do not choose the Google access route, provide a Gemini key, or gain a second billing path. Keep prompts/results transient in the proxy with no durable server content copy. Do not collapse to one Google route, add a customer-facing switch, or alter realtime PTT's separate provider portfolio.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-713 - Managed Gemini proxy authentication, limits, and payload guardrails

### Requirement implied by the retained proxy

> Every managed Gemini generation, streaming, and embedding request must pass one account and cost-safety boundary before our provider credentials pay for it.

This does not choose a Gemini model or Google access route. IR-711 pins the ordinary model workloads and IR-712 keeps Vertex plus platform-owned AI Studio access. IR-713 is the shared front door around those calls.

### Exact current behavior

Before forwarding a request, the Python proxy:

- requires a valid Firebase user identity;
- returns `402 trial_expired` when the retained desktop trial paywall is enabled and that account has exhausted it without paid access;
- counts every generation, streaming, and embedding proxy request for that UID in Redis;
- permits at most 30 requests in 60 seconds and 1,500 requests in 24 hours;
- fails closed with `503` when the Redis limiter is unavailable, rather than spending against an unmetered provider path;
- permits only allowlisted Gemini models and four explicit actions;
- rejects request bodies over 5 MiB;
- rejects more than one candidate, clamps requested output to 8,192 tokens, and supplies the existing bounded thinking budget;
- strips client-supplied safety and cached-content controls before forwarding; and
- returns sanitized product errors to the Mac without logging raw prompt/screenshot/embedding content in this route.

The limits are per account, not per Mac or per feature. For example, a runaway Focus loop and a separate embedding loop under the same signed-in UID consume the same 30-per-minute and 1,500-per-day counters. Normal proactive cadence is far below the daily ceiling; the boundary is primarily protection against bugs, automation loops, or deliberate bulk use.

The Mac converts `429`/quota responses into the generic temporary message **AI service is busy. Please try again in a moment.** The existing expected-product-state copy still mentions BYOK; IR-062 requires removing that stale wording and adapting entitlement language to the Dodo-backed plan, without changing the guardrail mechanics.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the exact shared guardrail pattern.** Preserve Firebase authentication, retained entitlement/trial gating, the 30/minute and 1,500/day UID counters, fail-closed Redis behavior, model/action allowlists, and payload/output bounds. Adapt only rejected BYOK/Omi billing copy and configuration ownership.
2. **Delete application-side limits.** Rely only on Google project quotas and billing alerts, allowing one account or bad client loop to consume the shared provider budget until the provider intervenes.
3. **Create plan-specific dynamic Gemini limits.** Define new per-Dodo-plan proactive/embedding allowances, UI, usage reporting, and enforcement instead of the current universal safety ceiling.

### Recommendation

`keep the current shared Gemini proxy guardrails exactly; adapt only entitlement ownership and stale BYOK copy`

These controls are live and protect a retained paid-compute route. The fixed limits are simple, already shared across all proxy workloads, and high enough for ordinary usage. Removing them increases cost risk; turning them into a customer plan matrix creates a new quota product that the current UI and billing contract do not implement.

### Question

Should we keep the current authenticated and entitlement-gated Gemini proxy boundary, including the exact 30-requests-per-minute and 1,500-per-day account limits, fail-closed Redis behavior, and request/output caps?

### Decision

`keep the current shared Gemini proxy guardrails exactly; adapt only entitlement ownership and stale BYOK copy`

Confirmed: retain Firebase authentication; the retained desktop entitlement/trial gate; shared per-UID Redis counters covering generation, streaming, and embeddings; the exact 30-request/60-second burst ceiling and 1,500-request/24-hour hard ceiling; fail-closed `503` behavior when the limiter is unavailable; model/action allowlists; the 5 MiB request cap; one-candidate rule; 8,192-token output clamp; bounded thinking configuration; and the existing request-control sanitization.

Keep these as universal managed-compute safety ceilings rather than a new customer-visible plan matrix. Adapt only Omi/BYOK entitlement wording and configuration to the retained Dodo-backed account contract under IR-006/062/191. Preserve transient proxy handling and sanitized errors; do not add durable prompt, screenshot, or embedding-text storage.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-714 - Callerless ElevenLabs TTS route beside retained Mac OpenAI TTS

### Requirement claimed by the backend route

> The new macOS product requires a second authenticated text-to-speech API backed by ElevenLabs, with arbitrary ElevenLabs voice/model/output settings, in addition to the retained OpenAI voice route.

### Exact current behavior and reachability

The canonical Python application mounts two unrelated TTS implementations:

```text
POST /v1/tts/synthesize
  -> OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts
  -> live Mac caller
  -> Onyx/Shimmer/Coral/Nova UI retained exactly by IR-224
  -> macOS system-speech fallback

POST /v2/tts/synthesize
  -> ElevenLabs
  -> arbitrary ElevenLabs voice ID, model ID, output format, and voice settings
  -> no retained Mac caller
```

Repository-wide tracing finds no production call to `/v2/tts/synthesize`. The route's own documentation calls it a mobile/background/lock-screen contract, but this checkout contains no mobile application source. The Mac's API client, playback service, tests, and product settings use `/v1/tts/synthesize`; the distinct `/v2` shape appears only in backend route/model/tests, OpenAPI inventory, excluded Windows generated compatibility, and comments.

The backend also exposes an `elevenlabs_voice_id` field in the floating-bar settings response, and the Mac decodes/tests it, but no Mac production behavior reads that decoded value. The visible voice selection is the locally persisted four-OpenAI catalog from IR-224.

This route owns its own ElevenLabs request model, secret/config entry, upstream client and semaphore, arbitrary-voice validation, 50-request/minute and 10,000-character/day policy, 5,000-character request cap, streaming adapter, tests, and OpenAPI surface. Its Redis `check_tts_rate_limit` primitive is shared with the live OpenAI route and therefore is not dead.

### Concrete choices

1. **Delete the verified callerless ElevenLabs slice.** Remove `/v2/tts/synthesize`, its request models, ElevenLabs-only secret/config, upstream client/semaphore, settings field/decoder, tests, OpenAPI registration, and exclusive docs. Keep the shared Redis rate-limit primitive and the complete `/v1` OpenAI Mac path.
2. **Keep it for hypothetical clients.** Continue operating and securing an additional paid voice vendor contract with no retained product caller.
3. **Switch the Mac to ElevenLabs.** Replace the explicitly retained OpenAI voice catalog and route, reopening IR-224 and requiring a new voice/fallback migration.

### Recommendation

`delete the callerless ElevenLabs /v2 TTS slice; preserve the live OpenAI /v1 route exactly`

This is dead-code deletion rather than a voice redesign. It removes a second provider, request contract, secret, and operational path that the retained Mac cannot invoke. It does not change spoken PTT, typed-answer playback, previews, prewarming, playback speed, or macOS system fallback.

Windows remains outside this macOS audit under IR-009; do not edit Windows files merely because a generated schema mentions `/v2`. Do not remove an `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` occurrence proven to belong to another independently retained deployment such as a self-hosted third-party chart.

### Question

Should we delete the verified-unused ElevenLabs `/v2/tts/synthesize` route and its exclusive support code while keeping the live OpenAI `/v1/tts/synthesize` Mac route exactly unchanged?

### Decision

`delete the callerless ElevenLabs /v2 TTS slice; preserve the live OpenAI /v1 route exactly`

Confirmed: remove the canonical backend's `/v2/tts/synthesize` registration and handler; `backend/models/tts.py`; ElevenLabs-only arbitrary voice/model/output/voice-settings validation and streaming adapter; the route-exclusive upstream HTTP client/semaphore; product-backend ElevenLabs secret/template/harness requirements proven exclusive to this route; the unused `elevenlabs_voice_id` settings response field and Mac decoder/test; route-specific OpenAPI inventory; and exclusive backend tests/docs.

Preserve the complete authenticated `/v1/tts/synthesize` OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` route, Onyx/Shimmer/Coral/Nova catalog, Shimmer default, voice instructions, preview/prewarm behavior, playback speed, macOS system-speech fallback, entitlement checks, OpenAI route limits, and the shared Redis `check_tts_rate_limit` primitive. Do not edit excluded Windows files under IR-009 or remove an ElevenLabs credential/config occurrence owned by another independently retained deployment without a separate caller audit.

No product code has been changed.

```text
  -> Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite returns title-only text
```

## IR-724 - GPT-personalized subscription and usage-limit notifications

### Exact current behavior

The Python backend has a second notification model workload that is separate from both the deleted Mentor/App pipeline in IR-723 and the retained local Mac proactive assistants:

```text
subscription purchase
  -> read as many as 100 Firestore memories
  -> ask OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini to write a warm welcome under 150 characters
  -> send it through Firebase Cloud Messaging

transcription allowance reached
  -> read as many as 50 Firestore memories
  -> ask OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini to write a personalized upgrade warning
```

The model is only writing the wording. It does not decide whether a purchase succeeded, how much usage remains, whether transcription is blocked, or which plan the account owns. Those facts come from the retained billing, entitlement, and quota systems.

For example, when an account has genuinely reached its transcription allowance, the important product behavior is a truthful state such as `transcription allowance reached`, the applicable plan/usage details, and the available next action. Confirmed: remove the `notifications` model route; subscription-notification usage feature; GPT prompts and generation helpers for purchase welcomes and credit-limit warnings; Firestore memory lookup used by those prompts; Redis recently-sent state used only for the generated credit-limit push; purchase-webhook welcome-push caller; live-listen generated credit-warning push caller; and exclusive tests, fixtures, configuration, telemetry, and documentation.

Keep quota enforcement, plan and usage details, the paywall/upgrade action, billing reconciliation and purchase status UI, Dodo subscription work, and relevant error/case/support information.

Do not replace these two deleted messages with a different LLM or with local-memory personalization. This decision does not alter the retained automatic Chat greeting, automatic Chat title, direct OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini integrations, local Mac proactive assistants, or the separately static silent-user nudge; that static nudge has no `notifications` model call and remains governed by the FCM/product-lifecycle decisions that own it.

## IR-726 - Provider for retained live transcript translation

### Exact current behavior

Production configures an ordered translation chain:

```text
foreign-language cloud-STT segment
  -> self-hosted Meta NLLB model on a separate GPU/GKE service
  -> if NLLB fails, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite through the existing managed Gemini integration
  -> validate and cache the translated sentence
  -> return it to the Mac for local display and storage
```

NLLB is not a small library inside the canonical backend. It has its own model image, CUDA/CTranslate2 runtime, GPU deployment, Helm chart, autoscaling, internal URL, release workflow, benchmarks, alerts, metrics, and fallback policy. Repository tuning results say the tested 1.3-billion-parameter model does not meet the intended 250-millisecond realtime p99 budget; the smaller 600-million-parameter option trades away quality to approach that target.

Gemini translation is already implemented and already serves as the configured recovery provider. When no usable provider list is supplied, the current code already defaults to Gemini.

### Decision

`delete self-hosted NLLB and use Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite alone`

Confirmed: keep retained cloud-STT live translation, but make the existing managed Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite structured-output route its single provider. Preserve target-language rules, language detection, sentence splitting and batching, cardinality/empty-response validation, deduplication, positive and negative caching, bounded failure behavior, useful metrics, local Mac result authority, live italic presentation, and later local display.

Remove the NLLB provider adapter and language-token compatibility unique to it; NLLB model service and Docker image; CUDA/CTranslate2/model-download runtime; health and translation endpoints; GPU/GKE deployment, chart, autoscaling, monitoring, release workflow, image contracts, runtime URL/secrets/settings, benchmarks/tuning scripts, fallback-to/from-NLLB branches, and exclusive tests/documentation. Collapse provider-selection configuration to the one explicit translation route instead of retaining a one-item provider list.

If Gemini translation fails, preserve the original transcript and the existing bounded missing/retryable-translation behavior; do not block or discard transcription. Do not add translation to local Parakeet, upload locally produced Parakeet text, change the visible translation UI, or alter unrelated direct Gemini workloads.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-727 - Managed models for retained conversation enrichment

### Exact current behavior

After a conversation is accepted for enrichment, Python currently performs two separately tuned structured jobs:

```text
conversation structure call
  -> transcript, language, local-time context and available participant/context hints
  -> OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini under the default direct profile
  -> generated title, overview, emoji, category and calendar commitments

action-item call
  -> transcript, language, time zone and potentially related open tasks
  -> OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini under the default direct profile
  -> validated tasks and due dates
```

The two prompts and response contracts solve different problems. The structure call describes the conversation; the action-item call applies ownership, commitment, deduplication and due-date rules. Combining them would change prompt behavior, validation, failure isolation and test expectations rather than merely localizing storage.

IR-608 deletes the separate LLM gateway, and IR-609 deletes the Premium/Max/BYOK profile system. IR-349/353/357/364/365 retain the useful summary, authoritative linked tasks, local calendar commitments, title and emoji while other decisions delete generated category, Apps, wearable-photo input, automatic folders, hosted calendar writes and cloud conversation/task authority.

### Decision

`keep the two existing OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini jobs with local result authority`

Confirmed: retain separate `conv_structure` and `conv_action_items` computations using their existing OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini prompt patterns, structured response validation, language and deterministic local-time handling, due-date normalization, conservative task-quality rules, related-task deduplication semantics, bounded errors, usage accounting and focused behavioral tests.

Adapt the ownership boundary: the Mac owns the accepted finalized transcript and supplies only the bounded transcript plus independently retained local language, time-zone, conversation-local speaker/context and related-task facts needed for transient computation. Python returns candidate structure and action items without creating or loading a hosted conversation, task, session or processing record. The Mac validates the response against the local enrichment generation, assigns local identities, and commits accepted title, overview, emoji, calendar commitments and linked tasks through the authoritative local transaction.

Remove the global quality-profile and BYOK switching already rejected by IR-609; standalone-gateway/auto-lane/shadow/promotion machinery already rejected by IR-608; Firestore conversation/task reads and writes; server-owned processing state and IDs; rejected category, wearable-photo, App/integration and automatic-folder inputs/outputs; and exclusive compatibility, synchronization and cloud-authority tests. Manual title edits and ordinary local task edit/completion behavior continue to override or mutate their authoritative local records.

This does not alter normal Chat's direct Anthropic Sonnet loop, automatic Chat greeting/title jobs, Gemini translation or proactive-assistant workloads, realtime PTT, or local Parakeet transcription.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-728 - Managed model for conversation-derived Memory extraction

The canonical conversation-memory path sends the readable speaker-prefixed transcript to the `memory_l1` workload. Every current model profile resolves that workload to OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini. The current backend then rechecks quoted evidence against hosted transcript segments, derives user/third-party/unknown subject attribution, assigns deterministic IDs, and writes the accepted items into the hosted canonical memory lifecycle. ## IR-730 - Managed consolidation and conflict judgment for Short-term memories

### Exact current behavior

The canonical lifecycle has a second model call after broad `memory_l1` capture. `memory_conflict` receives a bounded batch of evidence-backed Short-term candidates plus relevant active memories found by semantic similarity. Every current model profile resolves this workload to OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini.

Despite the route name, this call owns the full durable consolidation proposal. It must return exactly one decision for every pending candidate:

- lifecycle route: **promote**, **archive**, **review**, or **reject**;
- relationship to existing memory: **create**, **duplicate**, **replace**, **merge**, or **keep both**;
- any target or superseded memory IDs;
- proposed durable text and structured subject/predicate/arguments;
- exact supporting evidence IDs; and
- relationship-to-user, aboutness, basis, confidence, and rationale fields used by the safety policy.

Deterministic production code then checks that no candidate was omitted or invented; every referenced memory/evidence ID came from the supplied packet; restricted or third-party material was not promoted incorrectly; two decisions do not supersede the same target; and replacement/merge relationships are internally consistent. Invalid output or provider failure commits nothing and remains retryable or eventually enters explicit review.

For example, if local memory already says “Lives in New York” and a new evidence-backed candidate says “Moved to Tallinn,” the model can propose promoting Tallinn and superseding New York. The Mac must still verify that both IDs are current local records and that the evidence and subject boundaries are valid before applying the transition.

This is not the older per-fact legacy conflict helper removed under IR-729. It is the canonical batch consolidation pattern. It is also separate from `memory_l1` initial capture and `memory_l2` normalization of explicit Add/Edit assertions.

### Decision

`keep the existing OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini memory_conflict consolidation pattern with local authority`

Confirmed: retain the canonical batch prompt; OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini route; promote/archive/review/reject and create/duplicate/replace/merge/keep-both vocabulary; total one-decision-per-input contract; bounded similarity context; subject, evidence, sensitivity, aboutness, relationship and recurrence rules; supersession/merge semantics; structured output; deterministic allowlist and conservation validation; no-mutation-on-invalid-output behavior; retry/review escalation; usage accounting; and focused behavioral tests.

Adapt the ownership boundary: the Mac's local lifecycle runner selects a bounded due Short-term batch and relevant active local memories, assigns an input-generation identity, and sends only that packet through the authenticated canonical Python backend for transient inference. Python calls OpenAI directly, returns a proposed batch, and stores no memory, evidence, retry, cursor, watermark or decision record. The Mac validates every returned candidate, target, supersession and evidence reference against the same current local generation, then atomically commits accepted lifecycle and audit transitions to GRDB. Provider, parse, stale-generation or validation failure changes nothing and is retried locally under the retained bounded policy.

Remove the Cloud Run scheduler/job, Firestore candidate hydration and writes, hosted retry leases/cursors/watermarks/outbox, cohort gating, cloud graph/recurrence handoffs already rejected elsewhere, global quality/BYOK and gateway switching, the legacy per-memory resolver deleted under IR-729, and exclusive cloud-authority tests. Do not combine this prompt with `memory_l1`, make Python authoritative, put an OpenAI key on the Mac, or alter manual Add/Edit normalization under IR-710.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-732 - Managed discard judgment for short ambient conversations

### Exact current behavior

The retained automatic-capture policy under IR-362 has two deterministic fast paths and one model path:

```text
empty transcript       -> discard without a model call
more than 100 words    -> keep without a model call
short nonempty content -> call conv_discard
```

The `conv_discard` prompt asks whether the short content contains a concrete task, request, decision, commitment, follow-up question, personal fact, appointment, important interaction, insight, or other durable value. Very short filler, acknowledgements, noise and incomplete fragments should be discarded; recordings under two minutes receive the existing higher bar. A lenient structured parser reduces the response to one boolean.

The reachable default model profile routes this call to OpenAI GPT-4.1-nano. If provider invocation or parsing fails, the current code returns **keep**, preventing a model outage from silently deleting potentially valuable content. Wearable-photo descriptions currently influence the prompt but are already deleted under IR-359.

For example, “Yeah, okay, thanks” may be discarded, while “Call Sarah tomorrow at nine” is kept. A normal transcript over 100 words is kept without paying for this judgment.

### Decision

`keep the existing OpenAI GPT-4.1-nano conv_discard pattern with local conversation authority`

Confirmed: retain the empty-content discard fast path; over-100-word automatic keep; duration-aware higher bar for recordings under two minutes; existing meaningful-content versus filler criteria; OpenAI GPT-4.1-nano prompt; boolean schema/parser; bounded provider failure; keep-on-model/parse-failure safety; usage accounting; and focused behavioral tests.

Adapt the ownership boundary: the Mac supplies only the bounded authoritative local transcript, duration and word count through the authenticated canonical Python backend. Python performs transient inference, returns the proposed boolean, and stores no transcript, conversation, discard state or processing record. The Mac verifies the response against the current local finalization/enrichment generation and applies the retained local discard/cleanup policy atomically; stale results do nothing.

Remove wearable-photo input and visual criteria under IR-359; hosted conversation reads/writes and discard synchronization; premium/max/BYOK and gateway routing under IR-609/608; and exclusive cloud-authority tests. Do not route long or empty transcripts through the model, weaken keep-on-failure, apply this classifier to typed Chat/PTT, or change the downstream rule that discarded ambient captures do not produce visible conversation history, summaries, tasks or memories.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-001 - Per-user cloud Agent VM and local-database mirroring

### Requirement implied by the code

> Every signed-in desktop user should receive a dedicated GCE VM that can run a remote Claude agent over a mirrored copy of the user's local `omi.db`, remain updated through incremental synchronization, and serve remote/mobile agent chat through a proxy.

### Current path

```text
Desktop onboarding or signed-in Home launch
  -> AgentVMService
  -> POST /v2/agent/provision or GET /v2/agent/status
  -> Python desktop/product backend creates or restarts a per-user GCE VM
  -> desktop gzips and uploads the user's local omi.db directly to the VM
  -> AgentSyncService polls GRDB every 3 seconds
  -> selected table rows POST to the VM /sync endpoint
  -> agent-proxy accepts remote/mobile WebSocket traffic
  -> proxy starts or reaches the user's VM
  -> VM runs a Python FastAPI service and Claude Agent SDK session
  -> VM queries its copied SQLite database and may call product-backend tools
```

### Desktop triggers and lifecycle coupling

- `Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift` starts provisioning when onboarding completes.
- `Onboarding/SecondBrain/SBOnboardingModel.swift` does the same in the newer onboarding flow.
- `MainWindow/DesktopHomeView.swift` schedules `ensureProvisioned()` during signed-in session warmup.
- `AgentVMService.swift` provisions, polls, compresses/uploads `omi.db`, sends a Firebase token, and starts incremental sync.
- `AgentSyncService.swift` polls every three seconds and mirrors nine table families: transcription sessions, action items, memories, staged tasks, live notes, screenshots without `ocrDataJson`, transcription segments, focus sessions, and observations.
- `RuntimeOwnerIdentity.swift`, `AppState.swift`, and `ResourceMonitor.swift` stop, pause, or resume Agent sync during owner changes, sleep, and memory pressure.

### Cloud control plane and runtime

- `backend/routers/desktop_agent_vm.py` owns `/v2/agent/provision` and `/v2/agent/status`, Firestore `agentVm` state, GCE creation, restart, and recovery.
- `backend/agent_vm/` is the per-user VM image/runtime: upload, auth, health, incremental `/sync`, WebSocket chat, copied-SQLite tools, Claude Agent SDK, idle-stop, and self-update behavior.
- `backend/agent-proxy/` is the Firebase-authenticated remote/mobile WebSocket bridge to the VM and also persists remote chat history.
- `backend/routers/agent_tools.py` supplies VM status/ensure/keepalive plus product-backend tool discovery and execution for the VM.
- Agent-proxy Helm charts, GCE image/runtime registration, deploy workflows, VM reaper, deployment checks, failure classes, and focused tests exist solely or partly to operate this system.

### Relationship to normal desktop chat

This is not the normal desktop chat runtime.

Normal desktop chat is:

```text
Swift ChatProvider
  -> local AgentRuntimeProcess
  -> bundled local Node kernel and omi-agentd.sqlite3
  -> local provider adapter/harness
  -> Swift-owned desktop tools
```

Removing IR-001 does not inherently remove normal desktop chat.

### Decision

`delete candidate`

Reason: the fork does not require remote/mobile agent execution or a continuously mirrored per-user GCE copy of the Mac's local data. This subsystem adds local polling, database upload, Firebase coupling, Firestore state, GCE lifecycle management, a Python VM runtime, a GKE proxy, deployment workflows, cleanup operations, and a large test/contract surface without serving normal desktop chat.

### Complete deletion boundary to evaluate later

#### macOS client

- `AgentVMService.swift`
- `AgentSyncService.swift`
- provisioning calls from both onboarding flows and signed-in Home warmup
- sleep, owner-transition, and memory-pressure AgentSync hooks
- `provisionAgentVM` / `getAgentStatus` API models and methods
- focused Swift tests and e2e coverage that exist for this path

#### Backend provisioning and product-backend bridge

- `backend/routers/desktop_agent_vm.py` and its registration in both Python app entrypoints
- VM-only portions of `backend/routers/agent_tools.py`: VM status, ensure, keepalive, tool discovery, and tool execution bridge
- `agentVm` Firestore helpers that have no remaining caller
- route-policy and generated-client entries for removed endpoints

#### Remote runtime and proxy

- `backend/agent_vm/`
- `backend/agent-proxy/`
- agent-proxy Helm chart
- agent-VM reaper job and scripts

#### Operations and contracts

- agent-proxy deploy workflows
- runtime image registrations
- deployment-policy/concurrency checks specific to these artifacts
- VM/proxy/reaper tests and failure-class records
- docs and component-guide references

No deletion is authorized yet. This is the candidate boundary for the later deletion step.

## IR-002 - SQL and semantic search boundary

The current tree contains two separate implementations:

### A. Remote Agent VM copies

`backend/agent_vm/main.py` defines Python `execute_sql`, `semantic_search`, and `get_daily_recap` tools over the uploaded copy of `omi.db`. These exist to give the remote VM agent access to mirrored Mac data.

Recommended decision: `delete candidate` with IR-001.

### B. Normal desktop chat's local tools

`ChatToolExecutor.swift`, the local Node MCP bridge, and the generated local tool manifest expose `execute_sql`, `semantic_search`, and `get_daily_recap` against the Mac's live local database and Rewind index. They do not require the per-user GCE VM or `AgentSyncService`.

Decision: `keep` for now and question them separately later, because they are the direct retrieval path over data that already lives locally.

### Decision

`keep local; delete VM copies`

Confirmed boundary:

- Delete Python `execute_sql`, `semantic_search`, and `get_daily_recap` with `backend/agent_vm/` and IR-001.
- Retain the normal desktop chat implementations in `ChatToolExecutor.swift`, the local Node bridge, and the generated local tool manifest.
- The retained local tools remain eligible for their own later requirement review; this decision only prevents the cloud-VM deletion from removing them accidentally.

## IR-003 - Kernel journal backend projection

### Requirement implied by the code

> Every normal desktop chat turn should be durably stored in the local Node kernel and also projected into the product backend, retried until acknowledged, reconciled back from the backend, and coordinated with backend-owned chat-session metadata.

### Current turn path

```text
ChatProvider sends a turn
  -> local Node kernel atomically writes user + assistant rows to omi-agentd.sqlite3
  -> the same transaction creates backend outbox rows
  -> a Node timer drains the outbox
  -> JSONL journal_backend_sync/delete/reconcile messages cross into Swift
  -> KernelJournalBackendSyncDriver calls product-backend APIs
  -> /v2/desktop/messages and /v2/chat-sessions persist into the backend data plane
  -> the result crosses back to Node
  -> Node acknowledges, retries, parks, deletes, or reconciles the outbox row
```

### What is already local and independent

- `conversation-journal.ts` is the durable writer for chat turns in `omi-agentd.sqlite3`.
- `KernelTurnProjection` reloads the visible chat timeline from that local journal.
- The user-visible query is considered complete after the local kernel journal commit; the code explicitly says backend delivery retries independently afterward.
- Normal desktop inference and local tools do not require backend message projection to execute.

### Additional backend coupling around chat

Backend projection is broader than `KernelJournalBackendSyncDriver.swift`:

- Node maintains `backend_turn_outbox`, `backend_conversation_delete_outbox`, and `backend_reconcile_state` tables plus leases, retries, payload hashes, repair, and acknowledgement logic.
- `AgentRuntimeProcess.swift` implements the JSONL handlers that bridge Node delivery requests into Swift network calls.
- `APIClient+KernelJournal.swift` owns message save/read/reconcile calls.
- `ChatProvider` performs a one-release import of legacy backend messages into the local kernel.
- Multi-chat session listing, creation, titles, starring, initial greetings, and session metadata still use `/v2/chat-sessions` and related product-backend endpoints.
- Message ratings and attachments have additional backend dependencies that should be reviewed separately rather than silently grouped into this decision.

### Consequence of deleting only the Swift transport

That would be an incomplete deletion. Local turns would still be written, but the Node kernel would continue creating and pumping backend outbox rows that can never succeed. The proper deletion boundary must remove the projection machinery while retaining the local journal and projection that power desktop chat.

### Recommended decision

`delete candidate`

Keep the local kernel journal as the sole chat-history authority. Delete backend turn projection, remote reconciliation, and legacy backend import. Then review backend-owned multi-chat metadata as a separate but directly adjacent requirement, because it currently prevents the chat surface from being entirely local.

### Decision

`delete backend projection; keep local journal`

Confirmed boundary:

- Keep `omi-agentd.sqlite3`, the local conversation journal, and the local turn projection used to render desktop chat.
- Delete Node's backend outbox, delete outbox, reconciliation state, retry pump, leases, acknowledgements, and `journal_backend_*` protocol messages.
- Delete the matching Swift bridge in `AgentRuntimeProcess`, `KernelJournalBackendSyncDriver`, and `APIClient+KernelJournal`.
- Delete legacy backend-message import into the local journal.
- Review backend-owned chat-session metadata separately before deleting `/v2/chat-sessions`; this confirmation covers turn-history projection, not every adjacent chat feature.

## IR-005 - Local authority for retained personal-assistant product data

### Decision

`resolved by local-authority child decisions IR-024 through IR-038`

Confirmed: memories, tasks, goals, Focus results, Insights, proactive-assistant outputs, AI Profile state, and their retained settings use the Mac-local authorities selected by IR-024 through IR-038 and their detailed descendants. Delete backend synchronization, duplicate cloud authority, reconciliation, and projections for those personal product records unless a separately retained transient-compute boundary explicitly requires bounded input.

This umbrella adds no new feature and does not override any child's keep, adapt, delete, retention, owner-safety, or presentation decision.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-011 - Shared-backend copy of Rewind screen activity

### Requirement implied by the code

> OCR-enriched screen captures stored by Rewind on the Mac must also be uploaded to Omi's shared backend, stored once as queryable documents and again as vectors, and made available to backend chat agents and remote MCP clients.

### Before `ScreenActivitySyncService` was deleted

```text
ProactiveAssistantsPlugin captures a frame
  -> RewindIndexer encodes local video and performs OCR
  -> RewindDatabase inserts the screenshots row into local omi.db
  -> OCREmbeddingService obtains a Gemini embedding and writes its Float32 blob locally
  -> ScreenActivitySyncService polls for embedded rows every 60 seconds
  -> authenticated POST /v1/screen-activity/sync on the Python desktop backend
  -> Firestore users/{uid}/screen_activity/{clientDeviceId-rowId}
  -> Pinecone namespace ns3, vector id {uid}-sa-{clientDeviceId-rowId}
  -> backend agent tools and remote MCP APIs read the copied data
```

The uploader selected `id`, `timestamp`, `appName`, `windowTitle`, `ocrText`, `embedding`, `deviceName`, and `clientDeviceId` from local `screenshots` rows where `embedding IS NOT NULL`. It kept a `screenActivitySync_lastId` cursor in `UserDefaults`, uploaded at most 100 rows per request, and backed off after failures.

The name `rustBackendURL` is stale. For this path it resolved to the separately deployed Python `backend/desktop_backend.py` service (production default `https://desktop-backend-hhibjajaja-uc.a.run.app/`, development default `https://desktop-backend-dt5lrfkkoa-uc.a.run.app/`, or `OMI_DESKTOP_API_URL`).

### Exact Python write path and storage

- `backend/routers/desktop_screen_crisp.py` defines `POST /v1/screen-activity/sync`; the router is mounted by both `backend/desktop_backend.py` and `backend/main.py`.
- The endpoint converts the local row ID into a device-scoped `storageId`, authenticates and subscription-gates the request, limits it to 100 rows, and records a screen parity capture.
- `backend/database/screen_activity.py::upsert_screen_activity` writes one Firestore document at `users/{uid}/screen_activity/{storageId}`. It stores timestamp, app name, window title, at most 1,000 OCR characters, and optional device identifiers. It does not store the embedding in Firestore.
- `backend/database/vector_db.py::upsert_screen_activity_vectors` writes the supplied 3,072-dimension embedding to Pinecone namespace `ns3`. Metadata contains the user ID, screenshot storage ID, timestamp, app name, and optional device identifiers.
- A Pinecone failure is logged but does not fail the Firestore upload, so the two shared copies can diverge.

### Shared-backend readers fed by that upload

- Backend chat tools `get_screen_activity_tool` and `search_screen_activity_tool` read Firestore summaries/raw OCR and Pinecone semantic matches.
- MCP REST exposes `GET /v1/mcp/screen-activity`.
- MCP SSE exposes a `get_screen_activity` tool guarded by OAuth scope `screen_activity.read`.
- Generated macOS and Windows API clients contain the MCP screen-activity schema and endpoint.
- The memory-bank connector prompt tells remote agents to call `omi-memory__get_screen_activity`.
- Account deletion enumerates screen-activity Firestore IDs to delete matching Pinecone vectors.
- A dedicated Firestore composite index supports `appName + timestamp` queries.

### Current path after the macOS uploader deletion

```text
ProactiveAssistantsPlugin captures a frame
  -> RewindIndexer encodes video, performs OCR, and inserts local omi.db row
  -> OCREmbeddingService writes the embedding into that local row
  -> local Rewind UI, FTS, semantic search, and local agent tools read it
  X  no request reaches /v1/screen-activity/sync
```

The server endpoint now has no producer in this repository. Its Firestore/Pinecone writers and remote read surfaces therefore describe a dead shared-backend slice, not the retained local Rewind path.

One separate network dependency remains upstream: local `OCREmbeddingService` calls the generic Python desktop-backend Gemini proxy at `POST /v1/proxy/gemini/models/gemini-embedding-001:batchEmbedContents` to calculate vectors, then stores them only in local SQLite. That is compute proxying, not screen-activity persistence or synchronization, and must be questioned separately rather than silently deleted with this slice.

`AgentSyncService` was another separate downstream copier: it mirrored screenshot rows without `ocrDataJson` into the per-user Agent VM. It did not use `/v1/screen-activity/sync` or Pinecone. That copier is already covered by IR-001's delete decision.

### Decision

`delete candidate`

Confirmed: retain local Rewind and reject its Firestore/Pinecone/backend-agent/MCP copy. Deleting only the Swift uploader left the implementation untidy and made the backend contracts look supported despite having no current producer.

### Proposed deletion boundary if rejected

#### Write path

- Screen-activity request models, parity helper, imports, and `POST /v1/screen-activity/sync` from `backend/routers/desktop_screen_crisp.py`; retain the unrelated Crisp endpoint in the same file.
- The sync route-policy entry and its endpoint/parity tests.
- `backend/database/screen_activity.py` once its read and account-deletion callers below are removed.
- Pinecone `upsert_screen_activity_vectors`, `search_screen_activity_vectors`, `delete_screen_activity_vectors`, and namespace `ns3`.

#### Backend and remote read products

- `backend/utils/retrieval/tools/screen_activity_tools.py` and its registration in the backend agent tool set.
- MCP REST screen-activity models and endpoint.
- MCP SSE `get_screen_activity` tool, execution branch, OAuth scope, index-error helper, and descriptions.
- Screen-activity shaping/memory-filter helpers with no remaining callers.
- Generated macOS and Windows MCP screen-activity client surfaces.
- Memory-bank connector prompt references to the removed remote tool.

#### Storage lifecycle, contracts, and tests

- Screen-activity vector cleanup from account deletion.
- The Firestore `screen_activity` composite-index declaration and index registry entry.
- Model-endpoint inventory and direct query-embedding helper if they have no caller after backend semantic search is removed.
- Route legacy lists, OAuth smoke scopes, parity-pack documentation, focused tool/MCP/vector/account-deletion tests, generated-client fixtures, and import stubs that exist only for this slice.

#### Explicitly retained

- `ProactiveAssistantsPlugin` screen capture.
- `RewindIndexer`, local video chunks, OCR, and the local `screenshots` table in `omi.db`.
- `OCREmbeddingService`, local embedding blobs, local FTS/semantic search, local Rewind UI, and local-agent access—for now, pending their own requirement reviews.
- Generic Gemini proxy support—for now, pending a separate compute-dependency review.

The requirement decision is confirmed, but no code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-012 - Wearable BLE audio as a transcription input

### Requirement implied by the code

> The Mac must accept continuous encoded audio from an Omi or supported third-party wearable, decode its device-specific frames into PCM, force that source through cloud transcription, handle wearable button events, and label the resulting conversation by device type.

### Current path

```text
AppState.startTranscription(source: .bleDevice)
  -> require DeviceProvider active connection
  -> STTSessionState forces BLE sources to cloud mode
  -> TranscriptionService opens Python backend /v4/listen
  -> startBleAudioCapture
  -> BleAudioService consumes DeviceConnection.getAudioStream()
  -> BleAudioProcessor / codec-specific decoder emits PCM
  -> TranscriptionService.sendAudio
  -> /v4/listen emits transcript segments and conversation events
  -> AppState live projection + local TranscriptionStorage
```

`AudioSource` defaults to `.microphone`. The `AudioSourceSelector` component currently has no production reference outside its own preview, but the BLE branch remains compiled and reachable through the transcription API/state.

### Decision

`delete BLE audio input`

Confirmed: retaining transcription capability does not require accepting audio from an Omi BLE wearable. Mac microphone/system-audio transcription is a separate branch and is not removed by this decision.

### Proposed narrow deletion boundary

- `.bleDevice` audio-source selection and its forced-cloud STT policy.
- BLE-specific start/stop routing and wearable button handling in `AppState+Transcription`.
- `BleAudioService`, `BleAudioProcessor`, and audio codec/decoder surfaces with no remaining non-device caller.
- BLE conversation-source labeling and focused tests/docs for this input path.

This is not yet the complete device deletion boundary. IR-014 holds the sibling question of whether discovery, pairing, reconnection, battery, storage, and all device adapters should also disappear.

## IR-013 - Omi audio WAL and offline device-audio synchronization

### Requirement implied by the code

> Encoded wearable audio must survive interruptions by being buffered locally, persisted as recoverable chunks, downloaded later from device storage when necessary, uploaded to the product backend for transcription, reconciled until the backend job finishes, and cleaned up after acknowledgement.

### What this storage actually is

Omi WAL is not a SQLite database and is not SQLite's own WAL mode. It is a separate audio durability subsystem under the current desktop profile's `Application Support/.../wals` directory:

- encoded audio `.bin` chunks;
- `wals.json` metadata plus `wals_backup.json`;
- temporary recovery records ending in `.wal-pending.json`;
- in-memory active and pending frame buffers;
- statuses such as `inProgress`, `miss`, `uploaded`, `synced`, and `corrupted`.

The unrelated `omi.db-wal` file is SQLite/GRDB's normal transaction journal and is not covered by this deletion decision.

### Current branches

```text
A. Live wearable frames (currently dormant in production)
   AudioSourceManager.startStreaming(.bleDevice)
     -> BleAudioService rawFrameHandler
     -> WALService.addFrame
     -> local wals directory

B. Audio already stored on the wearable
   DeviceProvider detects device storage
     -> StorageSyncService over BLE OR WifiSyncService over device Wi-Fi/TCP
     -> WALService local chunks

A or B
  -> WALService.syncToCloud
  -> POST /v2/sync-local-files
  -> backend returns completed result or async job ID
  -> GET /v2/sync-local-files/{job_id} reconciliation
  -> backend decode/VAD/STT/conversation persistence pipeline
```

`AudioSourceManager.startStreaming` describes itself as dormant and has no production caller, so the live raw-frame WAL writer is already inactive. The device-storage download, upload, reconciliation, UI, and backend pipeline still exist.

### Decision

`delete`

Confirmed: the fork does not require raw wearable-frame durability or later device-storage recovery. Because the Omi device is also deleted, no supported producer remains for these WAL files. This removes the reason for the local Omi WAL subsystem, its upload request, and its asynchronous job-status polling while leaving ordinary `omi.db`/GRDB durability untouched.

### Proposed deletion branches

- SwiftPM `OmiWAL` target, `WALModel.swift`, and its dedicated tests.
- `WALService`, `WALCloudSyncLogic`, `WALSyncReconciler`, `StorageSyncService`, `WifiSyncService`, and `StorageSyncView` plus focused tests/docs.
- WAL hooks from `AudioSourceManager` and device storage detection.
- `uploadLocalFilesV2`, sync-job status polling, WAL result models, filename normalization, generated client surfaces, and imports that only support this subsystem.
- Python `POST /v1/sync-local-files`, `POST /v2/sync-local-files`, `GET /v2/sync-local-files/{job_id}`, and the internal `/v2/sync-jobs/run` handler.
- Wearable-offline-audio job state, content-ledger/deduplication branches, raw-file staging, fresh/backfill dispatch, queue configuration, processing pipeline, generated contracts, tests, metrics, deployment configuration, and documentation that exist only for these routes.

The Mac has no general recorded-audio import flow using these endpoints. Its handwritten caller is `WALService`; generated client methods are not independent product callers. Removing this slice does not remove live Mac transcription (`/v4/listen` or local Parakeet), push-to-talk (`/v2/voice-message/transcribe[-stream]`), or local Rewind persistence.

The `backend-sync` Cloud Run deployment also serves unrelated queued work. Deleting IR-013 therefore deletes the wearable sync workload, not automatically the whole shared deployment. The remaining deployment is held on the frontier for a separate caller/workload audit.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-125 - First-run Second Brain onboarding product

### Reconstructed PRD requirement

> After sign-in, a first-time user must complete or explicitly skip a conversational Second Brain setup before entering the main Mac product. The setup must establish the product promise and trust model, collect personalization, acquire the permissions needed by the assistant, configure its global entry points and capture policy, prove the screen-aware voice experience, offer external context/agent connections, and leave the user's Home experience immediately personalized.

This is the parent product requirement. “The current UI already works” is not evidence that the requirement should survive.

### Target user and entry contract inferred from the code

- The user has already authenticated with Firebase.
- Onboarding is a blocking first-run gate: until a local completion flag is set, the main product is not shown.
- It runs per signed-in account on a Mac because sign-out clears its local state.
- A user who quits during setup resumes at the saved step.
- A global **Skip** exits the entire setup at any time; most individual permissions and demos can also be skipped.
- The interface is presented as a streaming conversation with the assistant, intentionally hiding the number of remaining steps.

### Complete active requirement tree

```text
First-run Second Brain setup
├── Explain the product and earn trust
│   ├── promise: hears conversations, remembers everything, handles follow-ups
│   ├── disclose open-source code
│   ├── claim encrypted/private user data
│   └── promise pause and permanent deletion controls
├── Personalize the assistant
│   ├── name
│   ├── acquisition source: "How did you hear about Omi?"
│   ├── spoken/listening language, prefilled from the Mac locale
│   └── role/persona: Student, Founder, Engineer, free text, etc.
├── Acquire Mac capabilities one at a time
│   ├── microphone
│   ├── system audio
│   ├── Screen Recording
│   ├── Full Disk Access plus immediate local-file scan/profile memories
│   ├── Accessibility
│   └── Automation / Apple Events
├── Configure global entry points
│   ├── choose and physically test an open-Omi shortcut
│   └── choose and physically test the hold-to-talk shortcut
├── Prove the core experience
│   └── warm the local agent and realtime voice, then require or allow skipping
│       a real screen-aware spoken question answered in the notch/pill
├── Extend the assistant before first use
│   ├── export/connect memory to OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, or Codex
│   └── import/connect Calendar, Gmail, Apple Notes, Files, ChatGPT, or Claude
├── Choose capture policy
│   ├── listen only during meetings
│   └── start listening continuously immediately
└── Complete setup
    ├── persist completion and clear the throwaway onboarding chat
    ├── show a personalized Home opener and prompt suggestions
    ├── preserve/apply launch-at-login state
    ├── start Agent VM provisioning
    ├── generate goals
    ├── enable proactive screen analysis
    └── reconcile or immediately begin continuous transcription
```

### Product purpose inferred from those requirements

The flow is trying to solve four product problems:

1. **Trust:** explain why an always-available assistant wants unusually sensitive Mac permissions.
2. **Activation:** ensure capture, screen understanding, PTT, and shortcuts work before the user reaches an empty Home screen.
3. **Personalization:** collect enough information and context to make the first answer feel specific.
4. **Demonstration:** make the user experience the screen-aware spoken assistant instead of expecting them to discover it later.

### Evidence that the current PRD and current product have drifted apart

- Full Disk Access and Automation have already been rejected under IR-050/051.
- Browser/import/export/agent connector setup conflicts with IR-046/047/048/049.
- Agent VM provisioning is deleted under IR-001.
- The role answer is saved locally but no production feature reads it, despite the copy claiming it “shapes what I make for you.”
- Acquisition source is marketing attribution, not assistant personalization.
- The “click and type for you” Accessibility promise conflicts with the rejected general computer-operator and physical-click scope.
- The capture button says meetings are determined “from my calendar,” while retained meeting detection is an independent local app/call detector.
- “Remember everything” and the broad cloud privacy copy were written for Omi's larger synced product; the fork now has explicit local-authority and deletion boundaries.
- The codebase still contains a separate legacy 18-page onboarding implementation in addition to the active conversational flow. That duplicate implementation is not automatically justified by keeping onboarding as a product capability.

Therefore keeping the parent cannot mean keeping the present sequence unchanged. Every surviving child must still be challenged against the new product, and already rejected children must be removed.

### Audit-method correction

The reconstructed tree is a navigation map, not a product-level decision to put in front of the user. The PRD has already materialized into concrete Swift screens and side effects. Audit the active implementation in execution order and ask about exactly what exists: each screen's copy, controls, required/optional behavior, writes, permission prompts, demo, and completion effects. Do not ask an abstract parent question whose answer would silently retain or delete unreviewed children.
