IR-804 kept independent backend deployment plus live compatibility. None of those decisions chose whether this full server promotion state machine remains the publishing authority.

`ADAPT - retain the complete Beta/Stable release authority in our canonical backend`

Confirmed: retain immutable signed release manifests, exact-candidate reservation and admission, qualification evidence binding, Beta pointer advancement, promotion of the same accepted build to Stable, Sparkle appcast and download resolution, live-backend compatibility checks, Beta pause/recovery, qualified rollback, audited emergency rollout, idempotent retries and conflict-safe Firestore transactions.

Remove Omi-specific identities and duplicate backend ownership; leave Windows untouched under IR-009. Do not infer release channels only from GitHub release labels, replace the state machine with hand-edited static appcasts, or mix customer conversations and other rejected personal product data into this operational release ledger.

## IR-898 - Three-way System Audio capture mode

### Exact current behavior from the code

`AssistantSettings.SystemAudioCaptureMode` has three locally persisted values. **Always** runs microphone and system-audio capture for the whole enabled Listening session. **Only during meetings**, the default, runs the meeting detector, captures neither source outside a detected call, starts microphone plus system audio during the call, and finishes that local conversation when the meeting ends. **Never** is presented by the shared Listening status as **Mic only**: the microphone continues for the whole enabled Listening session while audio produced by other applications is never captured.

Settings exposes all three choices and applies a change live through `systemAudioCaptureModeDidChange`. The shared Home/header mode shortcut intentionally cycles only **Meetings only** and **Always**; **Mic only** remains an explicit Settings choice. Onboarding similarly offers meeting-only or continuous mic-plus-system setup and leaves the narrower microphone-only choice available afterward. Selecting Mic only also removes System Audio from the required capture-permission/paywall readiness set.

### Decision

`KEEP AS IS - retain Always, Only during meetings, and Never/Mic only with meeting-only as the default`

Confirmed: preserve all three labels, values, local `UserDefaults` persistence, default, Settings picker, live reconciliation notification, Home/header status wording, meeting-detector ownership, whole-capture meeting gate, meeting-end local finalization, continuous microphone behavior in Always and Never, system-audio suppression in Never, and the current shortcut/onboarding relationship. **Never** must continue to mean continuous microphone-only transcription while Listening is enabled, not disabling all recording.

Do not collapse the picker to the two onboarding choices, remove Mic only, make the header shortcut cycle into Mic only, capture application audio in Never, or reinterpret this local privacy control as a cloud synchronization setting. Existing hidden development overrides and actual System Audio permission/setup remain governed by their previously recorded requirements.

## IR-016 - Dedicated `backend-sync` deployment for surviving background work

### Requirement implied by the code

> Expensive or retryable product-backend work must execute through Cloud Tasks against a separately deployed `backend-sync` Cloud Run service instead of the main backend service.

### Current deployment split

`backend-sync` and the main `backend` deploy the same FastAPI image as separate Cloud Run services. Cloud Tasks targets `backend-sync` for four workload families:

1. wearable/offline-audio processing through `/v2/sync-jobs/run`;
2. conversation playback MP3 construction through `/v2/audio-merge-jobs/run`;
3. server-account deletion through `/v1/users/account-deletion-wipes/run`;
4. cloud conversation finalization through `/v1/conversation-finalization-jobs/run`.

There is also a separate scale-to-zero `backend-sync-backfill` service. Its purpose is the old/untrusted recording lane of the wearable `/v2/sync-local-files` pipeline. It has no surviving purpose after IR-013 and is therefore included in that deletion.

The ordinary `backend-sync` service cannot yet be decided as a single unit:

- conversation finalization is called by the current cloud-STT lifecycle and depends on IR-020;
- server-account deletion is called by the current Mac Settings UI and depends on whether accounts/server data survive under IR-006/008;
- playback-audio merge exists for backend-stored conversation audio and depends on the cloud conversation/storage decision under IR-020/008.

### Current recommendation

Do not treat a dedicated worker deployment as a product requirement. First decide its three surviving product behaviors. If any remain, prefer pointing their queues at the main backend service unless a measured isolation or scaling requirement justifies a separate service. This is a recommendation only; the deployment decision remains deferred until its child requirements are resolved.

### Decision

`resolved - delete both backend-sync and backend-sync-backfill Cloud Run deployments`

Every workload has now been decided: wearable/offline sync and backfill are deleted under IR-013/014; live-listen conversation finalization is deleted under IR-020; cloud conversation-audio merge is deleted under IR-121; and durable account deletion is retained but its Cloud Task targets the main backend under IR-120. Remove both service deployments, service-specific IAM/configuration, deployment workflow branches, URLs, monitoring, and documentation. Keep only the surviving account-deletion queue and configure it against the main backend.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-120 - Separate `backend-sync` deployment for account deletion

### Requirement implied by the code

> Because deleting an account is slow, destructive, and retryable, its Cloud Task must call a second `backend-sync` Cloud Run service rather than the normal product backend.

### What must survive

Account deletion is not optional after IR-006. The retained account and billing scaffold needs a real deletion path. The current Mac Settings flow calls `DELETE /v1/users/delete-account`, and the backend then:

1. durably records the deletion intent and a unique wipe-job ID;
2. enqueues a Cloud Task;
3. lets an OIDC-protected worker cancel billing, delete Firebase Auth, and wipe retained server data;
4. retries failures and reconciles jobs whose queue handoff or worker run failed.

Running all of that inside the original Settings request would be unsafe. If the request timed out or the backend restarted halfway through, the user could be left with a partly deleted account and no durable retry authority. The queue, job record, task authentication, run lock, retries, and reconciliation therefore remain requirements.

### What the second service actually adds

The main `backend` service and `backend-sync` service deploy the same FastAPI image. `backend/main.py` registers the account-deletion worker route on that app unconditionally:

```text
main FastAPI app
  ├── DELETE /v1/users/delete-account
  └── POST /v1/users/account-deletion-wipes/run
```

The deployment workflow currently looks up the separate `backend-sync` URL and configures Cloud Tasks to call the second route there. That target gives workload isolation, but it does not supply a different implementation or a missing correctness boundary.

### Choices

1. **Keep the separate service.** Account wipes cannot consume request capacity on the ordinary backend, but we continue deploying, configuring, securing, and monitoring a second Cloud Run service for a low-frequency operation.
2. **Target the main backend.** Keep the exact durable Cloud Tasks lifecycle, OIDC protection, retries, run lock, long per-route timeout, and reconciliation, but point the task at the main backend's existing hidden worker route. Use queue rate/concurrency limits to bound the load.
3. **Run deletion inline.** Delete the queue and worker and perform the wipe in the original HTTP request. This is the simplest deployment but loses the current crash/timeout recovery and is not recommended.

### Recommendation

`keep durable queued account deletion, but remove its dependency on the separate backend-sync deployment`

Point the account-deletion Cloud Task at the main backend's existing OIDC-protected handler. This removes deployment and configuration surface without turning a destructive multi-system operation into an unreliable request-thread job. Account-deletion volume should be low for an initial Mac product; if measured load later harms ordinary requests, a dedicated worker can be restored from evidence.

This decision alone does not yet authorize deleting the entire `backend-sync` service. The remaining playback-audio callers still need their own audit under IR-016/008.

### Question

Should we keep the complete durable account-deletion queue and retry behavior, but have the Cloud Task call the main backend instead of maintaining a separate `backend-sync` Cloud Run service for it?

### Decision

`resolved - keep durable queued account deletion, but point its Cloud Task at the main backend`

Preserve the durable deletion-intent/job record, opaque job ID, OIDC-protected handler, run lock, retries, terminal-attempt behavior, reconciliation, long route-specific timeout, privacy-bounded telemetry, and the retained billing-provider cancellation step. Configure the task to call the handler already registered on the main FastAPI app, with bounded queue rate/concurrency. Remove account deletion as a reason to deploy `backend-sync`; final deletion of that service still depends on the playback-audio workload audit.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-121 - Cloud conversation-audio recording and playback artifacts

### Requirement implied by the code

> The product must store raw conversation-audio chunks in cloud storage, merge them into replayable audio artifacts, and expose polling, signed-URL, and download APIs so a client can play a past recording.

### Current backend flow

```text
live/backend or offline-device audio
  -> upload timestamped private audio chunks to GCS
  -> write `audio_files` metadata onto a Firestore conversation
  -> enqueue `audio-merge` Cloud Tasks
  -> `POST /v2/audio-merge-jobs/run` on backend-sync
  -> download/decrypt/fill gaps/merge/transcode chunks
  -> upload per-part MP3s plus one conversation.mp3
  -> stamp the Firestore conversation with artifact fingerprint/spans
  -> client calls /v1/sync/audio/.../urls and polls while pending
  -> backend returns signed GCS playback URLs or streams a download
```

Late chunks invalidate the artifact and enqueue another build. The slice also carries cache expiration, unavailable markers, named-task deduplication, retries, range downloads, legacy WAV fallback, conversation-merge copying, account-deletion cleanup, telemetry, environment variables, deployment configuration, and a broad test surface.

### Actual Mac caller audit

The current Mac source has generated API methods for `precache` and `urls`, because they come from the shared OpenAPI schema. No non-generated Mac production code calls those methods or any `/v1/sync/audio` endpoint. The Mac conversation UI displays transcripts but contains no past-conversation recording player.

Its backend producers also belong to already rejected cloud-authority branches:

- wearable/offline audio upload is deleted under IR-013/014;
- `/v4/listen` server conversation ownership and finalization are deleted under IR-020;
- backend-owned conversation merge/playback depends on those server conversations.

### What this is not

Deleting this slice does **not** delete:

- microphone or system-audio capture used transiently for live transcription;
- locally stored conversation transcripts;
- realtime PTT answer audio or fallback TTS playback;
- local Rewind screen-history playback;
- the possibility of deliberately adding local raw-audio recording later as a separately designed feature.

The current code is specifically cloud storage and playback of backend-owned conversation recordings. It is not a working local Mac recording player that can be preserved by merely changing a database adapter.

### Choices

1. **Delete the whole cloud recording/playback slice.** Remove cloud audio-chunk persistence, `audio_files`/`conversation_audio` authority, merge tasks and handler, precache/URL/download APIs, GCS artifacts and cleanup, client generated bindings, configuration, and dedicated tests.
2. **Keep it.** Continue hosting private raw audio and derived MP3s in GCS plus the queue/worker/API lifecycle, even though the first Mac product currently has no UI or runtime caller for replaying them.
3. **Build local recording playback now.** Add durable local raw-audio capture, retention, indexing, a player, and deletion behavior. This is a new feature rather than a localization of an existing Mac behavior and would slow the first release.

### Recommendation

`delete the complete cloud conversation-audio storage and playback slice`

It has no current Mac consumer, and both of its main data producers are already rejected. Keeping it would preserve storage cost, sensitive raw-audio retention, Cloud Tasks, GCS artifact management, and API surface for an absent product behavior. Do not replace it with a new local recorder during this simplification pass.

If accepted, `backend-sync` has no surviving workload: wearable sync and backfill are deleted, conversation finalization is deleted, account deletion moves to the main backend, and audio merge is deleted. IR-016 can then resolve to deleting the separate service.

### Question

Should we delete the entire cloud conversation-audio storage and later-playback slice, while keeping live transcription, local transcripts, realtime/TTS voice playback, and Rewind unchanged?

### Decision

`resolved - delete the complete cloud conversation-audio storage and later-playback slice`

Remove raw conversation-audio uploads to GCS, `audio_files` and `conversation_audio` backend authority, per-part and conversation artifact builders, the `audio-merge` queue and handler, precache/poll/signed-URL/download endpoints, cache and unavailability markers, legacy WAV fallback, conversation-merge audio copying, provider-specific configuration, generated client bindings, cleanup branches, telemetry, tests, and documentation that exist only for this slice. Preserve transient live microphone/system-audio capture for transcription, locally authoritative transcripts, PTT/realtime/TTS playback, and Rewind playback. Do not add a new local raw-audio recorder/player during this simplification pass.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-017 - System audio as a continuous-transcription input

### Requirement implied by the code

> While Mac transcription is listening, the transcript must include both the user's microphone and audio produced by other applications, such as calls, videos, podcasts, and music.

### Current path

The current `microphone` audio-source name actually owns two independent inputs:

```text
Mac microphone ───────────────┐
                              ├── cloud mode: AudioMixer -> one mono stream -> /v4/listen
Core Audio system-output tap ─┘

Mac microphone ────────────────── local mode: user Parakeet instance
Core Audio system-output tap ──── local mode: non-user Parakeet instance
```

System audio uses a Core Audio Tap available on macOS 14.4 or later and converts other-app output to 16 kHz PCM. Failure falls back to mic-only capture. A separate settings branch currently provides `always`, `onlyDuringMeetings`, and `never`; whether that mode machinery is necessary will be challenged only if the base system-audio requirement survives.

### Consequence of deletion

The app would transcribe only sound reaching the selected microphone. Remote participants in headphones, videos, podcasts, and other Mac playback would normally be absent. The deletion would remove the Core Audio tap, system-channel buffering/mixing, its local STT instance, settings/mode handling, health/permission behavior, and related tests.

### Recommendation

`keep the capability`

For a Mac knowledge/capture product, system audio is a primary input rather than an Omi-specific accessory. Without it, meeting and learning-content transcripts become one-sided or empty. This recommendation does not imply keeping the current three-mode meeting detector or the cloud transcription path; those are separate child decisions.

### Question

Does the product need to transcribe audio produced by other Mac applications, in addition to the user's microphone?

### Decision

`keep`

Confirmed: audio produced by other Mac applications is a required transcription input. The Core Audio system-output capture path remains. Its meeting-detection, mode-selection, mixing, local/cloud STT, and storage children remain independent requirements to challenge.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-018 - Automatic meeting-gated listening and conversation boundaries

### Requirement implied by the code

> The app must infer when a supported conferencing call begins and ends, capture microphone plus system audio only during the inferred call, and automatically finalize the resulting conversation when the call ends.

### Current path

```text
Listening enabled in "Only during meetings" mode
  -> MeetingDetector polls every 4 seconds
     -> known native/browser process using microphone, or
     -> browser window title matching Google Meet / Teams
  -> detected meeting starts
     -> start microphone + system-audio capture
     -> emit meeting task-context event
  -> meeting disappears for an 8-second grace period
     -> stop both capture inputs
     -> finalize the current conversation
     -> wait for another meeting while listening remains enabled
```

The detector recognizes a fixed catalog of conferencing applications and bundle IDs. Browser title fallback needs Screen Recording permission. A muted or unsupported browser/app can therefore be missed. The mode is currently the default, is presented during onboarding and Settings, and adds capture-reconciliation state, hysteresis, UI status, automatic conversation boundaries, task-context integration, and focused tests.

`ConferencingApps` also supports proactive screen-capture throttling while the user is sharing their screen. Removing meeting-gated listening would not automatically authorize deleting that separate caller.

### Recommendation

`delete automatic meeting gating for the first ship`

Use the explicit Listening control as the capture authority: listening on captures the selected Mac audio inputs; listening off captures nothing. This removes an app/title heuristic from the ownership of recording and conversation finalization. A simple mic-only versus mic-plus-system choice, if required for privacy, is a separate smaller decision.

### Question

Must the app automatically decide when a meeting starts and ends, and use that inference to start/stop capture and finalize conversations?

### Decision

`keep`

Confirmed: meeting detection, meeting-gated microphone/system-audio capture, the grace-period transition, and automatic meeting-ended conversation finalization remain product requirements. Their UI, onboarding, task-context event, and tests remain in scope. Shared `ConferencingApps` callers remain separately auditable.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-019 - Cloud `/v4/listen` as a second continuous-STT engine

### Requirement implied by the code

> Continuous transcription must support both on-device Parakeet and the product backend's live `/v4/listen` pipeline so Intel Macs work and Apple Silicon can fall back to cloud when the local model cannot load.

### Current mode selection

```text
Apple Silicon + Mac audio
  -> local Parakeet by default
  -> separate mic/user and system/non-user transcription
  -> approximately 10-second windows
  -> segments persist in local GRDB

Intel Mac OR forced-cloud mode OR Parakeet model-load failure
  -> mix microphone + system audio into mono PCM
  -> authenticated WebSocket /v4/listen
  -> backend-listen / pusher / STT provider / diarization pipeline
  -> backend conversation lifecycle and events
```

If the cloud WebSocket exhausts reconnection on Apple Silicon, the current code can rotate back to local Parakeet. Local English uses the Parakeet v2 model; other supported European languages use v3. Model weights are roughly 600 MB to 1.2 GB and download from Hugging Face on first use.

### What retaining `/v4/listen` buys

- Intel Mac continuous-transcription support.
- Automatic recovery when local model download/load fails.
- Generic within-conversation diarization and provider routing. Persistent speech profiles and server conversation ownership were later rejected by IR-021 and IR-020.
- A second STT implementation when one path fails.

### What it costs

- Mac WebSocket transport, authentication, reconnect/watchdog, audio mixing, dual-direction fallback state, and cloud/local finalization reconciliation.
- The `backend-listen` GKE surface plus pusher, hosted/self-hosted STT provider capacity, diarization/VAD/speech-profile dependencies, runtime configuration, monitoring, and deployment workflows.
- A supported behavior in which raw continuous audio leaves the Mac.

Deleting `/v4/listen` from continuous Mac capture would make Apple Silicon and a successfully loaded local model hard requirements. A model failure would become a visible transcription failure rather than a cloud fallback. This decision does not remove PTT endpoints or decide whether completed local transcripts are later uploaded for cloud summaries/memories.

### Recommendation

`delete cloud continuous STT for the first ship`

Make Apple Silicon the supported hardware floor and let local Parakeet be the sole continuous-STT engine. This removes the largest hosted real-time compute branch. Model distribution and failure UX then become explicit local-product responsibilities rather than reasons to retain the cloud pipeline.

### Question

Should the first shipped app be Apple-Silicon-only and use local Parakeet as its sole continuous transcription engine, deleting the Mac `/v4/listen` path and cloud fallback?

### Decision

`keep both local and cloud continuous STT`

Confirmed: retain local Parakeet as the Apple Silicon default and retain `/v4/listen` for Intel Macs, local-model failure fallback, generic within-conversation diarization, provider routing, and dual-direction availability fallback. The Mac WebSocket client and live backend STT deployment family remain requirements. IR-020 later removes server conversation ownership from this transport, and IR-021 later removes persistent speech-profile identity. Locally transcribed conversations do not upload under IR-004.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-004 - Backend promotion of locally transcribed conversations

### Requirement implied by the code

> A conversation transcribed entirely on the Mac is not complete until its transcript is uploaded to the product backend, processed into a server conversation, and hydrated back into the local database.

### Current path

```text
local Parakeet mic/system segments
  -> transcription_sessions + transcription_segments in local GRDB
  -> finish marks the session pending_upload
  -> ConversationFinalizationService
  -> POST /v1/conversations/from-segments with the complete transcript
  -> backend process_conversation
     -> Firestore conversation
     -> title + overview + category
     -> memories + action items + vectors
     -> integrations and cross-device availability
  -> backend conversation ID returned
  -> local row becomes backendSynced/completed
  -> GET server conversation and hydrate structured fields back into GRDB
```

`TranscriptionRetryService` recovers this upload after crashes and retries pending/failed finalizations every 60 seconds. The current Conversations list filters local GRDB to `backendSynced == true`, so an unsynced Parakeet session is durable but normally invisible as a completed conversation. Backend promotion currently doubles as the UI publication boundary.

### Complete local-first deletion boundary

Deleting only `POST /v1/conversations/from-segments` would strand sessions in `pending_upload`. A clean deletion must instead:

- make finishing a local session transition directly to a local completed state;
- list and open completed local sessions without a backend ID or `backendSynced` flag;
- use stable local conversation identity for detail, star, title, folder, search, and deletion operations;
- remove the `.localSegments` upload/finalization retry branch and its backend endpoint/contracts;
- stop hydrating the server copy back over the locally authored transcript;
- separately replace or reject cloud-only title, overview, memory, action-item, vector, integration, and cross-device behaviors.

This question covers locally transcribed Parakeet conversations only. The retained `/v4/listen` path currently creates backend conversations during cloud transcription; whether that cloud STT transport must also own durable conversation storage is a sibling decision.

### Recommendation

`delete backend promotion; make local GRDB authoritative`

This is the direct transcript equivalent of deleting the agent-journal outbox: local persistence already exists, while the upload adds retry state, server storage, full backend processing, and a round-trip hydration dependency. Preserve the transcript and conversation UI locally. Challenge each derived cloud feature separately instead of using it to justify mandatory synchronization.

### Question

Should a conversation transcribed by local Parakeet ever be uploaded to `/v1/conversations/from-segments`, or should it become a complete, visible conversation entirely inside local GRDB?

### Decision

`delete backend promotion; keep local GRDB authoritative`

Confirmed: local Parakeet transcripts become complete, visible local conversations without `/v1/conversations/from-segments`, a backend ID, Firestore persistence, or server hydration. The eventual deletion must change completion, query filters, identity, local mutations, and retry recovery atomically; deleting only the HTTP call is explicitly incomplete. Cloud-derived enrichment features are unresolved children, not reasons to retain synchronization.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-020 - Durable server conversation ownership inside `/v4/listen`

### Requirement implied by the code

> Using cloud live transcription must also create a durable backend conversation, continuously persist transcript state, finalize it through the product processing pipeline, and bind the local recording to that server identity.

### Current path

```text
Mac opens authenticated /v4/listen WebSocket
  -> backend creates/reuses an in_progress Firestore conversation
  -> backend sends conversation_session with the server conversation ID
  -> transcript batches are returned to the Mac and saved in local GRDB
  -> the same batches are also attached to the backend conversation
  -> disconnect / meeting end requests durable finalization
  -> Cloud Tasks or pusher runs process_conversation
  -> backend sends memory_processing_started / memory_created
  -> Mac marks its local row completed and backendSynced
  -> server conversation fields are fetched and cached locally
```

The route therefore combines two responsibilities:

1. transient compute: streaming STT, translations, diarization, and speaker suggestions;
2. durable product ownership: Firestore conversation identity, transcript persistence, finalization, summaries/memories/actions, integration fanout, playback audio, and cross-device retrieval.

The Mac already receives every segment and writes it into local GRDB for crash safety. The cloud speaker matcher operates on the live audio ring buffer and segment stream, but some assignment/sample workflows currently use the backend conversation ID and would need a narrower session identity or their own explicit persistence decision.

### Local-authority alternative

Retain the cloud WebSocket as an STT transport but make its conversation state ephemeral:

- return transcript segments, translations, and any retained speaker suggestions;
- let the Mac's local session ID and meeting detector own boundaries;
- finish the local GRDB conversation without a backend ID;
- remove Firestore live-conversation writes, recording-session lifecycle events, `memory_created` completion binding, cloud reconciliation, and conversation-finalization jobs for this path;
- review speech profiles separately because they are user-level server data, not inherently conversation storage.

This would preserve the cloud fallback selected in IR-019 while preventing fallback mode from silently changing the data authority from local to cloud.

### Recommendation

`retain cloud STT compute; delete cloud conversation ownership`

One local conversation authority is simpler than having Parakeet sessions be local-only while `/v4/listen` sessions become server-owned. The backend should return transcription results; the Mac should decide when a conversation exists and persist it locally. Challenge summaries, memories, actions, playback, cross-device access, and speech profiles as separate product requirements.

### Question

Should retained `/v4/listen` remain a full server-conversation lifecycle, or should it become a transient transcription stream whose returned segments are stored and completed only in local GRDB?

### Decision

`retain transient cloud STT; delete server conversation ownership`

Confirmed: `/v4/listen` may perform cloud transcription and return live segment/speaker results, but the Mac owns conversation identity, boundaries, persistence, completion, and display in local GRDB. Remove Firestore live-conversation creation and transcript duplication, server lifecycle events, backend-ID binding, cloud reconciliation, and Mac-listen finalization jobs. Speech profiles and any non-Mac callers of shared finalization/playback infrastructure remain separate audits.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-021 - Persistent cross-conversation voice identity

### Requirement implied by the code

> The product must remember what the user and other named people sound like, persist their voice data in the backend, and automatically attach those identities to speakers in future conversations.

This is not the same requirement as diarization. Diarization only separates voices inside the current conversation as generic `Speaker 0`, `Speaker 1`, and so on. IR-021 is the extra claim that a voice should be recognized as `You` or a named person across different conversations.

### Current path

```text
Mac opens /v4/listen
  -> always sends include_speech_profile=true
  -> always sends speaker_auto_assign=enabled
  -> backend loads the user's stored speech profile / speaker embedding
  -> backend loads every server-side person with a verified speech sample
  -> missing embeddings may be rebuilt by downloading stored audio
  -> live segment audio is cut from the session ring buffer
  -> speaker-embedding compute compares that audio with stored identities
  -> matching segment events return the user/person identity to the Mac
```

The enrollment and teaching side adds several durable backend surfaces:

- `GET /v3/speech-profile` and `GET /v4/speech-profile` inspect or return the user's profile audio;
- `POST /v3/upload-audio` accepts a 5-120 second 16 kHz WAV, VAD-processes it, uploads it, computes a voice embedding, and writes that embedding to the user record;
- `GET` and `DELETE /v3/speech-profile/expand` manage additional user/person samples;
- `/v1/users/people` stores the user's named-person registry, including speech-sample paths and embedding metadata;
- assigning server conversation segments to a person can cut audio from the server recording, quality-check it, store the sample, and compute the person's embedding;
- `backend/routers/listen/speakers.py` loads those identities and performs live matching for `/v4/listen`.

The Mac currently opts into this on every conversation-mode cloud STT connection in `TranscriptionService.swift`; this is not an isolated settings feature.

### Why this feature exists

Cloud and local transcription currently receive different audio shapes:

```text
local Parakeet
  microphone -> dedicated local transcriber -> is_user=true
  system audio -> dedicated local transcriber -> is_user=false

cloud /v4/listen
  microphone + system audio -> summed into one mono stream -> backend
```

In cloud mode the source boundary has been discarded. Diarization can decide that three different voices spoke, but a numeric diarization label does not reveal which voice belongs to the Mac user or whether a recurring voice is Alice. Speech profiles add that identity layer after diarization.

For example, in a call with the user, Alice, and Bob:

- diarization alone can produce `Speaker 0`, `Speaker 1`, and `Speaker 2`;
- a user speech-profile match can change the appropriate segments to `You` and right-align them in the Mac transcript;
- a taught-person match can display `Alice` instead of a generic speaker number;
- future conversations can reuse those identities instead of requiring the same manual labels again.

This does not improve the words produced by STT. Its direct value is speaker attribution: who said each set of words. That attribution also becomes available to any retained downstream summary, memory, task, or chat feature.

The architecture is especially understandable for the original Omi/wearable input: one microphone hears everyone, so audio-source routing cannot identify the wearer. Deleting wearable capture removes that original justification, although the current Mac cloud path recreates the same ambiguity by mixing mic and system audio to mono.

### Current Mac completeness gap

The Mac contains generated bindings for the speech-profile endpoints but no non-generated caller that records and uploads the primary user's enrollment sample. It can consume a profile that already exists on the Omi account, and its person-labeling flow can teach another person's voice from backend conversation audio. Therefore, as a standalone Mac-first product, automatic recognition of `You` currently depends on enrollment performed somewhere outside the Mac, while teaching named people depends on the server-conversation/audio path rejected in IR-020.

### Dependency exposed by IR-020

The teach-from-conversation workflow requires a durable backend conversation, transcript segments, and backend audio files. IR-020 deletes those for Mac listen sessions. Keeping voice identity would therefore require a new upload/persistence path—or reducing the feature to separately enrolled voice profiles. That is additional architecture, not something the transient STT route gets for free.

### Clean deletion boundary

If cross-conversation voice identity is rejected:

- stop sending `include_speech_profile=true` and `speaker_auto_assign=enabled` from the Mac;
- delete speech-profile upload/retrieval/expansion APIs when no other retained client needs them;
- delete stored user/person voice samples, voice embeddings, migration/recovery logic, and their object-storage/database helpers;
- remove live embedding matching and speaker-suggestion identity events from `/v4/listen`;
- remove conversation-derived speaker-training jobs and UI promises that naming a speaker trains future recognition;
- audit whether the server-side people registry has any surviving non-voice purpose before deleting it.

### Explicitly separate siblings

- Keep cloud STT and within-conversation diarization: the transcript may still distinguish generic speakers without remembering their identity.
- Manual renaming of speakers inside a local conversation can remain, but it must be local data and must not silently train or upload a voice profile.
- A local address-book/people feature is a separate product requirement. Rejecting voiceprints does not automatically prove that named contacts should be deleted.
- Whether microphone-channel provenance can label the Mac user as `You` without voice recognition is a separate, narrower implementation question.

### Recommendation

`delete persistent voice identity; keep diarization and local manual labels`

This removes sensitive durable voice audio and embeddings, cloud object storage, user/person embedding records, migration machinery, and extra speaker-identification compute. More importantly, it avoids rebuilding a teaching pipeline after IR-020 removed the backend conversation and audio source it currently depends on. Generic speaker separation preserves transcript readability; manual local labels preserve correction without creating a cloud biometric identity system.

### Question

Must the first shipped product automatically recognize the same person by voice across conversations using server-stored speech samples and embeddings, or can it retain generic within-conversation diarization plus local manual speaker labels?

### Decision

`delete persistent voice recognition; keep generic diarization and local manual speaker labels`

Confirmed: remove cloud speech-profile audio, user/person voice embeddings, automatic identity matching, sample migration/recovery, and conversation-derived speaker-training workflows. Retain generic within-conversation speaker IDs from diarization. Users may manually replace those generic labels locally; manual correction must not upload audio, train an embedding, or require a backend conversation.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-022 - Reusable people identities for manual speaker labels

### Requirement implied by the code

> Manually naming a speaker must create or select a reusable person identity that exists independently of any one conversation and can be referenced from transcripts across the user's history.

### Current path

```text
Mac startup
  -> GET /v1/users/people
  -> hold server people records in AppState memory

user taps Speaker 1
  -> choose You, an existing person, or + Add Person
  -> POST /v1/users/people when creating a name
  -> PATCH /v1/conversations/{id}/segments/assign-bulk
  -> server updates person_id / is_user on conversation segments
  -> Mac mirrors personId / isUser into local transcription_segments

conversation display
  -> local segment contains personId, but not the person's name
  -> peopleById resolves that ID through the server-fetched people list
  -> missing people data falls back to a generic speaker label
```

There is no local people table. The local transcript retains an opaque server `personId`, while the human-readable name remains backend-owned. The server people API's only visible Mac use is speaker naming; no separate Mac contacts/address-book product surfaced in this trace.

### Two distinct product requirements

1. **Conversation-local naming:** in one transcript, manually change `Speaker 1` to `Alice` and optionally apply that text to every segment carrying the same diarization speaker ID. The same name must be entered again in another conversation.
2. **Reusable local people:** create a local `Alice` identity once, choose it in later conversations, rename it globally, and potentially group/search all locally assigned statements by that person. This is cross-conversation identity, but manual rather than biometric.

Both can be entirely local and neither requires voice samples. The second requires a local people model, stable local IDs, lifecycle rules, and migration of every existing server-backed `personId` consumer. The first needs only conversation-owned speaker-label data and a smaller naming UI.

### Recommendation

`keep conversation-local names; delete the reusable people directory for the first ship`

This satisfies the retained manual-label requirement with the smallest durable model: `You`, a typed name, and an apply-to-this-speaker-in-this-conversation action. It removes `/v1/users/people`, server person IDs, cloud CRUD, cross-conversation identity semantics, and the need to migrate a contacts subsystem before shipping. A reusable local directory can be added later if users demonstrably need to group or repeatedly label the same people.

### Question

When a user manually names `Speaker 1` as Alice, must Alice become a reusable local identity selectable in future conversations, or is it enough for that name to apply only inside the current conversation?

### Decision

`keep conversation-local names; delete reusable people`

Confirmed: manually naming a diarized speaker applies a plain local name inside that conversation only. Do not retain `/v1/users/people`, server person IDs, reusable cross-conversation contacts, or the current create/select-person workflow. The eventual local transcript model must store the displayed name directly (or through a conversation-owned speaker-label mapping), support `You`, and apply a label only to the selected segment or matching speaker within that conversation.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-023 - Cloud synchronization of transcription preferences

### Requirement implied by the code

> A signed-in user's transcription language, single-language versus auto-detect mode, and custom vocabulary must be stored in the product backend and restored across clients rather than being owned only by this Mac.

### Current path

The Mac already persists all three settings in `AssistantSettings` via `UserDefaults`. The settings UI then maintains a second server copy:

```text
open Settings
  -> load local language / auto-detect / vocabulary
  -> GET /v1/users/language
  -> GET /v1/users/transcription-preferences
  -> backend response can overwrite the local values

change a setting
  -> immediately update local AssistantSettings
  -> PATCH language or transcription preferences in backend

open /v4/listen
  -> Mac sends its effective language
  -> backend still reads Firestore transcription preferences
  -> backend derives single-language mode, vocabulary, and translation target
```

This creates two authorities for a device-local capture configuration. A failed or delayed backend fetch can leave the local value in use temporarily and then replace it after Settings loads.

### Local-authority alternative

- Keep language, auto-detect, and vocabulary in local Mac settings.
- Remove the Mac's GET/PATCH synchronization calls for these fields.
- Send every retained cloud-STT input needed for the current session explicitly when opening `/v4/listen`, instead of asking the backend to reconstruct the request from Firestore.
- Let local Parakeet read the same local settings directly, so local and cloud modes have one configuration authority.
- Review live translation separately: if retained, its target language can also be an explicit session parameter rather than a server-owned user preference.
- Treat non-Mac clients and broader account-language uses as sibling audits; this decision does not automatically delete every backend language field.

### Recommendation

`keep transcription preferences local; delete their backend synchronization`

These are Mac runtime preferences, already have local persistence, and do not need durable cloud storage for transient STT. Passing a complete session request also makes `/v4/listen` deterministic: the backend transcribes according to the request it received, not mutable account state loaded on connection.

### Question

Must transcription language, auto-detect mode, and custom vocabulary follow the user across devices through the backend, or can this Mac own them locally and send them only as parameters for each cloud-STT session?

### Decision

`keep transcription preferences local; delete their backend synchronization and stored cloud copy`

Confirmed: the Mac owns transcription language, auto-detect mode, and custom vocabulary locally and sends the complete effective configuration with each retained cloud-STT request. Remove the Mac's GET/PATCH synchronization, remove `/v4/listen`'s Firestore dependency for these inputs, and delete the corresponding stored cloud transcription-preference fields after surviving callers are removed or migrated.

This does **not** authorize deleting the entire `users/{uid}` document or every server-side setting. `transcription_preferences` currently also contains `uses_custom_stt` telemetry, and the top-level `language` field is read by server conversation processing, memories, integrations, chat voice messages, and proactive/insight flows. Those are sibling requirements that must be reviewed before their shared cloud fields or APIs can be deleted. The offline wearable-sync readers are already inside the IR-013 deletion boundary.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-006 - Firebase identity, subscriptions, and cloud-compute quota

### Requirement implied by the code

> Every Mac user must have a Firebase-backed product account, and access to centrally funded cloud transcription and AI compute must be controlled by trials, Stripe subscription plans, stored entitlements, usage accounting, and quota enforcement.

### Current retained-STT admission path

```text
Mac starts cloud transcription
  -> AuthService obtains/refreshed Firebase bearer token
  -> open authenticated /v4/listen WebSocket
  -> backend verifies token and derives uid
  -> reject an expired desktop trial
  -> require users/{uid} to exist
  -> load valid subscription + monthly transcription usage
  -> accept unlimited/BYOK/within-quota user, otherwise emit paywall event
  -> Mac stops capture and displays its usage-limit/subscription UI
```

The same product branch includes Mac calls for subscription/trial status, available plans, overage information, checkout, upgrades, the Stripe customer portal, BYOK activation, LLM usage, and usage quota. The backend includes Firebase Auth, Firestore user/subscription state, Stripe checkout and webhooks, Redis caches, usage records, fair-use enforcement, notifications, and plan-specific fallback behavior.

### What prevents blind deletion today

- `/v4/listen` explicitly closes with `Bad user` when `users/{uid}` does not exist.
- It obtains transcription permission from subscription and usage state; removing fields without changing admission makes every affected user lose cloud STT or fall into inconsistent defaults.
- The whole `users/{uid}` document also stores unrelated product/account state. Deleting the document is broader than deleting transcription settings.
- Several failures are silent semantic fallbacks rather than compile errors: missing language becomes English/multilingual defaults, missing subscription becomes no credits or Basic limits, and missing profile/settings data changes downstream behavior.
- Stripe webhooks, account deletion, quota UI, and BYOK state can continue writing or recreating fields unless their callers are removed as part of the same boundary.

Nothing makes the data intrinsically undeletable. The safe order is to choose the surviving product contract, move retained callers off the fields, stop all writers, then delete the stored data and dead infrastructure.

### Actual product fork

1. **Hosted SaaS compute:** users sign in; the product pays for cloud STT/AI; trials, subscriptions, quota, abuse prevention, and account deletion remain product requirements.
2. **Local-first with user-funded optional cloud compute:** the app works locally without an account; a user supplies their own provider key or self-hosted endpoint for fallback; Firebase, Stripe, product subscriptions, centrally tracked usage, and the product user document are not required for transcription.
3. **Free centrally hosted compute:** remove billing but keep some admission credential, rate limit, and abuse/cost boundary. This is not equivalent to deleting identity; public unauthenticated STT would expose an unbounded paid compute endpoint.

### Recommendation

`superseded by decision: retain account and billing behavior as bootstrap scaffold`

The product will centrally host paid capabilities, so identity and entitlement are legitimate requirements. Simplification applies inside the retained boundary: reuse the existing account, admission, quota, checkout, webhook, and account-deletion flow; remove Omi-specific product data; substitute providers without inventing a new account architecture.

### Question

For the first shipped Mac product, are we paying for and selling access to hosted cloud STT under user accounts, or should cloud STT be optional and funded/configured by the user so the app itself needs no Firebase/Stripe subscription system?

### Decision

`keep account and billing scaffold; migrate Firebase project and payment provider`

Confirmed:

- retain Firebase authentication and `users/{uid}` as the account/entitlement boundary, configured against the new product's Firebase project rather than Omi's;
- retain subscription state, trials/plans as required by the eventual offer, cloud-compute quota/usage enforcement, paywall behavior, checkout/customer management, webhook-driven entitlement updates, and account deletion;
- replace Stripe-specific payment integration with Dodo Payments (`https://dodopayments.com/`) while preserving the existing product flow as the bootstrap scaffold;
- do not redesign identity, billing, or entitlements during the ruthless-deletion phase;
- continue deleting unrelated Omi cloud-data fields and APIs from the shared user document as their own product requirements are rejected;
- review exact plan names, limits, prices, and Dodo API mapping later because they are configuration/provider-migration details, not justification for retaining other Omi products.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-024 - Cloud-authoritative memories

### Requirement implied by the code

> Facts, insights, focus observations, and manually added memories must be copied to `/v3/memories`, assigned backend identities and lifecycle tiers, synchronized back into the Mac cache, and remain available to other devices and hosted backend products.

### Current path

The Mac has a substantial local `memories` table in the same GRDB database used by Rewind. It stores content, category, tags, visibility, review state, source/provenance, screenshot links, insight/focus context, lifecycle tier, deletion/read/dismissal flags, and timestamps. Local chat tools, proactive suggestions, and focus analysis already query it directly.

It is nevertheless implemented as a bidirectional cache:

```text
open Memories page
  -> read GRDB for immediate display
  -> always GET /v3/memories
  -> merge server rows into GRDB
  -> treat server lifecycle tier as authoritative
  -> run background full-sync/reconciliation passes

local Memory/Insight/Focus assistant extracts a record
  -> insert into GRDB with backendSynced=false
  -> POST /v3/memories
  -> store returned backendId and server lifecycle fields locally

manual edits/deletes/read/visibility
  -> backend mutation endpoints
  -> mirror result into the local cache
```

The backend side brings more than storage: short-term/long-term/archive lifecycle, canonical maintenance jobs, device scope, visibility/public memory, batch imports, knowledge-graph generation, hosted MCP access, persona/profile inputs, and cross-device reads.

### Local-authority alternative

- Keep the memory product and its GRDB table.
- Make local IDs, lifecycle/category, edits, deletion, read/dismissal state, search, and pagination authoritative.
- Remove `backendId`, `backendSynced`, server merge/adoption/pruning behavior, API refresh, upload retries, and `/v3/memories` CRUD from normal Mac operation.
- Keep local Memory, Insight, Focus, import, and manual-create producers, but have them finish locally.
- Keep local chat/proactive consumers reading GRDB.
- Challenge lifecycle promotion/archive rules as local product behavior rather than retaining the server merely because it currently assigns tiers.
- Delete or separately redesign cloud-only knowledge graph, hosted MCP, public visibility, persona, and cross-device memory features; accounts/billing retained under IR-006 do not imply cloud storage of memory content.

### Recommendation

`keep memories as a local product; delete backend memory synchronization and authority`

The local schema and consumers already exist. Removing the sync state makes this the same simplification chosen for transcripts: one durable local authority, no Firestore copy, no reconciliation, and no server maintenance pipeline. The actual memory feature remains.

### Question

Must a user's memory content and lifecycle sync to the product backend for cross-device/hosted use, or should the Mac's GRDB memory table be the sole authority while account and billing data remain cloud-hosted separately?

### Decision

`keep memories as a local product; delete backend memory synchronization and authority`

Confirmed: the Mac's GRDB `memories` table becomes the sole authority for memory content, identity, lifecycle/category, provenance, edits, deletion, read/dismissal state, search, and pagination. Remove normal Mac use of `/v3/memories`, Firestore memory copies, backend IDs/sync flags, upload/retry/reconciliation/pruning logic, and canonical memory maintenance jobs. Delete the memory-only cases in `backend/testing/contracts/test_desktop_backend_parity.py`, root `contract_tests/fixtures/memories.json`, and the corresponding `contracts` job/path triggers in the mixed `.github/workflows/desktop-backend-contracts.yml`; preserve its independent retained T0 self-check. Because S-12 removes the final file under `backend/testing/contracts/`, it also removes that prefix's `WORKFLOW_COVERED_PREFIXES` registration in `backend/scripts/check_unit_test_discovery.py` and updates the dedicated discovery-check tests in the same change. Local Memory, Insight, Focus, manual-create, chat, and proactive consumers remain, rewritten to finish and read locally. Hosted knowledge graph, MCP/public visibility, persona, imports, and cross-device memory projections lose their cloud source and are deletion candidates unless separately retained later. Account, entitlement, and billing data remain cloud-hosted under IR-006.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-025 - Cloud-authoritative core tasks/action items

### Requirement implied by the code

> Ordinary user tasks must be copied to `/v1/action-items`, assigned server identities, reconciled against Firestore, and remain consistent across devices and backend integrations.

### Current path

The Mac already has a broad local `action_items` GRDB model and `ActionItemStorage` query/mutation layer. It supports incomplete/completed/deleted state, dates, priority, tags/categories, source, scoring/order, recurrence and richer task metadata. Manual task creation is local-first.

`TasksStore` nevertheless treats the backend as the durable authority:

```text
open Tasks / Dashboard
  -> read local action_items for immediate display
  -> page GET /v1/action-items
  -> merge server rows into GRDB and reload
  -> fetch server ID census and reconcile absent/deleted rows
  -> run one-time full synchronization and server migrations

create task
  -> insert local row with local_<rowid> identity
  -> POST /v1/action-items
  -> replace local identity with returned backendId
  -> retry unsynced rows on later launches

complete/edit/delete/reorder/score
  -> mutate GRDB optimistically
  -> call backend mutation/batch endpoints
  -> merge or roll back according to the result
```

The backend task product also contains sharing, third-party task integrations, relevance scoring, staged-task migration, candidates, task-intelligence interventions/feedback/outcomes, work intents, and workstreams. Those are not necessary for a local checklist and are challenged separately rather than bundled into IR-025. IR-938 closes the previously missing external task-integration/export child.

### Local-authority alternative

- Keep the Tasks and Dashboard product surfaces plus the GRDB `action_items` table.
- Use stable local IDs and make create/edit/complete/delete/reorder/score operations finish locally.
- Remove `backendId`, `backendSynced`, API paging/merge, ID census, missing-row reconciliation, upload retries, rollback-on-remote-failure, full-sync flags, and server migration calls.
- Keep local/manual and retained local-agent/proactive task producers writing the same table.
- Delete `/v1/action-items` Firestore CRUD from normal Mac operation.
- Review sharing, external task integrations, staged suggestions/candidates, workstreams, and cross-device tasks as separate requirements. IR-938 now resolves the integration/export branch.

### Recommendation

`keep ordinary tasks locally; delete backend task synchronization and authority`

The local task store is already more than an offline placeholder. Making it authoritative removes a large two-way reconciliation state machine without deleting the task product. Accounts and billing remain cloud-hosted independently.

### Question

Must ordinary tasks synchronize to the Python product backend for cross-device/shared/integration use, or should the Mac's GRDB `action_items` table be their sole authority while advanced task-intelligence and integration features are reviewed separately?

### Decision

`keep ordinary tasks locally; delete backend task synchronization and authority`

Confirmed: the Mac's GRDB `action_items` table becomes the sole authority for ordinary task identity, content, completion, deletion, dates, priority, tags, ordering, scores, recurrence, and metadata. Remove normal Mac use of `/v1/action-items`, Firestore action-item copies, backend IDs/sync flags, API paging/merge, server ID census, absent-row reconciliation, upload retries, rollback-on-remote-failure, full-sync flags, and server task migrations. Manual and retained local-agent/proactive producers finish locally. Sharing, staged suggestions/candidates, task intelligence, workstreams, and cross-device task access remain separate audits; IR-938 separately deletes external task integration/export.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-026 - Cloud candidates, Suggested Tasks, and What Matters Now

### Requirement implied by the code

> The Mac must send task context to a backend control plane that stores proposed task or workstream mutations as candidates, ranks what the user should act on now, records every intervention and response, and applies accepted candidates to server-authoritative tasks or workstreams.

This is not ordinary task CRUD. It is a separate review, recommendation, and learning product layered over tasks, goals, workstreams, memories, and proactive context.

### Current production path

```text
local task/memory/goal signals and contextual matches
  -> PUT /v1/task-intelligence/context-snapshot
  -> POST /v1/what-matters-now/evaluate
  -> backend evaluates and persists ranked recommendations

candidate producers
  -> POST /v1/candidates
  -> backend stores a proposed task create/update/complete/cancel/supersede
     or a proposed workstream create, with evidence and confidence

Tasks > Suggested
  -> GET /v1/candidates/control
  -> GET /v1/candidates?status=pending&surface=suggested
  -> show at most five proposed items
  -> Do now / Later / Dismiss / Edit
  -> accept or reject candidate on backend
  -> accepted candidate mutates backend action_items or workstreams

Dashboard > What Matters Now
  -> GET /v1/what-matters-now
  -> show ranked candidate/task/workstream recommendation
  -> navigate into Suggested or an existing task/thread
  -> record Do now / Later / Dismiss feedback

all recommendation surfaces
  -> POST interventions, feedback, and outcomes
  -> owner-scoped local UserDefaults outboxes retry backend attribution writes
```

`TaskContextualResurfacingService` also sends normalized context snapshots to the same backend evaluator and can use its response for proactive interruptions. Therefore this branch is wider than the Suggested section on the Tasks page.

### What candidate acceptance really does

The backend candidate contract can propose:

- task creation;
- task update, completion, cancellation, or supersession;
- workstream creation with an anchor task.

Each proposal carries evidence references, capture and ownership confidence, optional goal/workstream links, source surface, account generation, and idempotency state. Accepting a candidate materializes the mutation in the backend task/workstream stores; it does not currently write the Mac's local GRDB task authority directly.

### Collision with decisions already made

IR-024 and IR-025 make local memories and local tasks authoritative and remove their backend copies. That breaks this system in two places:

1. its evaluator expects cloud-accessible product context and persists derived recommendation state; and
2. accepting a candidate targets backend task/workstream identities that ordinary tasks will no longer have.

Keeping this product would therefore not be a small exception. We would have to invent a new local candidate database and lifecycle, redirect candidate acceptance to local task IDs, decide which context may still be uploaded, and either retain or replace the backend ranking, feedback, rollout-control, account-generation, suppression, and attribution machinery.

### What deleting it does not mean

Deleting this control plane would not delete:

- local ordinary tasks;
- a local agent or proactive assistant creating an ordinary local task directly;
- the proactive-assistant runtime as a whole;
- local reminders or local task resurfacing that do not require backend recommendation state;
- goals or workstreams, which remain separate child audits.

It would delete the distinct review-and-learning product: Suggested candidate cards, What Matters Now recommendations, cloud context/open-loop snapshots, candidate lifecycle APIs, server evaluation/ranking, intervention/feedback/outcome telemetry, their retry outboxes, and staged-task compatibility/migration paths.

### Recommendation

`delete the cloud candidate/task-intelligence/What Matters Now product for the first ship`

Reason: its authoritative target has already been rejected, it sends locally held product context back into a substantial backend state machine, and preserving it requires a redesign rather than a simple local-storage substitution. Direct local tasks and retained local producers cover the core behavior with far less machinery. A local suggestion-review queue can be reconsidered later only if users actually need approval before an agent creates a task.

### Question

Does the first ship require this separate Suggested Tasks / What Matters Now review-and-learning product, or are ordinary local tasks plus local agent/proactive creation of those tasks enough?

### Decision

`delete the cloud candidate/task-intelligence/What Matters Now authority; retain the task-candidate review pattern locally under IR-032`

Confirmed: delete candidate and staged-task compatibility APIs, server candidate state and resolution, What Matters Now ranking/evaluation, context and open-loop snapshot uploads, intervention/feedback/outcome persistence, cloud retry outboxes, rollout-control machinery used only by this product, and associated backend/generated contracts. Keep ordinary local tasks and retained local producers. The existing task-candidate review behavior and Suggested UI are ported to local authority under IR-032; workstream candidates and What Matters Now remain deleted.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-027 - Explicit goal tracking and goal-aware assistance

### Requirement implied by the code

> The user must choose and track longer-term goals, and the app should use those goals to shape onboarding, chat advice, task ranking/extraction, focus judgments, and proactive assistance.

### The implementation currently contains two goal products

#### Older numeric goal tracker

```text
onboarding or Dashboard
  -> create a boolean/scale/numeric goal through /v1/goals
  -> backend stores it in Firestore
  -> Mac mirrors it into local GRDB goals
  -> user edits a current/target value and sees a progress bar/history
  -> backend remains authoritative and local records carry backendId/backendSynced
```

This version supports manual goals, AI-generated goals, progress extraction from chat, AI advice, task-to-goal links, goal history, and automatic retirement of stale AI goals. Despite having a local table, create/update/delete and reconciliation still depend on the backend.

#### Newer canonical goal system

```text
redesigned Dashboard
  -> DashboardIntelligenceStore loads /v1/goals/all
  -> goals have focused/background/achieved/abandoned lifecycle
  -> user may focus a limited set of goals
  -> goal details include desired outcome, success criteria,
     linked tasks, progress events, and workstreams
  -> starting work resolves a backend workstream/thread
```

This version is Firestore-authoritative and shares account-generation, idempotency, relationship, workstream, and rollout machinery with the task-intelligence product rejected in IR-026. The redesigned Home screen uses this system by default; the older numeric widget remains as a fallback/legacy design.

### Goals are not only UI decoration

The older local goal records are read by normal desktop chat and inserted into its system prompt. The Focus Assistant reads them when judging whether screen activity supports the user's goals. Task extraction/prioritization and AI profile generation also consume goals, although several of those callers still fetch the cloud copy. Onboarding explicitly asks for a measurable goal and currently saves it through the backend.

Therefore there are three legitimate choices:

1. **Delete goals from the first release.** Remove goal onboarding, both goal UIs/models, backend routes/storage, goal-aware prompting/coaching, AI goal generation/advice/progress extraction, and task/workstream goal links.
2. **Keep one simple local goal feature.** Retain a small local goal record and goal-aware chat/focus context, but delete both backend authorities, synchronization, canonical lifecycle complexity, AI generation/advice/progress automation, and workstream coupling unless separately justified.
3. **Keep the current rich goal product.** This preserves substantial Firestore, task-intelligence-control, workstream, AI-context, lifecycle, history, and synchronization machinery and conflicts with the local-first simplification unless redesigned.

### Recommendation

If goal-aware guidance is central to the new product, choose option 2: one small local goal model, with manual create/edit/complete and optional inclusion in local agent prompts. If it is not central to the first release, choose option 1 and delete goals entirely. Do not preserve the two current overlapping cloud implementations.

### Question

Does the first release actually need users to set goals so the local assistant can shape advice around them? If yes, are a few simple local goals enough, or do users need progress numbers, AI-generated goals, history, focused/background states, and linked workstream threads?

### Decision

`keep one simple local Goals feature; delete both cloud goal systems and synchronization`

Confirmed: retain one local goal model with a stable local identity, title, optional description, and active/completed status. Normal desktop chat may read active goals from the local database. Remove Firestore goal authority and normal Mac goal API calls; `backendId`/`backendSynced` and reconciliation; numeric/scale targets and progress history; AI goal generation, advice, and chat progress extraction; automatic stale-goal retirement; canonical focused/background/achieved/abandoned lifecycle; account-generation/idempotency machinery; and goal relationships to cloud tasks and workstreams. Rewrite onboarding and the surviving goal UI to create and finish locally. Whether onboarding must require a goal can be challenged later as an onboarding-flow question, without changing the retained local goal capability.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-028 - Backend workstreams and task-attached agent chat

### Requirement implied by the code

> Clicking “Work on this with Omi” for a task or goal must open a durable agent thread whose identity, related tasks, events, artifact versions, and continuation checkpoints are owned by the Python backend.

### Current path

```text
user opens task chat
  -> TaskChatCoordinator checks task.workstreamId
  -> if absent, GET candidate workflow control for account generation
  -> POST /v1/work-intents with the backend task ID
  -> backend creates/finds a Firestore workstream and links the task
  -> GET /v1/workstreams/{id}
  -> download linked backend tasks, recent events, artifacts, checkpoints
  -> prepare a context packet
  -> open TaskChatState on local Node kernel surface workstream:{id}
  -> local kernel journal stores the actual chat turns

agent finishes work
  -> local runtime may produce artifact descriptors and continuation checkpoints
  -> Mac uploads them to Firestore workstream subcollections
  -> later openings download them to continue the task thread
```

The UI is a separate sidebar chat on the Tasks page, labelled “Work on this with Omi.” The task-row “Execute” action also enters the same thread and asks the local agent to investigate or perform the task in the background. Both are distinct from normal desktop chat. Multiple backend tasks can share one workstream, and a workstream may contain a running summary, ordered events, versioned artifacts, evidence references, and per-runtime continuation checkpoints.

### What earlier decisions break

- IR-025 removes backend task IDs and Firestore action items, but `/v1/work-intents` resolves workstreams from those canonical backend tasks.
- IR-027 removes cloud goals and goal-to-workstream relationships.
- IR-026 removes the workflow-control/account-generation system this path checks before creating or mutating workstreams.

Therefore the existing backend workstream implementation cannot survive unchanged. Preserving it would recreate cloud task/goal identities and a large part of the rejected control plane.

### Important boundary

The local Node agent and its journal already store the task-chat messages. Firestore does not own the message transcript itself. The backend owns the richer container around that chat: workstream identity, linked canonical tasks, events, artifact descriptors, checkpoints, generation checks, and mutation receipts.

That leaves two practical choices:

1. **Delete task-attached agent work for the first release.** Keep only normal desktop chat. Users can mention or select a local task there, but there is no separate permanent sidebar conversation or “Execute” agent run per task.
2. **Keep simpler local task-attached agent work.** Use the local task ID directly as the local kernel surface/session identity for both sidebar chat and “Execute,” and use the local task record as context. Delete backend work intents, workstreams, events, artifact descriptors, checkpoints, account-generation checks, and cloud continuity delivery. Any artifact files remain ordinary local agent resources rather than a synchronized workstream catalog.

Keeping the current backend implementation is not compatible with the decisions already made.

### Recommendation

For the fastest first release, delete the task-specific sidebar chat and Execute path and use the already-retained normal desktop chat. If asking the agent to work persistently on an individual task is central to the product, keep only option 2 and simplify it to a local task-keyed journal.

### Question

Does the first release need “Work on this with Omi” and “Execute” as persistent agent work attached to each task, or is normal desktop chat—using local tasks as context—enough?

### Decision

`delete task-attached agent work and the complete cloud workstream product`

Confirmed: delete “Work on this with Omi,” task sidebar chat, the task-row “Execute”/background-investigation path, task-to-workstream IDs and state, goal-origin threads, work-intent resolution, workstream detail/events/artifacts/checkpoints, continuity preparation/persistence/delivery, workflow-control coupling, their UI/settings/tests/generated contracts, and the backend Firestore workstream stores and routes. Keep normal desktop chat and allow it to read or act on local tasks through separately retained local tools. A future task-specific conversation must be designed as a local feature rather than preserving this architecture.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-030 - AI screen-activity focus coach

### Requirement implied by the code

> While Rewind capture is running, the app should send selected screen images and local user context to Gemini, classify the visible activity as focused or distracted, and coach the user when their state changes.

### Current path

```text
Rewind/proactive screen capture observes the frontmost app and window
  -> wait through the configured analysis delay
  -> FocusAssistant receives a captured JPEG
  -> load local active goals, tasks, memories, time, and recent judgments
  -> send the screenshot and prompt to Google Gemini
  -> Gemini returns focused/distracted, app/site, description, coaching message

on state transition
  -> save a focus_sessions row in local GRDB
  -> also save the same event into local memories
  -> upload that memory to the product backend
  -> show a notification and focused/distracted window glow
  -> start cooldown until context changes or the interval expires

Focus page
  -> show current detected app and AI status
  -> calculate focused/distracted minutes from transition timestamps
  -> show top distractions and event history
```

This is not a user-started timer. A “focus session” is simply the period between two AI classifications. The current Mac does not call the older `/v1/focus-sessions` routes; those are a separate legacy backend store. The active Mac path uploads focus events as backend memories instead, which IR-024 has already rejected.

### Cost and privacy boundary

Rewind screenshots remain locally stored, but this assistant sends selected screenshot pixels to Gemini for classification. It also places local goal/task/memory context into that model request. Therefore “keep the focus coach locally” would mean local persistence only; the AI judgment would still be cloud compute unless a new on-device classifier is built.

The feature also brings a dedicated page, settings and exclusions, prompt customization, capture orchestration, delay/cooldown state, notifications, glow effects, focus-memory duplication, statistics, tests, and model-call cost.

### Practical choices

1. **Delete the focus product.** Keep local Rewind capture, but remove FocusAssistant, its Gemini screenshot calls, Focus page/sidebar/status, focus settings, focus session table/storage, duplicate focus memories, notifications/glows, and both legacy backend focus routes/storage.
2. **Keep a cloud-compute but local-storage focus coach.** Continue sending selected screenshots and local context to Gemini, but store results only in local `focus_sessions`; remove backend-memory uploads, backend focus routes, sync IDs/flags, and duplicate memory records. Review the history/statistics page separately under IR-029.
3. **Keep it fully on-device.** This requires a new local classifier or simpler rule system and is new product engineering, not a deletion-only simplification.

### Recommendation

For the fastest first release, delete the focus product unless distraction coaching is part of the new product's core promise. Rewind still captures and retrieves screen history without it.

### Question

Does the first release need the app to inspect screenshots with Gemini and interrupt the user when it thinks they are distracted, or should Rewind remain a passive local history without focus judgments?

### Decision

`keep Gemini focus analysis with local-only results; delete cloud focus persistence`

Confirmed: retain screen-context selection, transient Gemini screenshot/context analysis, focused/distracted classification, delay/cooldown policy, exclusions, live notification/glow behavior, and the minimum recent local state needed by the classifier. Store any durable classification records only in local GRDB. Remove the second write into local memories, backend memory upload, backend IDs/sync flags and retry/delete behavior, and the unused legacy `/v1/focus-sessions` and `/v1/focus-stats` routes/database. The dedicated Focus history/statistics product remains a separate decision under IR-029.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-029 - Focus history and statistics page

### Requirement implied by the code

> Users need a dedicated page to review the AI focus coach's classifications over time, measure focused versus distracted time, identify their most distracting apps, search older events, and delete their history.

### Current path

```text
FocusAssistant changes between focused and distracted
  -> insert transition into local GRDB focus_sessions
  -> FocusStorage also caches up to 500 records in UserDefaults
  -> load the last 30 days into memory
  -> infer each period's duration from the next transition timestamp

Focus page
  -> current app and current AI judgment
  -> analysis-delay and cooldown countdowns
  -> today's focused minutes, distracted minutes, and focus rate
  -> most distracting apps/sites
  -> today/all-history filter and text search
  -> delete one event or clear the visible history
```

The live coach itself does not require this entire page. It needs the current classification, cooldown, and a short recent judgment history. Durable statistics and long-term browsing are an additional product requirement.

### Practical choices

1. **Live coach only.** Keep notifications/glows and only minimal recent local state. Delete the Focus navigation page, long-term history, statistics, top-distraction ranking, search, UserDefaults record cache, and history-management UI.
2. **Keep a simple local Focus page.** Use local GRDB as the sole authority and show current status, today's focused/distracted time, and a short recent history. Delete duplicated UserDefaults record storage and broader history/search complexity.
3. **Keep the full page locally.** Retain 30-day/all-time history, top distractions, search, deletion, and clear-all behavior, but remove all backend/sync fields under IR-030.

### Recommendation

Because the focus coach itself is retained, option 2 gives the user a visible explanation and small amount of value from the collected classifications without preserving the whole analytics product.

### Question

Should the first release show a simple local Focus page with today's focused time, distracted time, and recent judgments, or should focus coaching exist only as live notifications with no history page?

### Decision

`keep a simple local Focus page`

Confirmed: use local GRDB as the sole record authority and retain the current AI status, analysis-delay/cooldown visibility, today's focused time, today's distracted time, and a short recent-judgment list. Delete the 30-day/all-time browsing mode, text search, top-distraction analytics, duplicate UserDefaults record cache, backend-derived IDs/sync behavior, and broader history-management complexity. Retention length and deletion controls can be set during implementation, but must stay small and local.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-031 - Automatic task extraction from screen activity

### Requirement implied by the code
