### Requirement implied by the code

> In addition to managed subscriber access, PTT must let a user enter a personal OpenAI or Gemini API key, connect directly with it, pay the provider separately, and bypass managed-session usage reporting.

### Decision

`delete PTT BYOK access`

Confirmed: PTT has one commercial access model for the first release. A paying user signs into the product and uses the managed short-lived credential path retained under IR-007. Remove PTT-specific personal-key selection, `.byokKey` authentication branches, direct-key connection eligibility, BYOK-specific provider fallback, BYOK-specific usage-report bypass, PTT setup/error wording that asks for a provider key, and focused tests that exist only for that second PTT access mode.

This decision was originally scoped to PTT so the shared key plumbing was not deleted without review. IR-062 subsequently completed that sibling audit and deletes customer BYOK globally: `APIKeyService` BYOK state, developer-key Settings, account activation, and personal-key use by normal text Chat, transcription, embeddings, TTS, and model proxies are all inside the product-wide deletion boundary.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-056 - Per-user managed PTT usage accounting

### Requirement implied by the code

> Because the product pays OpenAI or Gemini for managed PTT, each completed voice turn must count against the user's product usage and contribute an estimated provider cost to the server account ledger.

### Current path

```text
OpenAI/Gemini finishes a managed PTT turn
  -> provider sends token-usage metadata to the Mac
  -> Mac separates text, audio, cached-input, and output token counts
  -> POST /v2/realtime/usage with counts and opaque cache/context IDs
  -> backend calculates an estimated dollar cost
  -> Firestore users/{uid}/llm_usage/{date}
       increments desktop_chat totals
       increments desktop_chat_realtime breakdown
       increments one quota question for the visible PTT turn
  -> monthly usage reader combines PTT and typed-chat questions
  -> Mac usage limiter can block another managed PTT turn and show upgrade UI
```

The usage report does not contain microphone audio, transcript text, answer text, screenshots, OCR, or rendered context. It contains provider/model names, numeric token counts, and opaque hashes/identifiers.

### What deleting it means

PTT would still technically work through the managed temporary credential retained in IR-007, and the provider would still bill our account. But our product would no longer know which user generated that cost, could not count PTT against a plan limit, and could not show accurate per-user usage. Every subscriber would effectively receive unmetered managed PTT unless a different accounting system were built.

The existing report is useful product metering, not perfect security: it is sent by the Mac after the provider turn and is fire-and-forget, so a modified client or a failed request can omit usage. Strong fraud-proof accounting would require provider-side reconciliation or a different token/session ledger and is a separate hardening project.

### Recommendation

`keep count-only per-user usage accounting for managed PTT and adapt its entitlement/plan mapping to our Firebase and Dodo scaffold`

Because we chose to pay the provider on the subscriber's behalf, removing all usage accounting would expose an uncontrolled variable cost. The current payload avoids storing private voice content and already feeds the shared chat quota UI. Exact plan limits and pricing can change later without removing the ledger.

### Question

Should managed PTT usage count toward each subscriber's product allowance, or should every paying subscriber receive unlimited unmetered PTT at our expense?

### Decision

`resolved - keep count-only per-user usage, estimated provider cost, and quota-question accounting for managed PTT. Retain the shared monthly allowance/upgrade UI behavior and adapt plan limits and entitlement mapping to our Firebase and Dodo scaffold. Do not store voice audio, transcript text, answer text, screenshots, OCR, or rendered prompt context in this usage ledger. Stronger provider-side reconciliation remains a separate hardening question, not a reason to delete basic accounting.`

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-057 - Firestore record for every temporary PTT credential

### Requirement implied by the code

> Every time the backend mints a short-lived OpenAI or Gemini credential, it must also store a hashed record of that credential in the user's Firestore account.

### Current write

```text
POST /v2/realtime/session succeeds
  -> hash the temporary credential with SHA-256
  -> write users/{uid}/realtime_sessions/{credential_hash}
       provider
       model
       status = minted
       minted_at
       expires_at
       max_minutes
```

The actual temporary credential is not stored. Only its hash and metadata are written.

### What the code proves

A repository-wide search finds only the writer and its unit-test stub. No production code reads this collection to authorize PTT, check entitlement, calculate usage, enforce quota, reconcile provider cost, revoke a credential, investigate support problems, or display session history. The write is best-effort: if Firestore fails, the backend logs a warning and still returns the credential, so working PTT deliberately does not depend on it.

OpenAI or Gemini already owns credential validity and expiry. The separate `llm_usage` ledger retained under IR-056 records billable use.

### Recommendation

`delete the unread realtime_sessions Firestore write`

Deleting it does not change PTT, authentication, expiration, usage limits, billing, or the retained cost ledger. Keeping it adds a cloud write and a stored collection with no named consumer. If a future security or compliance requirement needs a credential-mint audit trail, it should define retention, reader, investigation workflow, and deletion policy explicitly rather than preserving an unused document indefinitely.

### Question

Do we have a real security, support, or legal requirement to retain a Firestore audit record every time a temporary PTT credential is created?

### Decision

`resolved - delete users/{uid}/realtime_sessions token-hash documents, _record_session/_persist_session, their mint-call hooks, and focused tests that assert this unused write. Keep provider-owned credential expiry, managed token minting under IR-007, and the separate billable usage/cost/quota ledger under IR-056.`

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-055 - Backend realtime-STT relay as an intermediate PTT fallback

### Requirement implied by the code

> If the primary direct realtime voice hub has not connected while the user is still holding PTT, the Mac must switch mid-recording to a second live transcription path that sends microphone frames through our backend before falling back to completed-turn batch transcription.

### Where it sits in the current fallback chain

```text
normal case
  -> direct RealtimeHub session on the Mac
  -> OpenAI Realtime or Gemini Live performs speech, reasoning, tools, and voice

hub is still unavailable while user is holding PTT
  -> RealtimeOmniService opens our /v1/omni/relay WebSocket
  -> Mac streams buffered and new microphone frames to our backend
  -> backend opens another realtime OpenAI/Gemini WebSocket
  -> backend copies every frame in both directions
  -> provider returns interim/final transcript only
  -> transcript goes through the normal text agent and existing TTS

relay fails, or hub failed after the user released PTT
  -> transcribe the complete buffered turn with existing batch STT
  -> transcript goes through the normal text agent and existing TTS
```

The relay is not the primary PTT path and it does not run the local agent's reasoning or tools. In current PTT use it is an STT-only voice shell. Its special user-visible value is that, after the primary hub times out during a long held turn, interim transcription can continue before the user releases the shortcut.

### Cost of keeping it

- a long-lived authenticated backend WebSocket for each fallback turn;
- backend forwarding of all microphone frames to another provider WebSocket;
- separate OpenAI and Gemini wire-protocol handling on the Mac relay client;
- provider-key/BYOK, paywall, gateway-mode, buffering, resampling, timeout, deduplication, and teardown branches;
- `RealtimeOmniService`, `/v1/omni/relay`, settings/provider selection, diagnostics, tests, and backend dependencies.

The current relay also contains BYOK handling that conflicts with the PTT BYOK deletion in IR-058 and would need pruning even if the relay survives.

### Deletion alternative

Keep the microphone audio buffer that already exists. If the direct hub is unavailable, continue recording locally and use the existing batch-STT fallback as soon as the user releases PTT:

```text
direct realtime hub
  -> if unavailable: buffer locally until release
  -> batch STT
  -> normal local text agent
  -> existing TTS spoken response
```

PTT still answers the question. The lost behavior is live interim transcription during the fallback turn, and the fallback answer begins later because transcription starts after release. The primary working realtime path, spoken response, text-agent tools, and batch recovery remain.

### Recommendation

`delete the intermediate backend realtime-STT relay and fall directly from the primary hub to the existing completed-turn batch-STT path`

This removes a second realtime transport and an audio-proxy workload from our backend while preserving an existing recovery path. It is a real reliability/latency tradeoff, not a claim that PTT can be deleted: when the main realtime hub fails, fallback becomes slower and no longer shows live transcript text during the held turn.

### Question

When the primary realtime hub cannot connect, do we require live interim transcription while the user is still holding PTT, or is it acceptable to buffer the turn locally and run batch transcription immediately after they release it?

### Decision

`resolved - keep the intermediate backend realtime-STT relay as a PTT fallback when the direct provider hub is unavailable while the user is still holding the shortcut. Preserve live interim/final fallback transcription and the handoff into the normal text-agent/TTS answer path. This keeps microphone audio forwarding through /v1/omni/relay for fallback turns. Do not infer that the relay keeps PTT BYOK, both providers, every setting, or all current protocol branches; IR-058 still removes PTT BYOK and the remaining children stay separately reviewable.`

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-059 - Completed-turn batch STT as final PTT recovery

### Requirement implied by the code

> If both the primary provider-native realtime path and the retained live STT relay fail, the Mac must preserve the complete microphone recording and make one final transcription attempt after the user releases PTT.

### Current path

```text
PTT begins
  -> Mac keeps a bounded copy of the complete 16 kHz microphone turn

direct realtime hub fails
  -> retained /v1/omni/relay live-STT fallback starts

relay fails, times out, or never returns a final transcript
  -> stop the dead relay
  -> keep recording until the user releases PTT
  -> POST complete PCM buffer to /v2/voice-message/transcribe
  -> backend selects its prerecorded STT provider/model
  -> transcript returns to the Mac
  -> normal local text agent reasons and uses retained tools
  -> existing TTS speaks the answer
```

The same batch path is also used when the direct realtime hub fails only after the user has already released PTT, because there is no value in starting a live relay for a completed recording.

### What deleting it means

The primary realtime hub and the relay remain. But when both fail during a turn, the buffered recording is discarded and the user receives an error instead of one final recovery attempt. Deleting the PTT caller would remove audio buffering/finalization and some failure-state/tests, but the shared `/v2/voice-message/transcribe` endpoint still has non-PTT/mobile and separately auditable callers.

### Recommendation

`keep completed-turn batch STT as the final PTT recovery path`

It reuses an existing authenticated endpoint and the audio buffer already required for warm-up/failure handling. It is slower than realtime, but it runs only when the two realtime routes have already failed and prevents the user's spoken question from being lost. PTT-specific BYOK headers must still be pruned consistently with IR-058; that is not a reason to remove the recovery path.

### Question

If both realtime PTT paths fail, should the app make this final batch-transcription attempt, or immediately fail the voice turn and ask the user to try again?

### Decision

`resolved - keep completed-turn batch STT as the final PTT recovery path after the direct realtime hub and retained live relay have failed or become unavailable after release. Preserve the bounded whole-turn audio buffer, authenticated /v2/voice-message/transcribe call, backend provider selection, transcript handoff to the normal local text agent, and existing TTS response. Remove PTT-specific BYOK headers consistently with IR-058 without removing this managed recovery path.`

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-060 - Provider-native realtime speech-to-speech as the primary PTT path

### Requirement implied by the code

> In the normal successful case, one realtime OpenAI or Gemini model should hear the user's audio, reason, call scoped tools, and stream spoken audio back inside the same live session.

### Current normal path

```text
user holds PTT
  -> microphone audio streams into RealtimeHubSession
  -> one realtime provider performs input transcription
  -> the same provider reasons and may request scoped local tools
  -> tool results return into that live provider session
  -> provider begins streaming spoken audio before a separate text/TTS pipeline finishes
  -> another PTT press can interrupt the in-progress spoken reply
```

This is different from the retained fallback cascade:

```text
live relay or batch STT
  -> transcript text
  -> normal local text-agent runtime
  -> completed/generated answer text
  -> separate TTS playback
```

### What native realtime buys

- faster time to the beginning of a spoken answer;
- one live voice session rather than separate STT, text-model, and TTS requests;
- provider-native spoken delivery and turn timing;
- in-session tool calls and continuation;
- interruption/barge-in capability, although its exact behavior remains a separate child audit.

### What deleting it means

PTT would still exist because the relay and batch routes are retained. But every ordinary question would be forced through transcription, the normal text agent, and TTS. That would turn the current failure/degraded route into the only product experience. Managed ephemeral-token minting from IR-007, direct provider WebSockets, native audio playback, context caching, and provider-specific realtime tooling would lose their primary purpose and need to be reopened for deletion.

### Recommendation

`keep provider-native realtime speech-to-speech as the normal PTT path`

This is the existing fast spoken-assistant behavior, while the relay and batch paths remain reliability fallbacks. Replacing it with the slower cascade would be a deliberate product downgrade, not merely removal of cloud synchronization. The provider portfolio, barge-in details, screen grounding, tool set, caching, and continuity remain separate decisions.

### Question

For normal successful PTT turns, should the realtime model continue hearing the voice and streaming the spoken answer directly, or should every turn be converted to text, processed by normal Chat, and spoken later through TTS?

### Decision

`resolved - keep the existing provider-native realtime speech-to-speech path as the normal PTT experience. Preserve the direct live provider session in which microphone audio, reasoning, scoped tool calls, and streamed spoken output share one turn. Keep the relay and batch STT -> normal text agent -> TTS routes as fallbacks rather than promoting them to the normal experience. Provider portfolio, barge-in details, screen/local grounding, tools, caching, and continuity remain separate child decisions.`

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-061 - Two realtime providers and cross-provider failover

### Requirement implied by the code

> Normal realtime PTT must work with both OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live, let the configured/automatic choice select one, and try the other provider before degrading to the retained relay/text-agent/TTS cascade.

### Current provider differences

```text
OpenAI Realtime
  -> gpt-realtime-2
  -> GA speech-to-speech
  -> 24 kHz microphone input
  -> standard authenticated WebSocket
  -> explicit input-transcription language hint
  -> in-session cancellation for barge-in

Gemini Live
  -> gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview
  -> lower configured token prices
  -> 16 kHz microphone input
  -> native screenshot/video frame grounding
  -> custom/raw WebSocket handling on the Mac
  -> no explicit transcription-language hint
  -> fresh-session replacement for active-reply barge-in
```

Both providers have separate authentication/token-mint requests, session setup, event parsing, audio/transcript handling, usage parsing, tool-call wire formats, interruption behavior, errors, and focused tests. The relay also speaks both provider protocols.

### Current failover behavior

The Advanced setting can select Auto, Gemini, or OpenAI. Auto currently resolves to a daily model pick and falls back to Gemini when no pick exists. If the selected primary provider has an authentication or quota failure, the hub can mint a credential for the alternate provider and try it before falling to the retained non-native voice cascade.

### Choices

1. **Keep both providers.** Preserve provider redundancy and the ability to use Gemini's cheaper/vision-oriented path or OpenAI's GA/language-hinted path. Continue maintaining two complete realtime protocols.
2. **Keep one provider.** Delete the other provider's minting, transport, protocol parsing, failover, pricing, settings, and tests. This materially reduces code, but one provider outage or quota problem immediately degrades to the relay/text-agent/TTS fallback.

The Auto picker and its daily Artificial Analysis/backend model-selection machinery are decided separately under IR-600.

### Recommendation

`keep both realtime providers for the first release, then challenge Auto selection and the user-facing provider picker separately`

Both implementations already exist and supply materially different strengths. More importantly, cross-provider failover preserves the fast native voice experience when one provider has a provider-specific quota/auth problem; the relay and batch paths remain slower degraded modes. This recommendation does not keep BYOK, which was deleted for PTT under IR-058.

### Question

Should the first release keep both OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live for managed PTT and fail over between them, or choose one provider and accept immediate degradation to the relay/text-agent/TTS path when it is unavailable?

### Decision

`keep both OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live as interchangeable managed PTT providers, with explicit switching and cross-provider failover`

Confirmed: retain both provider-native speech-to-speech implementations as first-class production paths. Preserve managed short-lived credential minting for both providers; the direct client WebSocket transports; provider-specific session setup, microphone sample-rate handling, audio/transcript/event parsing, tool-call and tool-result protocols, screenshot grounding, interruption mechanics, usage parsing and count-only accounting; and the focused tests that keep both paths behaviorally interchangeable behind the normalized realtime-hub contract.

Retain an explicit provider-selection seam so the configured primary can be changed between OpenAI and Gemini without changing the surrounding PTT product. If the chosen primary fails with an eligible authentication, quota, or early transport failure, try the other retained native provider before degrading to the separately retained backend relay and batch-STT -> normal-Chat -> TTS paths.

This does not restore customer BYOK, which remains deleted under IR-058/062. IR-600 subsequently keeps the daily Artificial Analysis-backed Auto picker and the current user-facing Voice Model selection exactly as implemented. Specific model aliases may be upgraded behind each retained provider contract without reopening the decision to keep both providers.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## Parallel review range: Python backend and model workloads

IR-600 onward is reserved for the retained Python backend services and model-workload review so this work can proceed without colliding with the parallel Home and Conversation Detail teardown ranges.

## IR-600 - Daily Artificial Analysis-backed Auto realtime-provider selection

### Requirement implied by the code

> Advanced Settings must let the user choose Auto, Gemini, or OpenAI for realtime PTT. Auto must refresh a backend-selected provider once per day using Artificial Analysis quality and speed data, while retaining the last successful choice and falling back to Gemini when no choice is available.

### Exact current behavior from the code

The Voice Model control exposes three choices:

- **Auto** - “Daily-picks the best model by quality & speed” and is the default setting;
- **Gemini** - the Gemini Live path retained under IR-061;
- **OpenAI** - the OpenAI Realtime path retained under IR-061.

Manual Gemini or OpenAI selection directly chooses that provider. Auto asks authenticated Python route `/v1/auto/model-pick` for one of those same provider identifiers. The backend maps the realtime providers to Artificial Analysis proxy text models, scores matching data at 65% quality and 35% speed with speed capped at 250 tokens per second, and holds one process-local result for 24 hours. Its response includes the selected provider, score inputs, and Artificial Analysis attribution.

The Mac independently caches the last successful Auto pick and date in `UserDefaults`, refreshes at most once per local day, and retains the last good result if a refresh fails. With no usable server or local pick, both the backend and client choose Gemini. A changed manual setting or refreshed Auto result notifies the realtime hub so it clears stale failover state and warms the newly effective provider.

This behavior retains the `ARTIFICIALANALYSIS_API_KEY` backend dependency, the authenticated route and response contract, the daily server/client caches, the Gemini fallback, the user-facing picker and effective-provider status copy, and the focused tests around each layer. IR-061 separately owns both native provider implementations and cross-provider failover after the primary choice is resolved.

### Choices

1. **Keep it exactly as implemented.** Retain Auto as the default alongside both manual choices, including the daily Artificial Analysis-backed selection, caches, fallback, Settings copy, hub re-warm, and tests.
2. **Delete Auto but keep manual switching.** Remove the external ranking dependency and daily caches while retaining a direct Gemini/OpenAI choice.
3. **Hide provider choice.** Keep both providers internally but move primary-provider selection to controlled configuration rather than user-facing Settings.

### Recommendation

`delete Auto but keep the direct Gemini/OpenAI picker`

The direct picker already provides the interchangeability requested under IR-061. The Auto path adds an external ranking dependency and two caching policies while choosing a native audio model indirectly from proxy text-model quality and speed. That is not a direct measurement of this product's voice quality, latency, tool behavior, or reliability.

### Question

Should Auto remain exactly as implemented, or should the first release keep only direct Gemini/OpenAI selection?

### Decision

`keep the Auto/Gemini/OpenAI Voice Model selection and daily Artificial Analysis-backed Auto behavior exactly as implemented`

Confirmed: preserve Auto as the default option and retain the complete current control plane unchanged: the three-choice Advanced Settings picker and labels; persisted manual selection; effective-provider display; authenticated `/v1/auto/model-pick` route; Artificial Analysis proxy-model mapping, 65/35 quality-speed scoring, attribution, and 24-hour backend cache; once-per-local-day Mac refresh; last-good local cache; Gemini fallback; settings-change notification and realtime-hub re-warm; environment configuration; and existing tests.

Manual Gemini and OpenAI choices remain available whenever the user wants to bypass Auto and switch directly. When Auto is selected, its resolved provider remains the primary; the cross-provider failover retained under IR-061 still applies afterward when that primary has an eligible failure. This decision changes no provider protocol, customer-BYOK decision, model alias, or product code.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-601 - Realtime voice escalation to the managed Claude model

### Requirement implied by the code

> OpenAI Realtime or Gemini Live must be able to call `ask_higher_model` when the user rejects an answer, asks for a deeper answer, or needs facts the realtime model does not know. The Mac must send that question and the retained local context to managed Claude, then give Claude's text back to the realtime provider to adapt and speak.

### Exact current behavior from the code

Both realtime providers receive the same generated `ask_higher_model` tool. Its description tells them to use it sparingly: when the user pushes back, rephrases, says the prior answer is wrong, requests a better/deeper answer, or needs precise current facts. Ordinary, creative, and long-form questions are meant to stay with the realtime provider.

When the provider calls the tool, the Mac:

1. requires the voice turn's immutable account owner still to be current;
2. uses the provider's `query`, or the turn transcript when no query is supplied;
3. attaches the locally resolved semantic guidance and canonical Chat context plus any provider-supplied context clearly labelled as untrusted;
4. sends a non-streaming, 1,024-token Claude request through the same authenticated `/v2/chat/completions` boundary retained under IR-113;
5. returns Claude's text to the realtime provider, which decides how to phrase and speak it.

The request has a 60-second timeout. An account change fails closed. Other network/model errors are converted into the ordinary tool text “I ran into an error reaching the model,” so the realtime provider can speak the failure instead of terminating the whole voice turn.

### Current live-facts mismatch

The escalation system prompt tells Claude to use web search for current news, weather, prices, scores, and schedules. The Mac also sends `omi_web_search: true`. In the current checkout, however, `backend/routers/desktop_chat.py` never reads that field, never injects a web-search tool, and sends the translated request directly to Anthropic. Therefore the current escalation can provide a second Claude opinion, but it does **not** currently provide the promised live web lookup through this path.

### Choices

1. **Keep the second-model escalation.** Retain `ask_higher_model` as a deeper-reasoning fallback that reuses the already retained Claude gateway. Audit the inaccurate live-web-search promise and error-as-success behavior as separate children.
2. **Delete the escalation.** Make the selected OpenAI/Gemini realtime model answer every voice question itself, removing the extra tool, context handoff, second model call, latency, cost, and failure path.

### Recommendation

`keep ask_higher_model, then separately repair or remove its unsupported live-web-search promise`

The foundational Claude endpoint is already retained under IR-113, so this capability adds no new model provider or Python route. It gives voice a useful deeper-reasoning escape hatch when a user explicitly rejects an answer. The current-facts claim should not be used as a reason to keep it because that part does not work in the current Python route.

### Question

Should realtime voice retain `ask_higher_model` so it can hand difficult or challenged questions to Claude, or should OpenAI/Gemini answer every voice question themselves?

### Decision

`delete the realtime ask_higher_model tool entirely`

Reopened and confirmed after the live-web mismatch was explained: remove `ask_higher_model` from the source tool manifest and regenerated OpenAI/Gemini schemas, realtime capability lists, authorization surface, provider instructions, dispatch switch, synthetic harnesses, and tests. Delete its unique Mac execution path: `escalateToHigherModel`, escalation prompt/body construction, `omi_web_search` flag, owner-bound higher-model transport, response parsing, failure text, logging, and comments. Remove files or context/cache plumbing only when no surviving caller remains after regeneration and reference tracing.

The selected OpenAI Realtime or Gemini Live model now owns every ordinary voice answer itself. It must answer, decline, or state that it cannot verify live information; voice no longer calls Claude for a second opinion. This does not delete the managed `/v2/chat/completions` endpoint or normal typed Chat retained under IR-113. IR-603 separately deletes the Agent Pill title/ack caller. This decision does not change the two-provider portfolio, Auto/manual selection, or cross-provider transport failover retained under IR-061 and IR-600.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-602 - Truthful live web lookup for voice escalations

### Requirement implied by the code

> When realtime voice delegates a current-facts question through `ask_higher_model`, the retained Claude path must actually search the live public web and ground its answer in that lookup rather than answering from model knowledge while claiming freshness.

### Exact current behavior from the code

The user-visible intent already exists in three places: the realtime tool description says to escalate for precise up-to-date facts; the escalation system prompt tells Claude to search for news, weather, prices, scores, and schedules; and every escalation request includes `omi_web_search: true`.

The Python `/v2/chat/completions` implementation does not honor that intent. `_request` translates only the supported Chat fields, drops `omi_web_search`, and calls Anthropic without a web-search tool. The non-streaming response path extracts ordinary text and tool calls but has no live-search continuation, source, or citation projection. The result can therefore sound current without having performed the promised lookup.

This is specific to realtime voice's direct higher-model request. Normal typed Chat has its own public-web routing and progress machinery; changing this voice child need not remove or redesign that separate typed-Chat behavior.

### Choices

1. **Implement the promised live lookup.** Route qualifying current-facts escalations through a real managed search-capable model path, keep public queries privacy-bounded, fail clearly when lookup fails, and preserve enough source provenance for the spoken answer and local Chat record.
2. **Remove the promise for v1.** Keep IR-601 only as a Claude reasoning escalation. Delete `omi_web_search`, the current-facts/web-search instructions, and the corresponding tool-description claim so voice never presents model knowledge as live research.

### Recommendation

`implement a truthful live lookup for current-facts voice escalations`

Current weather, prices, scores, schedules, and news are ordinary assistant questions, and confidently stale speech is worse than a clear lookup failure. The repository already contains managed Anthropic server-tool pass-through and typed-Chat public-web machinery, so this can reuse an existing provider/control-plane direction rather than introduce a new search vendor. The retained boundary should require an actual lookup before making time-sensitive claims, avoid sending unrelated private context into public search, and surface the source in the spoken answer or visible Chat record.

### Question

Should realtime voice gain a real, privacy-bounded live lookup for current facts, or should we remove every live-web claim from `ask_higher_model` and keep it only for deeper reasoning?

### Decision

`delete by dependency with the entire ask_higher_model tool under IR-601`

Confirmed: do not build a voice-specific web-search continuation. Deleting `ask_higher_model` removes its current-facts tool description, escalation prompt, `omi_web_search` request field, unsupported freshness claim, and all prospective source/citation projection for this path. Normal typed Chat's separate public-web behavior is outside this deletion and remains unchanged.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-603 - Claude-generated Agent Pill title and acknowledgement

### Requirement implied by the code

> When a newly spawned background-agent pill has no title already supplied by its router, the Mac must make a separate Claude Haiku request to replace its local title with a polished three-to-five-word title and replace its temporary Starting/Warming status with a short friendly acknowledgement.

### Exact current behavior from the code

An Agent Pill is the small visible item representing a background agent run. It immediately has enough local UI to start:

- its initial title is derived without AI from the first three words of the user's request, uppercased and capped at 32 characters;
- its status begins as `Starting…` unless the caller already supplied an acknowledgement;
- the actual background agent starts independently of title generation.

If the caller did not provide `preFetchedTitle`, the Mac launches an additional best-effort network request in parallel. It sends the full background-agent request to authenticated `/v2/chat/completions`, selects Claude Haiku, asks for at most 120 tokens, and waits up to eight seconds for one JSON object containing a polished title and acknowledgement.

For example:

```text
User request: “Research the best accounting tools for a small design studio”

Immediate local pill:
  title = “RESEARCH THE BEST”
  status = “Starting…”

Possible later Haiku update:
  title = “Compare Studio Accounting Tools”
  status = “Got it, comparing accounting tools.”
```

If auth, network, HTTP, response parsing, or the model fails, nothing important fails: the original local title stays and the background agent keeps running. If the router already supplied a title, this second call is skipped.

Despite the code comment describing a spoken acknowledgement, this generated acknowledgement is only assigned to the pill's temporary `latestActivity` text. The current voice-spawn path speaks a separately supplied journal acknowledgement or a generic local kickoff; it does not speak the Haiku-generated acknowledgement. The transient text is also replaced as the run advances to `Working…` and later statuses.

### Choices

1. **Keep the cosmetic model call.** Pay for and maintain a second request so some pills receive a more polished title and very short-lived custom status text.
2. **Delete it.** Keep the immediate deterministic title and normal status progression, or improve the local title formatter without sending the request to another model. This does not change the background agent's work, result, journal, or lifecycle.

### Recommendation

`delete the Claude Haiku title/ack call and keep pill metadata local`

The call sends the user's full task to a model, consumes quota/cost, adds an eight-second asynchronous failure surface, and can visibly rename a pill after it appears. Its failure path proves the product already works without it. The generated acknowledgement is not actually spoken and disappears as soon as real run activity arrives. A deterministic local title is sufficient cosmetic metadata; an authoritative title already supplied by the router should still win when present.

### Question

Should we delete this cosmetic Haiku call and keep Agent Pill title/status generation local, or retain it for prettier titles?

### Decision

`delete the Claude Haiku title/ack call and keep Agent Pill metadata local for v1`

Confirmed for v1 simplicity and ease of mind: remove `generateTitleAndAck`, its extra authenticated `/v2/chat/completions` request, Haiku model selection, prompt, eight-second timeout, response/JSON parsing, late title/status mutation, logs, comments, and tests that exist only for this cosmetic call. Remove the unused generated acknowledgement and instant-ack helpers only where reference tracing proves no surviving caller.

Preserve the immediate deterministic title derived from the request, the normal `Starting…` -> `Working…` -> terminal status lifecycle, any authoritative title or acknowledgement already supplied by the router, account-owner fencing around surviving pill updates, and all background-agent execution, results, journal, and UI behavior unrelated to cosmetic generation. The managed Claude endpoint remains for normal typed Chat under IR-113.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-604 - Shipped Chat Prompt Lab and direct Anthropic BYOK

### Requirement implied by the code

> Every signed-in desktop user must be able to open a prompt-engineering workbench from Advanced Settings, supply a personal Anthropic API key, run real-context Chat evaluations, ask Claude to grade and improve prompts, inspect repository prompt history, and compare those versions with production message ratings.

### Exact current behavior from the code

Advanced Settings always renders **Dev Tools -> Chat Prompt Lab -> Open**. There is no debug-build, employee, or administrator gate around the card. It opens a separate 1,100 x 750 window containing prompt history, a prompt editor, evaluation questions, AI and human scores, and version comparison.

The lab is not normal Chat. It is an internal product-development workbench embedded in the shipped app:

- it stores a user-entered Anthropic API key in `UserDefaults` under `chatlab_anthropic_api_key`;
- it calls `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` directly from the Mac for prompt generation and AI grading;
- it uses Sonnet for test answers and Haiku for grading;
- its test questions include memories, conversations, screen context, tasks, meetings, and personal facts;
- it runs those questions through a separate local `chat_lab` agent surface so they do not enter the ordinary Chat thread;
- in a source checkout, it shells out to `/usr/bin/git` to reconstruct prompt-changing commits from the repository;
- it fetches production ratings and tries to attribute them to prompt versions by date;
- in an ordinary shipped app without the source repository, the git-history portion simply becomes empty.

The lab does not change the production prompt automatically. Its generated versions and evaluation work help a developer compare prompt ideas inside the UI. Removing it does not remove normal typed Chat, its production prompt, the local agent loop, or the retained managed Claude endpoint.

### Existing decision conflict

IR-062 already deletes the product-wide customer BYOK plan and its stored provider keys. Chat Lab independently recreates a smaller Anthropic-only BYOK path and stores that key in ordinary preferences. Keeping the lab exactly as written would therefore contradict the accepted no-customer-BYOK boundary even if the rest of the four-provider BYOK UI is removed.

### Choices

1. **Delete the shipped Chat Lab.** Remove its Advanced Settings card, window/view model, direct Anthropic key and requests, local lab surface helpers, prompt-history/rating plumbing, special model constants, and exclusive tests. Prompt evaluation can live in repository-owned developer scripts or an internal tool outside the customer app if needed later.
2. **Keep it as an internal tool.** Add a real development/employee gate, remove direct BYOK, and route model calls through managed credentials. This retains a large prompt-evaluation surface and must clearly separate test queries from production user data and quota.
3. **Keep it customer-visible.** Reverse part of IR-062 and intentionally support a personal Anthropic key plus this developer workbench as a product feature.

### Recommendation

`delete Chat Prompt Lab from the v1 desktop app`

It is a developer workflow, not a user capability, and it currently exposes source-checkout assumptions, production-rating plumbing, real personal context, direct provider networking, and a separately stored BYOK secret inside the customer app. Deleting it gives the simplest v1 and reinforces the already accepted managed-credentials boundary. A future prompt-evaluation harness can be built as an internal repository tool without shipping it to customers.

### Question

Should the v1 app delete Chat Prompt Lab entirely, or retain it as a gated internal developer tool?

### Decision

`delete Chat Prompt Lab entirely from the v1 desktop app`

Confirmed: remove the unconditional Advanced Settings Dev Tools card, `ChatLabView` and its window manager/view model/data models, the `chatlab_anthropic_api_key` preference and direct Anthropic requests, prompt generation and AI grading, real-context lab questions and isolated `chat_lab` runtime surface, repository/git prompt-history reader, production-ratings attribution, prompt-version comparison/editor state, ChatProvider lab-only helpers, ChatLab-only model constants, and exclusive tests and documentation. Reference-trace shared Chat/runtime helpers before removal and retain anything with an independent production caller.

This does not change normal Chat, its production prompt, the local Node/Pi loop, managed Claude inference retained under IR-113, production message rating behavior outside the lab, or repository-level testing. If prompt evaluation is needed later, build it as an explicitly internal harness or developer script that is not shipped to customers and does not recreate customer BYOK.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-607 - Per-attempt LLM-gateway Firestore accounting ledger

### Requirement implied by the code

> Every provider attempt made by the internal LLM gateway must asynchronously create one immutable Firestore document containing user attribution, feature, route, provider/model, token/cache units, credential source, subscription snapshot, and an estimated micro-dollar cost.

### Exact current behavior from the code

The gateway already emits operational metrics for requests, latency, failures, fallback, first-token time, and accounting delivery. In addition, when `LLM_GATEWAY_ACCOUNTING_ENABLED=true`, every provider attempt is converted into an accounting event and queued for a best-effort Firestore write to `llm_gateway_attempts`.

The stored document does **not** contain prompts, completions, raw provider bodies, headers, or credentials. It does contain the user ID and detailed model-routing/cost metadata. Documents are create-only and idempotent by attempt ID. A bounded in-memory queue and write timeout prevent Firestore trouble from failing the user's model request.

This is separate from the usage that the product actually enforces:

```text
retained usage/quota counters
  -> decide entitlement, rate limit, and displayed/account-level usage

llm_gateway_attempts documents
  -> detailed per-provider-attempt cost record
  -> no reader, billing decision, quota check, UI, report, or cleanup job in this repo
```

A repository-wide reference trace finds only the writer, its sink, documentation, and tests. No production code reads the `llm_gateway_attempts` collection after it is written.

### Choices

1. **Delete the unread attempt ledger.** Remove the Firestore collection writer, async delivery queue, accounting-event persistence configuration, IAM/runtime bindings, rate-card/config pieces used only for these documents, and exclusive tests. Keep actual quota/usage accounting and low-cardinality operational metrics.
2. **Keep it for future cost analytics.** Continue paying the storage/write and maintenance cost despite having no in-repo consumer, with a separately defined retention/access/reporting owner.

### Recommendation

`delete the unread per-attempt Firestore ledger for v1`

It does not participate in billing, quota, failover, debugging UI, or any retained user behavior. The request path is already designed to succeed when accounting delivery fails, which proves it is non-authoritative. Keeping actual usage counters and gateway metrics provides the operational evidence v1 needs without storing a user-attributed document for every provider attempt.

### Question

Should we delete `llm_gateway_attempts` and its writer for v1, while retaining real quota/usage counters and operational metrics?

### Decision

`resolved - delete the unread per-attempt Firestore accounting ledger`

Confirmed: remove the `llm_gateway_attempts` writer, detached persistence queue, accounting-delivery configuration, Firestore/IAM bindings used only by this ledger, cost-rate-card machinery used only to price these documents, and exclusive documentation/tests. Retain authoritative subscription, entitlement, usage, and quota counters; retained request/failure/latency/fallback metrics; and any billing record that a separately retained payment or quota flow actually reads.

This decision deletes only the unread persistent receipt for each provider attempt. It does not yet decide whether the separately deployed LLM gateway itself survives; that operational boundary is IR-608.

No product code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-608 - Separately deployed internal LLM gateway

### Requirement implied by the code

> Retained Python model workloads must not call their selected model providers directly. They must first cross a separately deployed, service-authenticated LLM gateway that owns provider/model route resolution, request forwarding, provider fallback, and gateway-specific telemetry.

### Exact current path

The gateway is not the realtime voice provider switch retained under IR-061. OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live use their own native session/token and transport paths. This gateway is an extra server hop for normal Chat and Python background model work:

```text
normal typed Chat
  -> local Node/Pi agent loop on the Mac
  -> Python desktop backend /v2/chat/completions
  -> internal LLM gateway /v1/messages
  -> Anthropic Sonnet

retained Python model workload
  -> Python product backend / worker
  -> internal LLM gateway OpenAI-compatible endpoint
  -> configured OpenAI / Anthropic / OpenRouter provider route
```

When production gateway mode is enabled, `get_llm(feature)` replaces the provider/model selected by the Python model profile with an `omi:auto:<feature>` gateway lane. Normal Chat similarly replaces the ordinary Anthropic client with a gateway-only Anthropic client. The gateway validates a shared service token/caller header, resolves the lane, forwards the request, applies configured provider fallback rules, and emits bounded metrics.

The operational boundary is large. Production runs the gateway as its own GKE/Helm deployment with two baseline replicas and autoscaling up to twenty, an internal GCE ingress and static address, Workload Identity/service account bindings, a shared service-token secret, readiness/liveness/startup probes, Cloud Run VPC connectivity probes, a separate deployment workflow, route/lane artifacts, and gateway-specific validation/smoke tests.

The repository already contains direct provider clients and model selection in `backend/utils/llm/model_config.py`, `clients.py`, and `providers.py`. The desktop backend already receives its Anthropic credential directly, and the product backend deployment already receives provider credentials for direct retained workloads. Therefore the gateway is not the only place capable of making these calls or keeping provider credentials off the Mac.

### What this gateway does and does not protect

- It **does** centralize route configuration, service-to-service authentication, provider failover rules, request telemetry, and independent scaling.
- It **does not** own the Mac's local agent loop, tool approval/execution, product quota, Firebase/Dodo entitlement, realtime OpenAI/Gemini switching, or user-visible Chat history.
- It is an additional availability dependency in gateway mode: if the gateway cannot serve the request, the current normal-Chat gateway client fails rather than silently becoming the direct Anthropic client.
- IR-607 deletes its unread Firestore attempt ledger, but that decision alone does not require deleting the gateway's request routing or operational metrics.

### Choices

1. **Collapse retained routing into the Python backends for v1.** Normal Chat calls Anthropic directly from the desktop backend; each separately retained product workload calls its chosen managed provider through the existing shared Python client layer. Remove the independent gateway service, GKE/Helm deployment, ingress/VPC/service-token boundary, auto-lane and route-artifact system, shadow/promotion scaffolding, separate deploy workflow, and exclusive tests/metrics. Keep ordinary timeouts/retries, product quota/usage, sanitized operational metrics, and any provider fallback explicitly retained for a real workload.
2. **Keep the independent gateway.** Preserve a separately operated model-routing service so multiple backend callers can change provider/model routes centrally and use gateway-owned failover without redeploying those callers, accepting the extra deployment, network hop, configuration plane, and incident surface.

### Recommendation

`collapse retained model routing into the Python backends for v1; delete the separately deployed gateway service`

For this first release, the independent gateway duplicates a provider-client layer the Python backends already possess while adding another production service that must be deployed, authenticated, networked, scaled, probed, and kept route-compatible. Normal Chat is now deliberately pinned to Sonnet under IR-605, customer BYOK is deleted under IR-062, and the gateway's per-attempt ledger is deleted under IR-607. Those decisions remove much of the value of a general multi-tenant routing control plane.

This recommendation does **not** delete normal Chat, retained Python AI workloads, model-provider credentials, quota/usage controls, or the OpenAI Realtime/Gemini Live switch. It changes only where retained server-side provider calls are made: directly inside the owning Python backend instead of through an extra internal gateway service.

### Question

For v1, should we delete the separately deployed LLM gateway and let each retained Python backend call its chosen managed model provider through the shared in-process client layer?

### Decision

`resolved - delete the separately deployed LLM gateway and collapse retained routing into the owning Python backends`

Confirmed: normal typed Chat will call managed Anthropic Sonnet directly from the Python desktop backend. Each separately retained product/background model workload will call its chosen managed provider through the shared in-process Python client layer. Remove the standalone `backend/llm_gateway` service; GKE/Helm release; internal ingress/static-address and VPC connectivity boundary; service-token/caller-auth plumbing; gateway mode, auto lanes, route artifacts, shadow/promotion scaffolding, circuit and transport wrappers exclusive to the extra hop; independent deployment/probe/validation workflows; gateway-only metrics/docs/tests; and IR-607's already rejected attempt ledger.

Retain the Mac's local Node/Pi agent loop and tool controls, normal Chat, selected Python AI workloads, managed provider credentials, authoritative quota/usage accounting, sanitized workload metrics, and workload-owned timeout/retry/fallback behavior. The OpenAI Realtime/Gemini Live switching and failover retained under IR-061 is a separate native voice path and is unchanged.

Removing the gateway does not silently preserve every provider/model route currently named by its generated configuration. IR-609 and later workload audits must choose one explicit direct route for each surviving Python feature and delete routes whose product workload was already rejected.

No product code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-609 - Global premium, max, and BYOK model-QoS profiles

### Requirement implied by the code

> The Python backend must maintain three complete provider/model maps for every LLM-backed feature: a cost-optimized `premium` profile, a highest-quality `max` profile, and a highest-quality `byok` profile selected when a customer supplies personal provider credentials.

### Exact current behavior

`backend/utils/llm/model_config.py` duplicates the full feature map three times. At process startup, one global `MODEL_QOS` environment value selects `premium` or `max` for every request handled by that deployment. This is **not** a per-customer paid-plan choice and is not selected from the Mac UI.

```text
backend process starts
  -> read MODEL_QOS once
  -> if unset, use premium for every user and workload
  -> if set to max, use max for every user and workload

request has a customer BYOK key
  -> replace the chosen route with the byok profile route
```

No checked-in production runtime configuration sets `MODEL_QOS`, so the Python-side selected profile defaults to `premium`. The `max` profile is available only as an unreferenced operator environment override. The `byok` profile exists only to upgrade users who supplied personal provider keys, but all customer BYOK was deleted under IR-062.

There is one further layer of indirection in the current production gateway mode: after the Python process selects a profile entry, `get_llm(feature)` routes the request to an `omi:auto:<feature>` lane and the gateway's generated override can choose a different provider/model. Therefore the profile maps can be loaded and logged without being the final production route. IR-608 deletes that gateway override layer; unless this profile system is also simplified, the dormant `premium` default would then become the direct route after the collapse.

The names are also misleading from a product perspective: a Dodo paid plan does not automatically select `max`, and `premium` is the cheaper default rather than the top plan. The profiles independently name dozens of workloads, including many whose product surfaces are already deleted or being reviewed elsewhere.

### Concrete example

For `conv_structure`, the Python profiles and current gateway override name three different route states:

```text
Python premium map    -> gpt-5.4-mini
Python max/BYOK maps  -> gpt-5.4
gateway override      -> gpt-5.6-luna
```

The process defaults to `premium`, but current gateway mode can replace that route with `gpt-5.6-luna`. No customer plan selects `max`. Maintaining the extra global profiles therefore does not give paid users a deliberate higher-quality conversation summary; it leaves multiple conflicting places that appear to own the same model decision.

Normal typed Chat is already independently pinned to Sonnet under IR-605. Realtime voice uses the separate OpenAI/Gemini selection retained under IR-061/600 and is not controlled by these profiles.

### Choices

1. **Delete the profile system.** Replace the three duplicated maps and startup `MODEL_QOS` switch with one explicit provider/model route per surviving workload. Delete the entire BYOK map and its request-time upgrade path. During the remaining audit, remove rejected workloads and choose the direct provider/model for each retained workload.
2. **Keep global premium/max profiles.** Preserve an operator-controlled whole-deployment quality/cost switch even though no checked-in production deployment selects `max`; delete only the BYOK profile.
3. **Turn profiles into customer plan tiers.** Make paid plans dynamically select different model quality. The current code does not implement this and it would create a new product, quota, testing, and cost contract rather than simplify v1.

### Recommendation

`delete the global profile system and keep one explicit provider/model route per surviving workload`

For v1, the dormant `max` map adds configuration drift without serving a current customer or deployment behavior, while the `byok` map has lost its only valid caller. A single audited route per retained workload is easier to understand, test, price, and operate. If a real workload later needs a fallback model, that fallback should be attached to that workload's proven failure mode instead of multiplying the entire product-wide map.

This does not choose or delete the remaining model workloads by itself. It removes the three-way configuration duplication so each workload can be judged once.

### Question

Should we delete the global `premium`/`max`/`byok` profile system and keep one explicit managed provider/model route for each surviving Python workload?

### Decision

`resolved - delete the global model-QoS profile system and keep one explicit route per surviving workload`

Confirmed: remove the duplicated `premium`, `max`, and `byok` maps; the global startup `MODEL_QOS` selector; customer-BYOK route upgrades; profile-name/accessor/logging machinery; and profile-only tests/docs/config. Replace them with one typed managed provider/model route for each workload that survives its own audit. Delete a workload's route when that workload is rejected rather than keeping dead feature vocabulary in a generic map.

This decision does not choose every remaining provider/model in bulk. Normal Chat remains pinned to Sonnet under IR-605, realtime voice remains separately switchable between OpenAI and Gemini under IR-061/600, and later requirements will resolve each remaining Python workload once.

No product code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-610 - GPT-based fair-use classifier and graduated transcription restriction

### Requirement implied by the code

> After a customer exceeds rolling speech soft caps, the backend must ask a large language model to judge whether their recent hosted conversation history looks like personal live use or bulk audiobook, podcast, prerecorded-media, television/movie, or commercial transcription. Repeated high abuse scores must move the account through warning, throttle, and restriction cases.

### Exact current behavior

Production enables this system. Live `/v4/listen` and fresh uploaded-audio processing meter detected speech into per-user Redis minute buckets. The bounded-plan soft triggers are currently two hours in one day, eight hours across three days, or ten hours across one week. Code defaults double those triggers for Omi's legacy unlimited plan types.

Crossing a trigger does not immediately enforce a simple product quota. Instead, at most once per twelve hours, the backend runs a GPT-5.1 classifier. It fetches up to thirty hosted conversations from the previous seven days and sends these fields to the model:

- hosted conversation ID;
- generated title and the first 200 characters of its overview;
- category, duration, source, and creation timestamp.

It does not send the raw transcript in this classifier call, but it does send private derived conversation content for an account-enforcement judgment. The model returns a misuse score and labels such as audiobook, podcast, prerecorded, television/movie, or commercial use. A score of at least `0.7`, repeated over time, progresses the stored Firestore state from `none` to `warning`, then `throttle`, then `restrict`.

The `throttle` stage stores a seven-day timestamp and tells the user that transcription quality was reduced, but a repository-wide production trace finds no throttle-stage reader that actually changes transcription quality. The `restrict` stage is real: it can impose a thirty-day restriction, turn the rolling soft caps into hard blocks, and limit Deepgram forwarding to thirty minutes per UTC day.

This has become a complete support product around the model judgment: Firestore state and immutable case events, public case-reference lookup, authenticated user status, admin list/detail/reset/override/resolve endpoints, push notifications, Redis locks/caches/meters, payment-upgrade cleanup, generated clients, Firestore indexes, and extensive sync/listen tests.

### Conflict with the retained product

The Mac's authoritative conversations and summaries are local under IR-004 and the surrounding conversation decisions. Current Mac-authored conversations are not supposed to be uploaded as the backend's durable product record. Therefore the classifier's hosted seven-day history is no longer authoritative: it can be empty or stale even while the customer is actively using local transcription.

The retained backend already has deterministic controls that do not need an AI judgment:

```text
plan transcription allowance
  -> remaining seconds checked during live transcription
  -> predictable stop/upgrade behavior when allowance is exhausted

impossible-use safety ceiling
  -> current code uses 30 audio hours inside a rolling 24-hour window
  -> catches bulk/replayed ingestion that a single live human cannot produce
```

The free-credit path currently fabricates a `1.0` abuse score and sends exhausted free users through the same case state machine. That is quota exhaustion, not model-detected abuse, and can be handled directly by the ordinary plan quota.

### Choices

1. **Delete the AI fair-use case system.** Remove the GPT classifier/route, soft-cap classification triggers, warning/throttle/restrict state machine, Firestore case state/events, public/user/admin case APIs, enforcement notifications, restrict-only Deepgram budget, payment cleanup, and exclusive Redis/config/tests/bindings. Keep the ordinary plan allowance and rehome one deterministic impossible-use hard ceiling beside quota enforcement.
2. **Keep deterministic rolling soft caps but remove GPT.** Warn or restrict every high-volume user at the same thresholds. This is simpler than AI classification but would intentionally penalize legitimate meeting-heavy users despite plans that may promise high or unlimited transcription.
3. **Keep the complete classifier and case system.** Preserve model judgment, private summary inspection, support tooling, and graduated enforcement, then redesign its evidence source because hosted conversation history is no longer authoritative.

### Recommendation

`delete the GPT fair-use classifier and graduated case system; keep transparent quota plus one deterministic impossible-use ceiling`

For v1, a hidden model should not decide whether a customer's meetings look sufficiently personal before cloud transcription continues. The current evidence source conflicts with local conversation authority, the throttle stage makes an unimplemented quality-reduction claim, and the case system duplicates plan quota with a much larger privacy, support, storage, and failure surface.

This recommendation does not create unlimited free compute. The selected Dodo plans retain explicit transcription allowances and usage accounting, and a single deterministic hard ceiling can still stop technically impossible bulk ingestion without inspecting conversation meaning.

### Question

Should we delete the GPT fair-use classifier and its warning/throttle/restrict case system, while retaining transparent plan quotas and one deterministic impossible-use hard ceiling?

### Decision

`resolved - keep fair-use protection and adapt it to the retained product architecture`

Confirmed: preserve rolling usage awareness, a conservative abuse-review step after soft triggers, graduated warning/throttle/restrict states, a user-visible explanation/appeal path, support controls, and the deterministic impossible-volume ceiling. Do not collapse all protection into the ordinary monthly quota.

This is not approval to keep the current implementation verbatim. Its hosted-conversation evidence is no longer authoritative, the `throttle` stage currently claims a quality reduction that no production reader performs, and Omi/Deepgram/on-device wording and legacy plan types must become our own Dodo-backed contract. IR-611 through IR-709 now resolve the evidence, inference, thresholds, enforcement effects, recovery, user/support surfaces, retention, and operational-override boundaries.

The fair-use branch is now closed. Its children preserve the existing product pattern while moving classification onto the Mac, keeping content evidence local, retaining content-free backend enforcement/support state, and recording the user's explicit choices where current behavior remains intentionally imperfect.

No product code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-611 - Local-conversation evidence admitted to fair-use classification

### Requirement exposed by IR-610

> To distinguish a legitimate power user from bulk prerecorded-media ingestion, the adapted fair-use classifier must receive evidence derived from the Mac's local-authoritative conversation history after rolling speech soft caps are crossed.

### Why the current input no longer works

Omi's classifier reads up to thirty hosted conversation records and sends each generated title plus the first 200 overview characters to GPT. Under the retained architecture, current Mac-authored conversations, summaries, and transcripts are authoritative in local GRDB and are not uploaded as the backend's durable product record. Keeping the existing server query would make enforcement depend on empty, incomplete, or stale history.

Recreating a permanent cloud conversation copy just for enforcement would reverse the local-authority decision. The adapted classifier therefore needs an explicit evidence contract rather than silently reintroducing cloud synchronization.

### Practical choices

1. **Send a bounded content-free evidence envelope only after a soft trigger.** The Mac derives recent session duration, speaker/turn counts, user-participation ratio, microphone-versus-system-audio proportions, repeated/uniform-session patterns, and coarse time buckets. It sends no transcript, raw audio, title, overview, names, durable local IDs, or screenshots. The backend/model can judge only whether the aggregate pattern resembles automated or bulk prerecorded ingestion and must remain conservative when ambiguous.
2. **Temporarily send the current title/overview evidence after a soft trigger.** Do not persist a hosted conversation copy, but allow the backend model to inspect up to thirty local generated titles and 200-character overviews for a more specific audiobook/podcast judgment. This exposes private derived conversation content to an enforcement model and requires explicit disclosure, strict transport/retention rules, and support-access policy.
3. **Restore hosted conversation copies for classification.** Continuously upload conversation summaries so the current classifier can remain server-owned. This conflicts with local authority and recreates cloud product-content storage solely to support enforcement.

### Recommendation

`reuse the existing bounded recent-conversation evidence pattern against local GRDB; do not recreate hosted conversation storage`

Preserve the current title/overview/category/duration/source/time recipe and conservative semantic decision instead of designing a different behavioral classifier. The change at this boundary is only where the authoritative recent-conversation data is read: local GRDB rather than hosted Firestore records. IR-612 owns the inference location.

### Question

Should the current bounded evidence recipe be assembled from local GRDB after a soft trigger, without recreating hosted conversation copies?

### Decision

`resolved at the evidence-source boundary - adapt the existing recent-conversation pattern to local authority`

Confirmed flow:

```text
backend rolling speech meter crosses a soft trigger
  -> Mac receives a fair-use review request
  -> Mac reads up to thirty recent conversations from local GRDB
  -> assemble the current bounded evidence shape locally
     (generated title, first 200 overview characters, category,
      duration, source, and time)
  -> classifier returns the conservative misuse score/type/evidence result
  -> backend remains authoritative for warning/throttle/restrict state
```

Do not recreate durable hosted conversation documents, upload raw transcripts/audio, or let an empty/stale server conversation query stand in for the Mac's real local history. The evidence is assembled only after a soft trigger and exists only for that review.

This decision establishes where the evidence comes from, not yet where model inference runs. The repository has no existing general-purpose on-device language model for this task. `AgentBridge` is a local runtime/orchestrator, but its normal model inference is managed Claude through the Python desktop backend, so using it would still send the bounded title/overview evidence off the Mac. IR-612 resolves that boundary explicitly.

No product code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-612 - Genuinely on-device versus cloud fair-use inference

### Ambiguity exposed by "run the same pattern locally"

There are two different meanings of local in the current desktop architecture:

```text
local data + local orchestration
  -> AgentBridge/Node runs on the Mac
  -> managed model request still leaves the Mac

local data + local inference
  -> an on-device model/rule engine reads the evidence
  -> conversation title/overview content never leaves the Mac
```

The codebase currently has on-device speech transcription, but no general-purpose on-device language model that can perform the existing semantic audiobook/podcast/prerecorded/commercial classification. Reusing `AgentBridge` would preserve the prompt pattern but would route the evidence to managed Sonnet; calling that fully local would be misleading.

### Choices

1. **Require genuinely on-device semantic inference.** Add and support an on-device language-model boundary capable of classifying the bounded local title/overview evidence. Only the score, coarse type, confidence, and non-content enforcement facts leave the Mac. This best matches a literal local requirement but introduces a new model/runtime, hardware/OS support matrix, download/availability behavior, and tamper/trust problem for server-side cost enforcement.
2. **Use local evidence assembly with managed cloud inference.** The Mac reads local GRDB only after a soft trigger and sends the bounded evidence to our Python backend/model for the existing semantic judgment. No hosted conversation copy is created, but derived private content leaves the Mac for inference and must be disclosed and protected.
3. **Use a content-free local rules/model fallback.** Keep everything on-device using duration, turn-taking, audio-source proportions, repetition, and other behavioral signals. This preserves privacy and broad Mac compatibility but cannot honestly identify a specific audiobook, podcast, movie, or television programme.

### Recommendation

`move the existing semantic classifier onto the Mac behind the same input/output contract`

This is the narrow relocation that satisfies the local boundary without redesigning fair-use policy: local GRDB supplies the same evidence, a genuinely local model runs the same conservative prompt/schema, and only the verdict leaves the Mac. The implementation must not call the managed `AgentBridge` path and describe it as local.

### Question

Should the existing semantic classifier run through a genuinely local model on the Mac and send only its verdict to the backend?

### Decision

`resolved after correction - move the existing classifier pattern and inference onto the Mac`

Confirmed flow:

```text
backend detects a rolling soft-cap trigger
  -> authenticated Mac runs the fair-use review locally
  -> read up to thirty local evidence records
  -> use the existing conservative prompt/recipes and strict JSON schema
  -> local model returns misuse_score, type, confidence,
     evidence, and reasoning
  -> send only the bounded verdict/enforcement facts to backend
  -> backend applies the retained graduated enforcement policy
```

Preserve the existing semantic behavior rather than inventing a replacement heuristic: the same recent seven-day/up-to-thirty-conversation window, title/overview/category/duration/source/time evidence, conservative legitimate-use rules, misuse score, coarse usage type, confidence, evidence selection, and warning/throttle/restrict decision contract. The implementation change is the execution boundary: local GRDB replaces hosted conversation queries, and a genuinely local model replaces the backend GPT call.

No raw audio, full transcript, screenshot, title, overview, local conversation identity, or classifier prompt payload leaves the Mac. The backend remains authoritative for metered cloud usage and enforcement state, and the deterministic impossible-volume ceiling remains server-side even if a local client fails or is bypassed. The repository does not currently ship the required general-purpose local semantic model, so implementation must add a local inference adapter that preserves the existing classifier input/output contract; that is relocation work, not a new product policy.

IR-613 is resolved by this local boundary: content-specific evidence remains available only in local classifier state, while the backend receives and stores only the bounded verdict plus usage/enforcement facts.

No product code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-613 - Durable storage of classifier conversation evidence

### Requirement implied by the current case schema

> After the local LLM makes a fair-use decision, the backend must persist the classifier's conversation identifiers, titles, and content-specific reasons inside its Firestore `fair_use_events` case.

### Exact difference between temporary inference and durable storage

IR-612 keeps both evidence and inference on the Mac. Sending the resulting verdict to the backend does not require copying the local input or content-specific evidence into the backend case.

The current classifier returns evidence shaped like:

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "hosted-conversation-id",
  "title": "Chapter 7 - The Journey",
  "reason": "Sequential chapter pattern across long sessions"
}
```

The current backend nests that result in a durable Firestore fair-use event because it owns the classifier today. After relocation, the Mac can retain the detailed evidence locally. Persisting its local ID/title in the backend would recreate a searchable cloud content record even though both the main conversation and classifier now remain local.

### Choices

1. **Persist only content-free decision/audit facts.** Keep account UID, usage-window totals and thresholds, model/provider and prompt version, score, coarse type, confidence, bounded non-content reason codes, previous/new stage, action, timestamps, and case reference. Hold titles/overviews only in memory for the LLM request and exclude them from logs, metrics, Firestore, notifications, and support list responses.
2. **Persist selected titles and model reasons in the case.** Give support richer evidence for appeals, accepting that private derived conversation content becomes a durable backend record with retention, deletion, access-control, and disclosure obligations.
3. **Persist opaque local references only.** Store local IDs/hashes without text so the Mac can later resolve the conversations during an appeal. This couples server cases to owner-local records and still needs explicit user-mediated evidence sharing; the backend cannot interpret the references itself.

### Recommendation

`persist only content-free decision and enforcement facts; discard title/overview evidence after the LLM response`

Support needs to know why an enforcement stage changed, but it does not need a permanent cloud index of private conversation titles. Coarse reasons such as `sequential_long_sessions`, `low_user_participation`, or `uniform_prerecorded_pattern` plus the score and usage totals are enough for operational review. If a customer appeals, they can explicitly choose what local evidence to share at that time.

### Question

After local classification finishes, should the Mac send only the content-free score, reason codes, usage facts, and enforcement recommendation to the backend?

### Decision

`resolved by IR-612 - keep classifier content evidence local and persist only content-free case facts in the backend`

Confirmed: local classifier state may retain the selected local conversation references, titles, and content-specific reasons needed to explain its own decision on that Mac. The backend fair-use event retains account UID, rolling usage and thresholds, local-classifier version, score, coarse usage type, confidence, bounded non-content reason codes, prior/new stage, action, timestamps, and case reference. It receives no title, overview, transcript, raw audio, name, local conversation ID, or content-specific reasoning text.

No code deletion is authorized yet.

## IR-614 - Meaning of the seven-day fair-use throttle stage

### Requirement claimed by the product copy

> After a second qualifying fair-use violation, transcription quality must be reduced for seven days before a later violation can enter the thirty-day restriction stage.

### Exact current behavior

The state machine progresses as follows when the classifier repeatedly scores above the retained threshold:

```text
first qualifying violation  -> warning
second qualifying violation -> throttle + throttle_until = now + 7 days
third qualifying violation  -> restrict + restrict_until = now + 30 days
```

At `throttle`, the backend sends a notification titled `Transcription Quality Reduced` and the status API says quality has been temporarily reduced. But no production route reads `throttle` or `throttle_until` to change the STT provider, model, quality, speed, allowance, or transcript delivery. Focused integration tests explicitly protect warning and throttle as notify-only stages. Only `restrict` has a real service effect through cloud-STT limiting/hard restriction.

The seven-day timestamp is also not used to normalize an expired throttle. The current code automatically moves an expired `restrict` back to `throttle`, but never automatically clears or downgrades an expired `throttle` despite telling the customer it will reset.

### Choices

1. **Keep the existing three-strike behavior and make it truthful.** Warning and throttle remain notify-only chances to correct behavior before real restriction. Present `throttle` to the customer as a final warning/under-review stage, not reduced transcription quality. Make the seven-day expiry real and return the account to `warning` when it expires without another qualifying violation.
2. **Implement a real quality throttle.** Route the account to a lower-cost/lower-quality STT provider or model for seven days. The current code has no such behavior; this would couple fair-use policy to the still-unresolved STT provider portfolio and add a new quality contract.
3. **Delete the middle stage.** Move directly from warning to restrict on the next qualifying violation. This is simpler but changes the retained three-step grace period.

### Recommendation

`keep the existing notify-only second strike, rename it user-facing as a final warning, and make its seven-day reset real`
