> Home should refresh a small set of concrete, owner-scoped questions once per day from the user's retained context, without generating on every render or leaking suggestions across accounts.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep daily personalization, but move every context read to local authority.** Preserve the once-per-day owner cache, sanitization, failure retry, static fallbacks, and editable prefill; use bounded local memory/conversation/task/goal context for transient Gemini generation.
2. **Delete AI personalization and keep static questions only.** Remove the four context reads, Gemini request, owner/day cache, and refresh lifecycle; retain the universal and two static fallback questions.
3. **Generate only after an explicit user action.** Do not run on Home appearance; add a user-triggered refresh/generate control and cache its result locally.
4. **Keep the current cloud-projection reads.** Retain backend copies of memories, conversations, tasks, and goals solely to generate Home questions, contradicting the established local-authority decisions.

### Recommendation

`keep the once-daily personalized questions, but generate them from bounded local-authoritative context`

Concrete questions make the personal assistant meaningfully more useful than a permanent generic prompt list, and the existing owner/day cache avoids repeated model work. The useful behavior does not require cloud product-data authority: the retained local stores already contain the inputs. Preserve the account-switch fence and retry semantics, send only a bounded recent/relevant context set to Gemini, keep the cache local, and remove the dead onboarding-suggestion input under IR-160.

### Question

Should Home keep generating up to two personalized questions once per day, but read their memory/conversation/task/goal context from the authoritative local stores instead of the deleted backend copies, while retaining static questions as the fallback?

### Decision

`keep once-daily personalized questions from bounded local-authoritative context`

Confirmed: retain up to two owner-scoped personalized Home questions per local calendar day, the immediate owner-keyed local cache, sanitization/deduplication/length limits, account-switch authorization fence, successful-empty daily hold, transport-failure retry, universal first question, static fallbacks, and editable Ask-bar prefill. Replace all server memory/conversation/action-item/goal reads with bounded recent/relevant reads from their authoritative local stores and send only that selected context for transient Gemini generation. Do not restore backend product-data copies for this surface. Remove the orphaned `PostOnboardingPromptSuggestions` input under IR-160.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-509 - Focused-goals strip above the Home Ask bar

### Exact current behavior from the code

At the bottom of the resting Home hub, immediately above the Ask bar, `FocusedGoalsSection` is driven by the newer cloud `DashboardIntelligenceStore` goal product.

When canonical goals with `status == focused` exist, Home shows:

```text
Focused goals  [goal title] [goal title] ... (up to 5)   All goals
```

Clicking a title fetches a rich cloud goal detail and opens a sheet containing desired outcome, why it matters, success criteria, metric progress, active workstreams, progress events, and **Work on this with Omi**. **All goals** opens a 620x540 management sheet with Current/History, Add goal, Focus/Unfocus, Pause, Mark achieved, Abandon, and focus-set replacement.

When the cloud workflow-control endpoint has returned an account generation but no goal is focused, Home instead shows **No focused goals** with **Add goal** or **Choose focus**. If workflow control is unavailable or disabled, the whole strip disappears even if the older local goal table contains goals.

The strip therefore does not read `DashboardViewModel.goals`, even though those local GRDB-backed goals are already loaded elsewhere on Dashboard. Its visibility, content, creation, focus lifecycle, detail, and error state all depend on the canonical backend system.

### Collision with settled goal decisions

IR-027 keeps one simple local goal model with stable local identity, title, optional description, and active/completed status. It explicitly deletes:

- both cloud goal authorities and normal goal API calls;
- the canonical focused/background/paused/achieved/abandoned lifecycle;
- focus ranks, focus-set replacement, account-generation/idempotency machinery;
- desired-outcome/success-criteria/metric/progress-event richness;
- AI goal generation/advice/history automation; and
- goal relationships to cloud tasks and workstreams.

IR-028 separately deletes goal-origin workstreams and **Work on this with Omi**. Consequently the current Focused Goals strip and its sheets cannot survive unchanged. The remaining Home decision is whether a simpler local active-goals summary should occupy this space.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should keep the user's most relevant goals visible near the primary Ask surface and provide a quick path to view or manage them.

### Concrete choices

1. **Adapt the strip to the retained simple local goals.** Rename it **Active goals**, show up to five active local goal titles, open the simple local goal detail/editor, and make **All goals/Add goal** use the surviving local goal UI. Remove Focus/Unfocus, replacement, rich canonical detail, workstreams, and account-generation gating.
2. **Remove goals from Home.** Keep the simple local Goals feature and goal-aware Chat/Focus context retained by IR-027, but expose goal management only on its dedicated surviving surface.
3. **Add a new local focused subset.** Reintroduce focused/background state and selection solely for Home, expanding the simple model chosen in IR-027.
4. **Keep the current cloud canonical strip.** Preserve the rejected cloud goal and workstream systems to support this UI.

### Recommendation

`keep a compact Active goals strip backed only by the simple local goal model`

Goals were retained because they shape the assistant's guidance; keeping a few visible next to Ask reinforces that purpose and gives users a direct way to correct the context. The surface does not need a second focus lifecycle. Show active local goals in their existing deterministic order, cap the strip at five, open the simple local detail/editor, and remove every canonical/workstream-only branch. When no active goal exists, a small **Add goal** path can remain without depending on workflow-control state.

### Question

Should Home keep this strip in a simplified form—**Active goals** backed by the retained local goal records, with local Open/All goals/Add goal actions—while deleting the current Focus/Unfocus, rich cloud detail, and workstream behavior?

### Decision

`remove the goals strip and goal-management sheets from Home`

Confirmed: delete `FocusedGoalsSection`, its **Focused goals / No focused goals / All goals / Add goal / Choose focus** Home presentation, and the Home-owned canonical goal management/detail/create/focus/replacement sheets and error wiring. Do not rebuild an **Active goals** strip against the simple local model. This removes the more complex Home branch while preserving the one simple local Goals feature, its surviving dedicated management surface, and its retained use as context for normal Chat and Focus under IR-027. IR-028's deletion of goal-origin workstreams and **Work on this with Omi** remains unchanged.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-510 - Home Ask bar as the canonical main-Chat composer

### Exact current behavior from the code

The pill-shaped Ask bar remains anchored at the bottom of every current Home mode. Its text is not separate dashboard state: it binds directly to `ChatProvider.draftText`, the same canonical main-Chat draft used by Home's inline Chat. Switching between the hub, Chat, and Connect therefore does not create a second draft or thread.

On the empty-history hub, clicking the bar or reaching it with keyboard focus sets `homeAskFieldFocused`. A focus observer immediately opens Home's inline Chat mode and keeps the field focused after the stage transition. This actual behavior wins over a nearby stale comment that says the hero remains visible until send. IR-500 already retained Ask/focus navigation into the same canonical Chat surface.

The text field grows from one to six visible lines. Its keyboard contract is:

```text
Return         -> send when nonblank
Shift+Return   -> insert a newline
Return while the agent is responding -> stop the current main-Chat turn
```

Whitespace-only text cannot send. A valid send opens/keeps inline Chat, records the existing send analytics event, and calls `chatProvider.sendMainDraft` with the untrimmed draft so the canonical provider owns message acceptance and clearing. It does not create a new chat session. While the agent is responding, the send button becomes a Stop button; while stopping, that control is disabled and shows progress.

The same bar also owns attachments and an empty/unfocused **Connect** action. Those are separate child decisions. This requirement covers only the shared draft, focus-to-Chat transition, text entry, send, and stop behavior.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should provide one persistent composer for the user's canonical main Chat, with standard multiline keyboard behavior and an immediate way to stop a running response.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the current canonical composer behavior.** Preserve the shared draft, focus-to-inline-Chat transition, Return/Shift+Return contract, nonblank requirement, main-draft send, and Stop replacement.
2. **Keep the hub visible while drafting.** Focus and typing remain on the orientation hub; only an accepted send transitions into inline Chat.
3. **Use a separate Home quick-question draft/session.** Decouple the hub bar from the canonical Chat composer and merge or hand off only after send.
4. **Remove the Home composer.** Make users enter Chat through another action before typing.

### Recommendation

`keep the current shared Home Ask composer and send/stop behavior`

The bar is the shortest path from Home into the single Chat authority retained by IR-500. Reusing `ChatProvider` avoids draft/session reconciliation, Return and Shift+Return follow familiar desktop behavior, and replacing Send with Stop gives the user control over a running turn. Opening inline Chat on focus also makes the destination explicit before the user submits rather than changing the surrounding surface at the moment of send.

### Question

Should Home keep this canonical Ask-bar behavior exactly: focusing it opens the shared inline Chat, Return sends nonblank text, Shift+Return adds a newline, and the Send button becomes Stop while the assistant is responding?

### Decision

`keep the current shared Home Ask composer and send/stop behavior`

Confirmed: retain the direct binding to the canonical `ChatProvider.draftText`, focus/keyboard entry into Home's shared inline Chat, one-to-six-line field growth, Return-to-send, Shift+Return newline, whitespace-only rejection, `sendMainDraft` acceptance/clearing ownership, and Send-to-Stop replacement while the main assistant is responding. Do not introduce a separate Home quick-question draft or session. Preserve the existing deferred-focus generation fence and canonical main-Chat continuity retained by IR-500.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-511 - File attachments staged from the Home Ask bar

### Exact current behavior from the code

The Home Ask bar shares `ChatProvider.pendingAttachments` with the canonical main-Chat composer rather than maintaining its own files. A paperclip opens a multi-file picker for images, PDFs, text/content, JSON, CSV, and HTML; users may also drag file URLs onto the pill. The total is capped at four attachments. Once four are staged, the paperclip is disabled.

Staged files appear in the shared `AttachmentPreviewRow` above the field and can be removed individually. Disk images up to 25 MB are read immediately for local preview; non-image bytes are loaded later. The same pending attachments remain visible when Home transitions between its hub and inline Chat because the provider owns them.

Home does not permit an attachment-only send. The Send control appears only when the trimmed text field is nonempty, and Return with an empty field does nothing. A file therefore needs an accompanying instruction such as **Summarize this** or **What is wrong in this screenshot?**. This matches the current `ChatProvider.sendMessage` acceptance boundary, which rejects empty text.

The provider currently uploads staged files through `/v2/files` and may wait up to 60 seconds before admitting the message. IR-044 has already replaced that architecture with an owner/session-scoped app-managed local attachment store: copy or materialize files before local-journal admission, pass managed local URIs and relevant image bytes to the retained agent, render local previews, retain the four-file limit, and delete automatic cloud upload and identifiers. The Home bar must use that retained local lifecycle rather than preserving its current upload call.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> The canonical Home composer should let the user stage, preview, and remove a small set of local files for the next Chat message, while requiring text that explains what the assistant should do with them.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep Home attachments and the text-required send boundary.** Preserve picker/drop, previews/removal, four-file cap, shared pending state, and require a nonblank instruction; adapt persistence to the local store already chosen in IR-044.
2. **Allow attachment-only sends.** Define a default implicit instruction and change the canonical Chat acceptance boundary so a file by itself creates a turn.
3. **Keep attachments only inside the expanded Chat surface.** Remove paperclip/drop from the hub bar but retain the same files after the user explicitly enters Chat.
4. **Remove attachments.** Reverse IR-044 for the Home/main-Chat path.

### Recommendation

`keep the current Home attachment UX and require an accompanying text instruction`

IR-044 already retains attachments as useful normal Chat behavior and supplies the durable local storage boundary. Sharing the provider's pending list avoids duplicate staging state across hub and Chat. Requiring text makes the intended task explicit and avoids inventing a generic hidden prompt for files with very different meanings. Keep the four-file cap and existing remove/preview controls while replacing only the rejected upload lifecycle beneath them.

### Question

Should Home keep its paperclip, drag-and-drop, previews, removal, and four-file limit, while continuing to require the user to type a nonblank instruction before those locally managed attachments can be sent?

### Decision

`keep the current Home attachment UX with a required text instruction`

Confirmed: retain Home paperclip selection, file-URL drag and drop, shared `ChatProvider.pendingAttachments`, local previews, individual removal, four-file cap, and continuity from hub into inline Chat. Continue requiring nonblank text before Send appears or Return submits; do not invent an attachment-only implicit prompt. Implement the already-decided IR-044 lifecycle beneath this UI: copy/materialize attachments into the owner/session-scoped app-managed local store before journal admission, pass managed local URIs and relevant image bytes to the agent, and remove `/v2/files`, upload waiting, cloud identifiers, Firestore/OpenAI Files/GCS persistence, and public thumbnails.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-512 - Connect button and connector/export tray inside Home

### Exact current behavior from the code

When the Home Ask field is empty, unfocused, and the assistant is not responding, the bar's trailing action is not Send. It becomes a **Connect** capsule. Clicking it clears Ask focus and replaces the hub/Chat panel with a third `HomeStageMode.connect` tray. Clicking again, pressing Escape, clicking outside, or using the tray's **x** returns Home to its history-aware resting surface.

The tray presents a left-to-right **sources feed Omi, Omi memory flows to destinations** product:

```text
Connect data                         Use omi memory anywhere
  Gmail                                Ask Omi
  Calendar                             Claude / Claude Code
  Files                                ChatGPT / Codex
  Notes                                OpenClaw
  Omi Device                           Hermes
  More                                 More
```

Source rows open first-party import connector sheets or the Omi website. Destination rows open hosted-MCP/export setup sheets; **Ask Omi** merely returns to the already available Chat surface. Both **More** rows open the Apps popup on its import/export sections. The tray also maintains connector/export status stores, selected-item sheets, modal hit-testing/Escape ownership, responsive panel sizing, animations, analytics, and automation actions such as `home_connect_toggle`.

### Every substantive dependency has already been rejected

- IR-047 deletes all first-party imports/exports, their Home cards/sheets, connection status, OAuth/setup, local config writers, and automation.
- IR-046 deletes the cloud Apps marketplace/platform, Apps page/popup/provider, and its navigation/automation surfaces.
- IR-015 deletes hosted/public MCP and the ChatGPT/Claude/Codex/OpenClaw/Hermes connector clients while retaining only the private on-Mac agent-tool protocol.
- IR-012/014 delete the Omi/third-party wearable pairing and device-management product.
- **Ask Omi** duplicates the retained Ask bar and inline Chat rather than providing another destination.

After those decisions, the tray has no surviving source, destination, status, or setup action. Keeping an empty Connect mode would add a third Home state solely to preserve presentation scaffolding.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should be the central place to connect external sources that teach the product about the user and external AI destinations that consume the product's memory.

That requirement has been rejected by the connector, marketplace, hosted-MCP, and device decisions above.

### Concrete choices

1. **Delete Connect from Home by dependency.** Remove the Ask-bar Connect action, `.connect` stage mode, tray/cards/sheets/status wiring, Apps popup entry points, device website shortcut, transitions, Escape/collapse branches, telemetry, and Connect automation contracts.
2. **Keep an empty placeholder.** Preserve the third Home mode for hypothetical future integrations, with no working rows.
3. **Redesign Connect around a new local feature.** Invent a different surviving source/destination product and its setup lifecycle.
4. **Reverse the earlier decisions.** Restore connectors, marketplace, hosted MCP, or device management to populate the tray.

### Recommendation

`delete the complete Home Connect branch by dependency`

There is nothing left for it to operate. Deleting it simplifies Home from hub/Chat/Connect to hub/Chat, removes a large amount of sheet, status, popup, focus, animation, automation, and responsive-layout wiring, and frees the empty Ask-bar trailing state instead of advertising rejected capabilities. Future integrations can earn a new surface when a concrete retained requirement exists.

### Question

Should we delete the entire Home **Connect** button and tray now that every import, export, Apps, hosted-MCP, and Omi-device action inside it has already been rejected?

### Decision

`delete the complete Home Connect branch by dependency`

Confirmed: remove the Ask-bar **Connect** action and empty-state action mode; `HomeStageMode.connect`; the source/destination tray and cards; connector/export/device/Apps status and selection state; import/export/catalog sheets and popup entry points; device website shortcut; Connect-specific focus, collapse, Escape, modal, animation, responsive-layout, telemetry, and automation behavior; and exclusive tests/contracts. Home simplifies to the retained hub and canonical inline Chat modes. Do not preserve an empty placeholder or invent a replacement integration surface without a new requirement.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-513 - Obsolete cloud Dashboard Intelligence coordinator on Home

### Exact current behavior from the code

Every `DashboardPage` constructs a `DashboardIntelligenceStore`. On Home appearance it installs a recommendation action handler, registers automation actions, and starts a load. On every foreground activation it loads again. It also listens for What Matters Now context-refresh and recommendation-navigation notifications and applies them to the store.

One load currently performs a substantial cloud-control sequence:

```text
GET candidate workflow control
  -> obtain account generation / rollout mode
  -> load and retry owner-scoped feedback outbox
  -> GET What Matters Now projection
  -> project recommendations and emit presentation attribution
  -> GET all canonical goals
  -> publish recommendations, goals, focus state, and errors
```

The same store owns recommendation opening/dismiss/Later/feedback/outcome behavior; candidate/task/workstream destination resolution; canonical goal create/focus/unfocus/transition/detail; goal-origin thread creation/resumption; generation/idempotency checks; error/retry UI; analytics attribution; and desktop automation actions. Its dedicated test file exercises that control plane extensively.

### No surviving Home owner remains

- IR-026 deletes What Matters Now recommendations, cloud candidates, their intervention/feedback/outcome state, and context uploads.
- IR-505 replaces Home recommendation rows with retained local Insight rows and local actions.
- IR-027 deletes canonical cloud goals and keeps only one simple local goal model.
- IR-509 deletes the goal strip and goal-management sheets from Home instead of adapting them.
- IR-028 deletes task/goal workstreams and task-attached agent continuity.
- IR-255 deletes the alternate legacy Home widgets that also branch on `accountGeneration`.

After those decisions, the Home load, foreground refresh, notification listeners, error card, action handlers, automation registration, outboxes, goal/recommendation state, and rich sheets have no user-facing responsibility.

One small helper currently lives in the same source file but does survive: `TaskNavigationRequestStore` carries an ordinary local task selected on Home into the retained Tasks page under IR-506. That helper should move into a narrow local task-navigation file; its placement must not keep the unrelated cloud coordinator alive.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home requires one coordinator that loads a cloud-ranked recommendation/goal control plane, routes its actions, retries its feedback, and exposes its failures.

That requirement has already been rejected by the task-intelligence, simple-goals, and workstream decisions.

### Concrete choices

1. **Delete the coordinator by dependency.** Remove `DashboardIntelligenceStore`, its cloud client/projection/action/outbox models, Home lifecycle/listener/error/automation wiring, canonical goal/recommendation UI, and exclusive tests; extract only the retained local task-navigation helper.
2. **Keep an unused shell.** Leave the store, load hooks, and tests compiled but stop rendering their output.
3. **Redesign it as a local dashboard coordinator.** Move unrelated local task, Insight, goal, and suggestion owners behind a new umbrella store even though they already have authoritative owners.
4. **Reverse prior decisions.** Restore cloud recommendations/canonical goals/workstreams to give the coordinator a role.

### Recommendation

`delete DashboardIntelligenceStore and its Home control-plane wiring; preserve only the local task-navigation helper separately`

The coordinator is not a neutral view model: it is the client-side owner of products already rejected in full. Keeping or repurposing it would preserve account-generation, retry, notification, automation, and error complexity without a surviving requirement and would blur the independent local owners we have deliberately retained. Extracting `TaskNavigationRequestStore` keeps IR-506's simple shortcut without retaining the cloud architecture around it.

### Question

Should we delete the entire cloud `DashboardIntelligenceStore` branch and its Home loading/error/automation wiring now that recommendations, canonical goals, and workstreams are gone, while moving the small local task-navigation helper into its own file?

### Decision

`delete DashboardIntelligenceStore and preserve only local task navigation separately`

Confirmed: remove the cloud dashboard coordinator, its client/projection/recommendation/goal/action/outbox models, load and foreground-refresh lifecycle, What Matters Now notification listeners, recommendation and canonical-goal actions, generation/idempotency state, error/retry card, attribution/telemetry, desktop automation registration, rich UI, and exclusive tests. Do not repurpose it as an umbrella over retained local owners. Extract `TaskNavigationRequestStore` into a narrow local task-navigation source so IR-506's Home-to-Tasks shortcut survives without the rejected control plane.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-514 - Static welcome inside an explicitly opened empty Home Chat

### Exact current behavior from the code

IR-500 keeps the orientation hub as Home's resting surface when the canonical Chat journal is empty. If the user explicitly enters inline Chat anyway—for example by focusing the Ask bar—`ChatMessagesView` has no timeline rows to render, so Home supplies `dashboardChatWelcome` as its empty content.

There are two mutually exclusive branches:

1. If genuine onboarding completion left a pending `chatProvider.onboardingOpener`, Home renders the personalized completion opener retained under IR-144. That branch has its own starter actions and remains separately governed by that decision.
2. Otherwise Home renders a transparent static block with the bundled 40-point `herologo.png`, **Ask omi anything**, and **Your personal AI assistant — knows you through your memories and conversations**.

The ordinary static welcome performs no fetch, model call, journal write, or persistence. It disappears naturally when the first Chat message is admitted. Because the non-onboarding empty Chat also shows IR-504's stable suggestion rows above the Ask bar, this welcome is orientation rather than the only available action.

The current identity is not shippable unchanged: the repository-wide rebrand decisions already require replacing Omi artwork/name. The subtitle is also absolute even for a truly new account that has no memories or conversations yet. The retained local assistant can use those records when present, but Home should not claim that it already knows an empty user through data that does not exist.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> An explicitly opened Chat with no messages should have a calm local empty state that explains what the assistant is for without generating a fake greeting or creating a journal turn.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep a static empty-Chat welcome, rebranded and factually scoped.** Preserve the lightweight logo/title/subtitle block, replace Omi identity, and describe the ability to use local memories/conversations when available rather than claiming they already exist.
2. **Keep the exact current claim after name/logo replacement.** Continue saying the assistant knows every user through memories and conversations, including empty accounts.
3. **Delete the ordinary welcome.** Let the stable suggestions and Ask bar occupy an otherwise empty timeline; keep only IR-144's genuine completion opener.
4. **Generate a personalized welcome.** Add a model call and/or stored Chat message for this otherwise static empty state.

### Recommendation

`keep the small static welcome, but rebrand it and make the subtitle truthful for empty accounts`

This is inexpensive local orientation and prevents the explicitly opened empty transcript from looking broken. It does not need generation or persistence. Preserve the pending onboarding opener precedence, use the new product identity, and phrase the subtitle as a capability—for example, that the assistant **can use your local memories and conversations**—rather than an unconditional claim about data a new user may not have.

### Question

Should an explicitly opened empty Home Chat keep this small static welcome, with our logo/name and truthful copy that the assistant can use local memories and conversations when available, while leaving the genuine post-onboarding opener unchanged?

### Decision

`keep the static empty-Chat welcome, rebranded and truthfully scoped`

Confirmed: preserve the transparent local logo/title/subtitle welcome whenever inline Home Chat is explicitly open with no messages and no pending onboarding opener. Replace `herologo.png` and **omi** with the new product identity, and phrase the subtitle as the ability to use authoritative local memories and conversations when available rather than claiming an empty account is already known through them. Keep IR-144's genuine completion opener as the higher-priority branch. Do not generate or journal a greeting for the ordinary empty state.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-515 - Home Capture status and start/stop control

### Exact current behavior from the code

Home's top-right header includes a **Capture** capsule with a viewfinder icon. It is a live control for the retained `ProactiveAssistantsPlugin` screen-monitoring runtime, not a decorative preference indicator.

Its status is derived from actual runtime and permission state:

```text
Screen Recording absent, stale, or ScreenCaptureKit broken -> Blocked (red)
monitoring is actually running                              -> On (green)
permission healthy but monitor stopped                     -> Off (neutral)
```

The green state deliberately follows `isCaptureMonitoring || ProactiveAssistantsPlugin.shared.isMonitoring`, not only the stored `screenAnalysisEnabled` intent. Home reconciles that live state when it appears, when the app returns to the foreground, when assistant monitoring changes, and when Screen Recording permission is lost or ScreenCaptureKit reports failure.

Clicking the capsule first reconciles runtime state, then toggles the actual monitor:

- **On -> Off:** persist screen analysis disabled, stop monitoring, and clear the live indicator after the transition.
- **Off -> On with permission:** persist screen analysis enabled and start monitoring; if start fails, roll the preference and indicator back to off.
- **Off/Blocked -> On without permission:** keep capture off and open the native Screen Recording access/System Settings path rather than pretending monitoring started.

The capsule is disabled and shows a spinner while the transition is in flight. Its help/accessibility text reports **Capture: On/Off/Blocked**. On Home, right-clicking it exposes **Open Rewind**; the shell's equivalent control on non-Home pages exposes Rewind through a hover chip. Both layouts delegate to the same `CaptureListeningLogic` and mutate the same settings/plugin owner.

### Relationship to retained product behavior

IR-029/030/033/034/035 retain local Focus history/judgment, automatic memory extraction, periodic Insights, and grounded Live Suggestions. IR-148 retains proactive screen monitoring after genuine onboarding completion, while global Skip can leave it off. Those features need a truthful visible way to see, stop, restart, and repair capture after onboarding.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should expose whether retained screen monitoring is actually running and let the user start or stop it immediately, with native permission repair when capture is blocked.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the Home Capture control and current live-state semantics.** Preserve On/Off/Blocked, start/stop, failure rollback, permission repair, in-flight feedback, and the Rewind shortcut.
2. **Make Capture status read-only on Home.** Show live state but require Settings or another shell surface to change it.
3. **Remove Capture from Home.** Manage screen monitoring only from Settings/status menu or non-Home pages.
4. **Remove the off-switch.** Always restore monitoring when retained features want it, leaving only permission repair.

### Recommendation

`keep the Home Capture control with its current live-state and permission-safe behavior`

This is the user's clearest ongoing consent and truth surface for a sensitive retained capability. It correctly distinguishes stored intent from a running monitor, fails closed when permission is absent, rolls back failed starts, and offers immediate stop. The shared logic already prevents the Home and shell copies from implementing different behavior; whether the two layouts can later reuse one view is an implementation cleanup, not a reason to remove the Home control.

### Question

Should Home keep the **Capture** capsule exactly as a live On/Off/Blocked control for retained screen monitoring, including safe start/stop, permission repair, failure rollback, and its Rewind shortcut?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep the Home Capture control unchanged`

Confirmed: retain Home's **Capture** capsule as the live On/Off/Blocked control for the proactive screen-monitoring runtime. Keep immediate start/stop, native Screen Recording permission repair, failed-start rollback, in-flight feedback, runtime-state reconciliation, and the Home context-menu shortcut to Rewind. The indicator must continue following the actual monitor rather than merely the saved preference.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-516 - Home Listening status and start/stop control

### Exact current behavior from the code

Beside Capture, Home shows a **Listening** capsule. Its main clickable area owns the retained transcription session:

```text
appState.isTranscribing = false  -> neutral mic icon; Listening is Off
appState.isTranscribing = true   -> green waveform icon; Listening is On
terminal cloud-STT failure       -> red warning; Transcription unavailable / Blocked
```

Clicking the main area derives the requested action from the live `appState.isTranscribing` value, not only the saved `transcriptionEnabled` preference:

- **Off -> On:** if Microphone permission is absent, request it and do not pretend listening started. Otherwise persist enabled intent and post the shared event that calls `appState.startTranscription()`.
- **On -> Off:** persist disabled intent and post the shared event that calls `appState.stopTranscription()`.
- The control is temporarily disabled and replaces its icon with a spinner for 0.3 seconds after an admitted toggle.

The same shared logic drives the persistent top-bar copy on non-Home pages, so both surfaces mutate the same local `AssistantSettings` and `AppState` owner.

### What green **Listening** actually means

Green does **not always mean the microphone and System Audio are currently recording**. It means the broader transcription session is armed:

- In **Always** mode, an armed session captures continuously.
- In **Meetings only** mode, `isTranscribing` remains true and Home stays green while the app waits. Outside a detected call, both audio inputs are off. They start only when `MeetingDetector` identifies a call.
- Home reveals **Meetings only** or **In meeting** as a small second line only while the pointer is hovering over the capsule. At rest, both states simply look like green **Listening**.

That makes the resting label ambiguous in the privacy-sensitive case: a person can reasonably read green **Listening** as “audio is being captured now,” when it may actually mean “the meeting detector is armed, but no audio is being captured.”

### What **Transcription unavailable** means

The red state is set when the retained cloud `/v4/listen` engine reports a terminal `stt_failed` status. Audio may still be written into the crash-safe local WAL while the transport tries to recover, so this state reports that live speech-to-text is unavailable, not necessarily that all audio acquisition has stopped. A later backend `ready` event clears it; explicitly stopping/resetting the session also clears it.

The red capsule is still clickable. If the session remains armed, clicking it stops and resets that session. It is not a separate repair button and it does not diagnose the underlying service failure.

### Relationship to settled requirements

IR-017 retains microphone plus System Audio input. IR-018 retains automatic meeting-gated listening. IR-019 retains local Parakeet with the cloud engine as a narrow fallback, and IR-143 retains the explicit Meetings-only versus Always choice. This requirement is therefore about Home's truthful status and immediate start/stop authority, not whether those underlying capture modes survive.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should expose whether transcription is off, armed and waiting for a meeting, actively capturing audio, or unable to produce live text, and should let the user start or stop the retained transcription session immediately.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the control but make its resting state truthful.** Preserve immediate start/stop, permission handling, error visibility, and the shared runtime owner. At rest, visibly distinguish **Off**, **Waiting for meeting**, **Listening/recording**, and **Transcription unavailable** instead of using the same green **Listening** label for both waiting and active audio capture.
2. **Keep the exact current collapsed status.** Continue showing green **Listening** whenever the session is armed; reveal **Meetings only** versus **In meeting** only on hover.
3. **Make Listening read-only on Home.** Show status here, but require Settings or another shell surface to start and stop it.
4. **Remove Listening from Home.** Manage transcription only through Settings, the menu bar, or non-Home pages.

### Recommendation

`keep immediate start/stop on Home, but make waiting versus active capture visible without hover`

The control is the user's clearest ongoing consent surface for retained audio capture and should remain directly actionable. The implementation already has the exact state needed to be truthful: `isTranscribing`, `isAwaitingMeeting`, and `transcriptionServiceError`. Exposing that distinction at rest avoids suggesting that a waiting session is currently recording, while preserving all retained transcription behavior. The separate hover mode-switch action will be challenged next; it is not decided by this status-label recommendation.

### Question

Should Home keep the main **Listening** start/stop control, but visibly say **Waiting for meeting** when it is armed without recording and reserve green **Listening** for active audio capture, while retaining **Off** and **Transcription unavailable** states?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep the Home Listening status exactly as it is`

Confirmed: retain the current collapsed status semantics and copy. Whenever the broader transcription session is armed, Home may show the green **Listening** state even while Meetings-only mode is waiting with both microphone and System Audio capture stopped. Continue revealing **Meetings only** versus **In meeting** only on hover. Keep the neutral off state, red **Transcription unavailable** override, immediate main-area start/stop, Microphone permission request, shared local owner, and current transition feedback unchanged.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-517 - Home's hover-only Meetings-only / Always listening-mode switch

### Exact current behavior from the code

Hovering over Home's **Listening** capsule changes it from one control into two adjacent click targets:

```text
main area                         -> start or stop the transcription session
small person icon on the right   -> change the audio-capture mode
```

The hover state also reveals the current mode as a small second line:

```text
Meetings-only mode, no call detected  -> Meetings only + two-person icon
Meetings-only mode, call detected     -> In meeting + two-person icon
Always mode                           -> Always + one-person icon
hidden/debug Never mode               -> Mic only + one-person icon
```

Clicking the small icon is an immediate two-way toggle:

- **Meetings only -> Always:** store `.always` locally and, if listening is armed, reconcile capture immediately. A session that was waiting with both inputs off therefore starts microphone and System Audio capture without another start click or confirmation.
- **Always -> Meetings only:** store `.onlyDuringMeetings` locally and immediately apply the meeting gate. If no meeting is detected, active audio capture stops while the broader listening session stays armed.

The choice is local `UserDefaults`/`AssistantSettings` state and posts `.systemAudioCaptureModeDidChange`, which `AppState` observes to reconfigure the running session. It does not stop listening, create a new conversation boundary by itself, or synchronize the preference to the backend.

The button is visually hidden until hover and uses only `person.fill` / `person.2.fill`; its tooltip says what the next click will do. There is no menu, written confirmation, or warning before switching into continuous capture. The small mode button also remains independently clickable while the main start/stop area is showing its short transition spinner.

If the hidden debug `.never` value reaches this control, Home displays **Mic only**, but the next click changes it to Meetings-only. The Home toggle cannot intentionally select Mic-only.

### Relationship to settled requirements

IR-018 retains meeting-gated listening, and IR-143 retains the explicit onboarding choice between Meetings-only and Always. Those decisions require both modes to exist, but they do not require Home to expose them as a hidden one-click toggle. Settings remains another place where the current mode can be selected.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> From Home, a user should be able to change an armed transcription session between automatic meeting-gated capture and continuous capture without stopping and restarting listening.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep mode switching on Home, but make the choice explicit.** Retain live reconfiguration, but replace the hover-only one-click icon with a clearly named selector/menu showing **Meetings only** and **Always** before the user chooses. Do not require a second confirmation after that explicit choice.
2. **Keep the exact current hover-only toggle.** Preserve the compact person icon and immediate one-click switch, including immediate continuous capture when moving from a waiting session to Always.
3. **Make the mode read-only on Home.** Show the current mode in the Listening capsule but require Settings to change it.
4. **Remove mode information and switching from Home.** Leave only start/stop here and manage mode entirely in Settings.

### Recommendation

`keep live mode switching on Home, but present it as an explicit named choice`

The ability to switch without restarting is useful and is already safely owned by one local setting plus a live reconciliation path. The risky part is presentation: a tiny person icon is not a clear consent action for starting continuous microphone and system-audio capture. A short named selector preserves the convenience while making the consequence understandable before the click. This does not change the two retained modes, their meeting detector, or the user's IR-516 decision to keep the main Listening status unchanged.

### Question

Should Home keep the live Meetings-only/Always switch, but show those two names in a clear selector before changing modes, instead of immediately starting continuous capture from one click on the small person icon?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep live Home mode switching, presented as an explicit named choice`

Confirmed: retain the ability to change an armed transcription session between **Meetings only** and **Always** directly from Home without stopping or restarting listening. Replace the hover-only one-click person icon with a clear selector that names both choices before applying one. A deliberate selection may reconfigure the active session immediately; no additional confirmation step is required. Keep the setting local and continue using the shared `AssistantSettings` notification/reconciliation path.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-518 - Responsive single-column Home stage and readable width caps

### Exact current behavior from the code

The redesigned Home surface measures all available space with a `GeometryReader` and lays the current hub or Chat surface into one centered vertical stage. It does not use a fixed desktop canvas or horizontal scrolling.

Horizontal sizing is calculated from the current window width:

```text
side inset             = 6% of width, clamped to 30...96 points
general stage content  = remaining width, capped at 1,360 points
wide panel content     = capped at 1,280 points
Chat/message column    = capped at 900 points
Home Ask bar           = clamped to available content width
```

This means a large window does not stretch Chat bubbles and controls across the entire display, while a narrow window reduces the content width instead of preserving a minimum that would overflow horizontally. The Ask bar's special empty-versus-typed width behavior is separate and will be challenged next.

The vertical layout changes by stage:

- **Hub:** 74 points of top breathing room and 26 points at the bottom. Flexible spacers center the greeting/knows list in the remaining area while the retained bottom surfaces and Ask bar stay together near the bottom.
- **Chat:** no extra stage-top padding. The timeline takes all remaining height; empty-chat suggestions, Ask bar, and any Chat error sit beneath it.
- **Connect:** currently uses its own smaller top padding, but IR-512 already deletes the entire Connect branch, so that third layout is not a surviving requirement.

The stage fills the available Home area over a neutral dark gradient. Hub/Chat transitions animate with a gated spring so the outgoing hub moves upward and Chat rises in. Animation details are presentation, not a second data or navigation state.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should remain usable across supported Mac window sizes while keeping the Chat timeline and primary controls at a readable centered width on large displays.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the responsive single-column stage and current width caps.** Preserve proportional/clamped side insets, a 1,360-point maximum stage, a 900-point Chat column, and shrink-to-fit behavior. Remove only Connect-specific geometry by dependency on IR-512.
2. **Use the full available width.** Let hub, Chat, and the Ask bar stretch edge to edge on large windows.
3. **Use one fixed canvas size.** Keep the same content dimensions regardless of window size, accepting clipping or empty outer space.
4. **Create separate compact and regular Home layouts.** Add a breakpoint and maintain two substantially different arrangements.

### Recommendation

`keep the responsive single-column stage and readable width caps`

The existing geometry is small, deterministic, and handles both narrow and very wide windows without a second layout system. The 900-point Chat cap protects reading length, while the 30...96-point side inset and shrink-to-fit calculation prevent horizontal overflow. A separate compact design is unnecessary unless real testing finds a layout that this continuous sizing cannot handle. Connect-only constants and transitions should disappear when the already-rejected Connect branch is removed.

### Question

Should Home keep this one responsive centered layout—shrinking with narrow windows while capping the overall stage at 1,360 points and Chat at 900 points—instead of maintaining separate compact and large-screen designs?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep the responsive single-column Home stage and current readable width caps`

Confirmed: retain one continuously responsive centered Home layout. Keep the proportional side inset clamped to 30...96 points, the 1,360-point maximum general stage width, the 900-point maximum Chat/message-column width, and shrink-to-fit behavior for narrow windows. Do not add separate compact and regular Home implementations. Remove Connect-only geometry by dependency on IR-512, while preserving the surviving hub and Chat layout behavior.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-519 - Compact hub Ask bar and draft-measured width expansion

### Exact current behavior from the code

The retained Home Ask composer has different width rules depending on which Home stage is visible.

In Chat, its width is simple and stable:

```text
Chat Ask bar width = min(900 points, available responsive content width)
```

This aligns the composer's left and right edges with the Chat message column.

On the resting hub, the empty composer is more compact:

```text
empty hub draft -> min(560 points, available width)
```

If a non-empty draft exists while the hub is visible, Home measures that draft with a 15-point system font, adds a hard-coded 210 points for buttons/padding, and grows the bar between 560 and 980 points, still clamped to the responsive available width.

Normal pointer/keyboard use makes the measured-text branch largely incidental: focusing the hub composer immediately opens Chat, where the bar switches to the stable 900-point Chat width before normal typing continues. A non-empty hub draft can still occur when a draft is preserved while an empty Chat is collapsed back to the hub, or through programmatic state changes. In that edge case, different draft lengths visibly resize the resting bar.

A source-inspection test currently protects the exact text-measurement implementation, but that is an implementation tripwire rather than evidence that users require draft-length-dependent resizing.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> The resting hub should use a visually compact Ask entry point, then give the composer a stable readable width aligned with the message timeline once Chat opens.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep two stable widths based only on Home mode.** Use the compact 560-point/clamped width on the hub and the 900-point/clamped width in Chat. Preserve draft text, but do not resize the hub based on character count.
2. **Keep the exact draft-measured hub expansion.** Continue measuring preserved/programmatic hub drafts and resizing the bar from 560 up to 980 points.
3. **Use the Chat width everywhere.** Keep the composer at the 900-point/clamped column width on both the hub and Chat.
4. **Let the composer fill all stage content.** Remove its separate readable-width caps.

### Recommendation

`keep a compact hub composer and a stable full Chat composer; delete draft-text measurement`

The useful design distinction is hub versus Chat, not short text versus long text. Two mode-owned widths are predictable, preserve the compact resting composition, and keep Chat aligned. Measuring one-line text plus a guessed 210-point chrome allowance only affects unusual hub-with-draft states and introduces movement without adding capacity—the actual field already supports the text. The responsive clamping retained under IR-518 still protects narrow windows.

### Question

Should Home keep a compact Ask bar on the resting hub and a wider Ask bar aligned with Chat after it opens, but stop resizing the hub bar based on how many characters happen to be in a preserved draft?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep the Home Ask-bar width behavior exactly as it is`

Confirmed: retain the compact 560-point/clamped empty hub width, the draft-measured hub expansion up to 980 points using the current text measurement plus chrome allowance, and the stable 900-point/clamped Chat width. Preserve responsive shrink-to-fit behavior and allow preserved or programmatically supplied hub drafts to resize the resting composer according to their measured character width.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-520 - Reduced-motion-aware Hub / Chat stage transitions

### Exact current behavior from the code

Home changes between its retained empty-history hub and inline Chat using one spring configuration:

```text
response: 0.46 seconds
damping fraction: 0.86
```

The transition is directional rather than a simple cross-fade:

- When leaving the hub, the hub moves about 54 points upward, scales to 98%, and fades out.
- When Chat enters, it begins about 54 points below, at 98% scale and transparent, then rises into place.
- Returning to the hub uses the paired reverse-style transitions.
- The hub headline and suggestion rows have smaller fade/vertical offsets so they do not pop independently from the stage.

The motion wraps both the state mutation (`OmiMotion.withGated`) and SwiftUI's value animation (`.omiAnimation`). Those shared helpers read macOS `accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`; when the user enables **Reduce motion**, they return no animation and the same state change occurs immediately.

This movement does not delay Chat restoration, sending, focus ownership, or persistence. It only presents the already-decided stage change. The separate Connect-from-top transition has no surviving requirement because IR-512 deletes Home Connect.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Moving between the empty-history Home hub and the canonical Chat surface should preserve visual continuity, while honoring the user's macOS Reduce Motion setting.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the current reduced-motion-aware Hub/Chat transition.** Preserve the gated spring, paired vertical/fade/scale movement, and immediate no-motion fallback. Delete only Connect-specific transition code by dependency.
2. **Use only a reduced-motion-aware cross-fade.** Remove vertical and scale movement while keeping a brief opacity transition for users who permit motion.
3. **Remove Home stage animation.** Switch immediately for every user, regardless of system preference.
4. **Use raw animation without accessibility gating.** Preserve movement even when macOS Reduce Motion is enabled.

### Recommendation

`keep the current gated Hub/Chat transition and its immediate reduced-motion fallback`

The transition is short, locally owned, and already uses the repository's shared accessibility boundary. It helps explain that the hub is yielding to the continuous Chat surface without becoming a navigation or data dependency. Removing it would save little code, while bypassing the existing reduced-motion gate would be a regression. Connect-only movement should disappear with the rejected branch.

### Question

Should Home keep the current short spring transition between the hub and Chat, while continuing to switch instantly whenever the user has enabled macOS **Reduce motion**?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep the current reduced-motion-aware Hub / Chat transition`

Confirmed: retain the existing gated spring and paired vertical/fade/scale movement between the empty-history hub and canonical Chat. Continue honoring macOS **Reduce motion** by performing the same stage change immediately with no animation. Remove only Connect-specific movement by dependency on IR-512; do not make motion part of Chat restoration, focus, sending, or persistence.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-521 - Home's neutral dark canvas and private color palette

### Exact current behavior from the code

The redesigned Home always renders on a dark neutral canvas. `HomeCanvasBackground` draws a subtle top-to-bottom gradient:

```text
top     RGB approximately 14, 15, 17
bottom  RGB approximately 10, 11, 12
```

The outer Home surface also supplies an almost-black `HomePalette.paper` fallback. There is no image, live wallpaper, memory visualization, transparency, or data-dependent color in this background.

Home then defines a private `HomePalette` inside `DashboardPage.swift` for its panels, tiles, text levels, hairlines, green status/action color, and cool-grey glow. These values are close to—but not the same symbols as—the app-wide `OmiColors` and `SBTheme` dark tokens. As a result, Home owns a second hard-coded dark design system that surviving Home components must reference directly.

### Dark-only boundary

This is not Home independently refusing to follow a supported Light Mode. The main desktop window forces `.dark`, `SBThemeManager` is explicitly dark-only, and the shared `OmiColors` palette is documented as dark. Light values still exist in `SBTheme`, but the application does not expose them as a selectable mode.

The Home palette is neutral rather than purple and therefore follows the repository's current no-purple brand boundary. Its green is used for success/live status and some primary Home emphasis; keeping or narrowing those individual accents is separate from whether the canvas remains dark.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Home should use the desktop product's neutral dark appearance and provide a calm, non-data-dependent backdrop for the hub and Chat.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the current dark visual result, but consolidate its tokens into the shared app theme.** Preserve the neutral gradient and existing contrast. Promote any genuinely distinct Home tokens into the shared theme or map them to equivalent shared tokens, then delete the private parallel palette.
2. **Keep the exact private `HomePalette`.** Continue maintaining separate hard-coded Home colors alongside `OmiColors` and `SBTheme`.
3. **Use one flat shared background.** Remove Home's subtle gradient and use the ordinary app background token everywhere.
4. **Add adaptive Light Mode to Home.** Make Home react to macOS appearance even though the surrounding main window remains dark-only.

### Recommendation

`keep the neutral dark Home appearance, but do not preserve a second private design system as a product requirement`

The dark canvas is consistent with the rest of the shipping desktop and keeps the content visually calm. The duplicate palette is implementation ownership, not user-visible product behavior. Preserving the current visual values through shared tokens keeps the accepted look while preventing Home and the rest of the window from drifting independently. Adding Home-only Light Mode would create a mismatched window and belongs only in an app-wide theme decision.

### Question

Should Home keep its current neutral dark appearance, but use the shared desktop theme as the color authority instead of permanently maintaining a separate hard-coded `HomePalette`?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep Home's neutral dark appearance and consolidate its colors into the shared desktop theme`

Confirmed: preserve the current calm, neutral dark Home canvas, subtle gradient, contrast hierarchy, and no-purple boundary. Do not add a Home-only Light Mode. Treat the private hard-coded `HomePalette` as implementation duplication rather than a product requirement: map surviving Home components to shared theme tokens or promote genuinely distinct accepted values into that shared authority, then remove the parallel palette without intentionally changing the approved visual result.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-522 - Local desktop-automation controls for the surviving Home workflow

### Exact current behavior from the code

The desktop automation bridge exposes five Home-specific actions. They are not customer-facing commands and do not exist as a remote production API. `DesktopAutomationLaunchOptions` permits the bridge only in local-automation builds; published preview/production builds fail the build-capability check even if their environment is contaminated. The local bridge also uses a per-run token written to an owner-only file.

Current Home actions are:

```text
home_open_chat       -> post event -> DashboardPage.openHomeChat()
home_connect_toggle  -> post event -> DashboardPage.toggleHomeConnectPanel()
home_close_panel     -> post event -> DashboardPage.collapseHomeStagePanel()
home_ask(query)      -> validate non-empty -> same prefill/open/send path as Home
home_attach(path)    -> validate existing path -> same ChatAttachment/add path as Home
```

The bridge does not maintain an alternate Home model. `DashboardPage` observes the events and calls the same private functions used by the on-screen Ask bar, Escape/collapse behavior, and attachment controls. The automation snapshot also reports `homeMode` so a harness can observe whether the redesigned stage is on `hub`, `chat`, or `connect`, and reports whether the legacy design is selected.

### Consequences of settled deletions

- IR-512 deletes the complete Home Connect branch, so `home_connect_toggle`, `.homeStageToggleConnect`, the `connect` snapshot value, and Connect-specific documentation/tests must also be deleted.
- IR-255 deletes the legacy Home implementation, so `usesLegacyHomeDesign` and the guards that silently ignore automation in legacy mode no longer represent a surviving Home choice.
- The retained Home workflow still has meaningful UI paths to exercise: opening empty Chat, collapsing it to the empty-history hub, sending through the canonical composer, and staging attachments under IR-511.

`home_ask` currently acknowledges that the query was posted; it does not wait for a model response or prove that the turn succeeded. `home_attach` proves the filesystem path exists before posting, but the canonical attachment path remains responsible for type/limit admission. Higher-level E2E checks must observe the resulting state rather than treat the immediate bridge response as completion proof.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> Local desktop test harnesses and coding agents should be able to drive the real surviving Home Chat entry, send, collapse, and attachment paths without maintaining fragile cursor coordinates or a second implementation.

### Concrete choices

1. **Keep the surviving local automation seam and delete rejected branches.** Retain `home_open_chat`, `home_close_panel`, `home_ask`, `home_attach`, and observable `hub`/`chat` mode. Delete Connect and legacy-Home actions/state by dependency.
2. **Delete all Home-specific automation.** Require every Home E2E run to use pointer/keyboard automation even when the behavior under test is Chat admission rather than hit-testing.
3. **Keep only direct state mutation.** Let the bridge change `ChatProvider`/Home state without routing through the production UI functions.
4. **Expose Home automation in production builds.** Turn the local harness into an externally reachable customer runtime API.

### Recommendation

`keep the local production-path automation seam, narrowed to retained Home behavior`

These commands provide controllable seams for real Home behavior and avoid pixel-coordinate coupling while still entering through the same production functions. The build capability and token boundary keep them out of published runtime. Direct state mutation would make tests less representative, while deleting the seam would push tests toward brittle clicking. Remove every action, mode value, observer, and test that exists only for the already-rejected Connect or legacy Home branches.

### Question

Should we retain local test-only automation for **open Chat**, **close to the resting hub**, **ask**, and **attach**, while deleting the rejected Connect command and legacy-Home automation state?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`keep local Home automation narrowed to the retained Chat workflow`

Confirmed: retain local-build, token-protected automation for opening Home Chat, collapsing an empty-history Chat to its resting hub, sending through the canonical Home Ask path, staging an attachment through canonical admission, and observing `hub`/`chat` mode. Delete the Connect command/event/mode and legacy-Home state/guards by dependency on IR-512 and IR-255. Keep the bridge routed through the same production functions as the UI; do not replace it with direct provider-state mutation or expose it in published builds.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-523 - Home startup and foreground refresh after rejected dashboard features are removed

### Exact current behavior from the code

Home-related loading is currently spread across three layers.

**Process/startup warmup:**

```text
immediate database warmup
  -> TasksStore.loadDashboardTasks()             [local retained task snapshot]
  -> DashboardViewModel.loadCachedDashboardData() [local goals only]

deferred dashboard network warmup
  -> DashboardViewModel.loadDashboardData()
       -> GET scores
       -> refresh dashboard tasks from server
       -> GET goals + sync them into local SQLite
```

**When Home appears:**

- reconcile Capture runtime state;
- restore/choose hub versus Chat and consume pending Chat navigation;
- load/register the cloud `DashboardIntelligenceStore`;
- refresh `HomeStatusStore` connector/export/count/device state;
- refresh once-daily personalized Home questions.

**Whenever the app becomes active while Home is mounted:**

- refresh goals through a 30-second debounce;
- reload cloud dashboard intelligence;
- re-check permissions and reconcile Capture;
- refresh Home connector/export/count/device state through its activation cooldown;
- refresh personalized Home questions through their own owner/day gate.

### What prior decisions removed

- IR-509 deletes Home's goals strip and goal sheets. The local Goals feature remains in its own surfaces, but Home no longer needs to load, mutate, or foreground-refresh goals.
- IR-513 deletes `DashboardIntelligenceStore`, its load/foreground lifecycle, automation, and listeners.
- IR-512 deletes Home Connect and its connector/export/device presentation.
- IR-255 deletes the legacy dashboard widgets that consume scores, goal counts, and the old goal/task mutation methods.

The remaining redesigned Home still needs `TasksStore` data for IR-503/504/506's task count and typed task rows. It also needs IR-508's once-daily personalized questions, Chat restoration/navigation, and the Capture/permission truth retained under IR-515. Those owners already have narrower APIs and gates.

### Ownership cleanup implied by the decisions

`DashboardViewModel` currently exists mainly as an umbrella over Tasks, scores, and goals. Once legacy widgets and Home goals disappear, Home can observe `TasksStore.shared` directly and startup can call the TasksStore's local/network refresh methods directly. The score/goal fields, APIs, mutation methods, cached-goal warmup, and `goalAutoCreated` subscription then have no Home requirement.

`HomeStatusStore` currently combines an `ImportConnectorStatusStore` with screenshot/conversation/memory/task counts, Omi-device history, export status, cooldowns, database-ready handling, and refresh cancellation. Connect deletion removes Home's consumers of those projections. Onboarding and Apps still need the underlying import-connector status owner; it should be owned/injected directly rather than preserving the larger Home wrapper solely as a container.

### Requirement materialized by the surviving behavior

> Home should warm and refresh only the authoritative data it still displays, while keeping task rows, once-daily local questions, Chat restoration, and capture/permission status current.

### Concrete choices

1. **Narrow startup and activation work to surviving owners.** Load/refresh Tasks through `TasksStore`, questions through `HomeSuggestionsStore`, and capture/permissions through `AppState`/the capture owner. Keep Chat's existing restoration. Delete Home score/goal/intelligence/status-wrapper work and extract the connector-status owner for Onboarding/Apps.
2. **Keep all current dashboard refreshes in the background.** Continue fetching scores, goals, intelligence, connector/export metrics, counts, and device history even though Home no longer displays them.
3. **Remove all Home refresh behavior.** Rely only on whatever stale values happen to have been loaded by other pages.
4. **Create a new all-purpose Home coordinator.** Move every surviving and rejected load behind another broad umbrella object.

### Recommendation

`narrow Home lifecycle work to Tasks, local questions, Chat restoration, and capture/permission truth`

This follows the accepted ownership boundaries and removes network/database work with no remaining Home consumer. Direct stores already provide caching, session scope, and refresh gates, so another coordinator would recreate the umbrella we chose to delete. The underlying connector-status store survives for Onboarding and Apps, but its ownership should no longer force Home knowledge counts, export status, or device-history refreshes to run.

### Question

After deleting Home goals, Connect, legacy widgets, and cloud dashboard intelligence, should Home stop loading their scores/goals/metrics and refresh only the retained Tasks, once-daily local questions, Chat state, and capture/permission status?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`narrow Home startup and foreground work to surviving data owners`

Confirmed: Home and startup should load/refresh only retained Tasks through `TasksStore`, owner-scoped once-daily questions through `HomeSuggestionsStore`, canonical Chat restoration/navigation through `ChatProvider`, and capture/permission truth through `AppState` and the capture owner. Remove Home score, goal, cloud-intelligence, connector/export/count/device-history loads and their foreground observers. Remove the broad `DashboardViewModel` once only task observation/refresh has moved to `TasksStore`. Preserve the underlying import-connector status owner for Onboarding and Apps through direct ownership/injection rather than retaining unused Home projections.

IR-160 independently closes the obsolete **Try asking** popup and stored onboarding-suggestion readers still present in Home lifecycle code; they are deleted by that settled decision and are not a new Home requirement.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-524 - Unreachable standalone Chat page beside Home's canonical Chat

### Exact current behavior from the code

The main shell still defines a distinct `SidebarNavItem.chat = 2` and a `pages` switch branch that constructs `ChatPage`. That page is a separate, roughly thousand-line SwiftUI renderer with its own:

- header and Home-return button;
- selected Chat-app picker;
- multi-chat/default-session controls;
- timeline composition and loading behavior;
- citations and conversation-detail sheet state;
- structured and legacy error presentation;
- composer/attachments/send/stop wiring;
- browser-extension and Claude-auth sheets;
- upgrade alert and loading overlay; and
- previews/screenshot-export registrations.

It observes the same shared `ChatProvider`, so it is not a second message database. It is nevertheless a second large UI implementation over that owner, with independent presentation state and behavior that must be kept aligned with Home's retained Chat surface.

### Current reachability

No customer-visible navigation lists the Chat item:

- `SidebarNavItem.mainItems` excludes `.chat` in both the old sidebar model and current primary navigation derivation.
- `DesktopTopBar` has no Chat pill/menu item.
- the global Open-Omi shortcut, notch Ask action, `.navigateToChat`, and **Continue in Omi** all route to Home and open its inline canonical Chat under IR-500.
- no production source assigns `SidebarNavItem.chat.rawValue` directly.

The remaining entry points are developer/accidental surfaces:

```text
desktop automation target "chat"  -> raw page index 2
generic navigateToSidebarItem(2)   -> raw page index 2
ViewExporter / SwiftUI previews    -> direct ChatPage construction
```

Therefore a normal customer cannot deliberately enter the standalone page, while automation can test a page customers do not use.

### Relationship to retained Chat

IR-500 explicitly retains Home as the default host for the one canonical Chat timeline, including external entry routes. IR-510/511 retain Home's send/stop and attachment behavior. Deleting `ChatPage` must not delete `ChatProvider`, shared timeline/message components, the Home composer, the floating/notch view over the same provider, citation behavior still used by Home, or any app/session capability with another proven reachable surface.

Any code that currently exists only inside `ChatPage`—for example a particular multi-chat or Chat-app selection UI—does not become implicitly approved by deleting the page. Before removal, trace whether that capability has another reachable owner; preserve or relocate it only if an already-settled requirement requires it.

### Requirement materialized by this code

> The desktop must maintain a second full-page Chat renderer that customers cannot navigate to, so automation and screenshot previews can open it alongside Chat's canonical Home presentation.

### Concrete choices

1. **Delete the unreachable standalone Chat page.** Remove `ChatPage`, page index 2 routing, its hidden enum destination, exclusive state/views/tests/previews, and raw-index entry. Route the semantic automation target **chat** through the retained `.navigateToChat` Home path instead.
2. **Restore Chat as a visible destination.** Add it to the top navigation and maintain both full-page Chat and Home Chat as customer choices over one provider.
3. **Keep it automation-only.** Continue compiling and adapting the duplicate renderer even though E2E exercises a non-customer surface.
4. **Replace Home Chat with `ChatPage`.** Delete the retained hub/inline presentation and return to a dedicated Chat destination, reversing IR-500.

### Recommendation

`delete the unreachable standalone ChatPage and route semantic Chat navigation to Home`

One canonical Chat renderer is enough. The current hidden page has no customer journey, creates substantial presentation drift risk, and makes automation less representative. Preserve explicit raw values for later navigation items rather than renumbering them accidentally; remove the obsolete `2` page branch, and make automation target **chat** post the same Home navigation signal used by real shortcuts. Shared provider and component code survives based on live Home/floating callers, not because the dead page referenced it.

### Question

Should we delete the hidden standalone `ChatPage` and make developer automation's **chat** target open the same canonical Chat inside Home that customers use?

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`delete the hidden standalone ChatPage and route semantic Chat navigation to Home`

Confirmed: remove `ChatPage`, the hidden page-index-2 branch/destination, exclusive presentation state/views/tests/previews, and accidental raw-index entry. Route developer automation target **chat** through the same `.navigateToChat` Home path used by customer shortcuts. Preserve explicit raw values for later navigation items rather than renumbering them accidentally. Keep `ChatProvider`, the canonical Home/floating timeline, Home composer/attachments, and shared components with other proven live callers.

IR-045 already deletes the standalone page's cloud Chat-app/persona picker and app-specific normal-Chat behavior. That settled child is not relocated into Home.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-525 - Multiple local Chat threads inside canonical Home Chat

### Settled parent requirement

IR-040 already retains complete multiple-chat behavior with local metadata authority:

- separate owner-scoped Chat threads and stable local identities;
- new-thread creation and selection;
- date-grouped listing, title, preview, message count, and activity ordering;
- search, rename, starring/starred filtering, and deletion;
- drafts and local kernel journals per thread; and
- no Firestore `/v2/chat-sessions` authority or cross-device catalog.

The **Multiple Chat Sessions** Settings toggle remains off by default. When off, the product uses the one default local Chat.

### Current presentation gap

The canonical Home Chat retained under IR-500 does not render a thread title, New Chat action, history list, or thread switcher. It only shows the active `ChatProvider.messages`, suggestions/errors, and the Home Ask composer.

The now-rejected standalone `ChatPage` showed only a small subset in its header: default/current-thread status and a New Chat button. Although `ChatSessionsSidebar` and another full history popover implement the complete list/search/star/rename/delete UI, they have no production construction at all; their only direct use is a `ViewExporter`/preview entry.

Therefore the Settings toggle can reinitialize `ChatProvider` into multi-chat mode, and other code can create a new session, but a normal customer has no reachable way to browse back to an older thread or use most behavior retained by IR-040. Deleting `ChatPage` does not create this gap; it exposes that the accepted local catalog was never integrated into the current Home product.

### Home-specific behavior needed

When Multiple Chat Sessions is enabled, canonical Home Chat needs one reachable catalog control. It should:

- show the current thread title or a clear **Chats** label;
- open a compact popover/tray over Home rather than create another page;
- use the locally authoritative session list and derived previews/counts;
- provide New Chat, selection, search, star filter, rename, star/unstar, and confirmed deletion;
- keep the selected thread in the same Home timeline/composer;
- close after selection without changing the Home destination; and
- remain absent when multiple sessions are disabled, leaving the one-default-Chat experience unchanged.

Creating or selecting an empty thread is an explicit Chat action, so Home should remain on the Chat stage for that interaction rather than immediately replacing it with the generic hub. A later ordinary Home entry can continue applying IR-500's settled resting policy based on the authoritative selected Chat state.

### Requirement materialized by this integration

> When the retained local multiple-thread option is enabled, Home must expose the complete local Chat catalog without reintroducing a second Chat page or message authority.

### Concrete choices

1. **Add a compact Chats catalog to Home Chat.** Use a named button/current-title control that opens a popover or tray with the complete IR-040 actions, while preserving Home's readable single-column timeline.
2. **Add an always-visible thread sidebar to Home.** Permanently split Home Chat into thread-list and timeline columns whenever multi-chat is enabled.
3. **Restore the standalone Chat destination for threads.** Keep Home for the default thread but require the second page for session management.
4. **Leave the toggle without usable thread navigation.** Keep the local catalog code and Settings option even though customers cannot reopen their other threads.

### Recommendation

`integrate a compact complete Chats catalog into Home Chat`

This fulfills the already-settled multiple-thread requirement while preserving the one Home/Chat destination and the 900-point readable timeline retained under IR-518. An always-visible sidebar would consume space for an optional, default-off feature; a clear popover/tray gives the full catalog on demand.
