## IR-660 - Durable local deletion of Focus history

### Requirement implied by the visible controls

> **Delete** and **Clear All History** must permanently remove the selected owner-scoped Focus records from the authoritative local database rather than only making them disappear temporarily from the page.

### Exact current behavior

Each Focus session row has a confirmation-protected **Delete** action, and the page menu has a confirmation-protected **Clear All History** action. `deleteSession` removes the row from the in-memory list and UserDefaults cache before launching a background deletion. A numeric ID may then delete the SQLite row, while a synchronized backend ID follows the duplicate-memory/backend branches rejected by IR-030. Errors are discarded, so a failed authoritative deletion can make the row look gone until the next reload restores it.

`clearAll` is more directly broken: it clears only the in-memory list, current status/app, and UserDefaults cache. It never deletes `focus_sessions` from SQLite. Refreshing or relaunching therefore reloads the supposedly cleared records from the authoritative database even though the confirmation says the operation cannot be undone.

### Decision

`keep individual Delete and Clear All History, and make both authoritative local deletions`

Confirmed: retain both visible controls and their existing confirmations. Individual **Delete** must permanently delete the exact owner-scoped Focus row from local GRDB before removing it from the displayed list. **Clear All History** must permanently delete all Focus rows owned by the current local owner in one authoritative local operation before clearing the page. Recompute current status/app from the newest surviving row after an individual deletion, and clear them when no row remains.

On local deletion failure, keep or restore the affected records on screen and present an actionable error rather than silently claiming success. Remove UserDefaults-cache mutation, synchronized/backend-ID branching, duplicate-memory deletion, backend DELETE, and swallowed-error behavior under IR-029/030. Do not change Focus analysis, notifications, settings, the retained summary/history presentation, or the Insights/Focus hub merely to repair deletion durability.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-661 - Truthful Focus monitoring status

### Requirement implied by the page header

> The Focus page may say **Monitoring** only while Focus analysis is enabled and the shared screen-capture runtime is genuinely healthy and running.

### Exact current behavior

`FocusViewModel.isMonitoring` returns only `FocusAssistantSettings.isEnabled`. The page therefore renders a green dot and **Monitoring** whenever the saved Focus Assistant switch is on, even if the user turned Capture off, Screen Recording permission is missing or stale, ScreenCaptureKit is unhealthy, or the proactive monitor failed to start. In those states no new screen frames reach Focus Assistant, so the label reports permission to run as though work is actually happening.

The current Home/top-bar Capture control already derives **On / Off / Blocked** from `ProactiveAssistantsPlugin.isMonitoring` plus the shared permission and capture-health state under IR-515. Focus additionally needs its own assistant switch: capture may be live for Rewind and other retained assistants while Focus itself is disabled.

### Decision

`make the Focus monitoring label follow the real capture runtime`

Confirmed: show green **Monitoring** only when Focus Assistant is enabled and the shared proactive screen-capture runtime is actually healthy and running. Show distinct truthful non-running states for **Focus disabled**, **Capture off**, and **Capture blocked** rather than deriving all status from the saved Focus toggle. Reuse the canonical live Capture/permission/health state retained by IR-515 and react to its runtime changes; do not create a second monitoring authority.

This changes only the Focus-page status presentation. Do not automatically enable Focus, start or stop Capture, request permission, alter assistant settings, change stored Focus results, or modify analysis/cooldown behavior merely because the page observes the real state.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-662 - Focus result-card wording for restored history

### Exact current behavior

When Focus history loads, `FocusStorage` assigns the newest persisted row's status and app to `currentStatus` and `currentApp`. The large Focus-page result card then displays the unqualified **Focused** or **Distracted** headline and app name whenever no live delay or cooldown banner has priority. It does not show the row's date, age, monitoring run, or whether the result was restored rather than newly analyzed.

Consequently, a result from an earlier day may continue to look current beside today's separately calculated statistics. IR-661 makes the small monitoring label truthful, but it does not relabel or hide this result card. IR-502 independently keeps Home's existing stale-result wording and is not changed here.

### Decision

`keep the Focus result card exactly as it is`

Confirmed: preserve the current unqualified **Focused / Distracted** headline, app subtitle, focus-rate leading value, colors, and status-banner precedence. Continue restoring `currentStatus` and `currentApp` from the newest locally loaded Focus row and showing that row without a timestamp, **Latest result** label, freshness threshold, current-run requirement, stale treatment, or automatic hiding when capture is off.

Keep IR-661's separate truthful **Monitoring / Focus disabled / Capture off / Capture blocked** header state. Do not infer that the monitoring label changes the retained result-card wording or stored Focus history.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-663 - Open-ended Focus-duration calculation

### Exact current behavior

Focus statistics infer each classification period from transition timestamps. For every older row, the period ends when the next newer classification begins. The newest row has no following transition, so `computeStats` always extends it from `createdAt` to the current wall-clock time. It ignores the row's optional `durationSeconds` value and has no persisted monitoring-run or stop boundary.

Stopping Capture clears detected-app, delay, and cooldown presentation state but does not close the newest classification period. Therefore a result recorded shortly before Capture stops, permission is lost, the app exits, or monitoring otherwise pauses can continue accumulating focused or distracted minutes until the page next computes statistics. The separately truthful non-running label under IR-661 does not stop this arithmetic.

### Decision

`keep the current Focus-duration calculation exactly as it is`

Confirmed: continue ending older classification periods at the next newer transition and extending the newest locally loaded row to the current time. Do not persist or honor an explicit end time, use `durationSeconds`, add monitoring-run identity, close the period when Focus/Capture stops or permission is lost, cap it at the last captured frame, or distinguish active from restored sessions for duration accounting.

Today's focused minutes, distracted minutes, focus rate, session count, top-distraction durations, and the result-card focus-rate value may continue using this inferred open-ended duration behavior even while IR-661 reports **Focus disabled**, **Capture off**, or **Capture blocked**. Do not change IR-662's retained result-card wording.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-664 - Focus totals while the page remains open

### Exact current behavior

The Focus page owns a one-second timer, but it assigns the timer's value to view state only while an analysis-delay or cooldown end time exists. That keeps the visible delay/cooldown countdowns moving. During the normal **Focused / Distracted** state, passing wall-clock time alone does not publish a view change even though `computeStats` would extend the newest classification to a later `Date()` under IR-663.

Consequently, today's focused minutes, distracted minutes, focus rate, and the result card's rate behave as a snapshot while the page remains otherwise idle. They may recompute when a new Focus row or another observed state change arrives, the page is reopened, deletion changes the store, or the user forces a refresh, but not simply because another minute elapsed.

### Decision

`keep the current snapshot refresh behavior exactly as it is`

Confirmed: do not add a per-minute or other normal-state display timer for focused minutes, distracted minutes, focus rate, session count, or the result-card value. Keep the existing one-second updates only for active analysis-delay and cooldown countdown presentation. Allow the normal totals to remain unchanged until another existing observed state change, page reconstruction, or explicit refresh causes recomputation.

This does not change IR-663's open-ended duration arithmetic; it preserves only when that arithmetic is visibly recomputed while the page is open. Do not add background model calls, database writes, or a new refresh control.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-665 - Owner-safe Focus state during account changes

### Relationship to the existing cloud-to-local decision

This is not a new Focus product or a redesign of its user experience. IR-029/030 already retain the Focus coach and simple page while moving durable results from cloud/duplicate authorities into each authenticated owner's local GRDB database. IR-665 specifies the in-memory owner transition required to finish that same-pattern adaptation safely.

### Exact current behavior

`RewindDatabase` correctly closes and retargets its pool to a separate per-owner directory when `RuntimeOwnerIdentity` changes, and `ProactiveStorage` can invalidate its cached pool. `FocusStorage`, however, is one process-wide `@MainActor` singleton. Its `sessions`, `currentStatus`, `currentApp`, detected-app/timer state, and shared `omi.focus.sessions` UserDefaults cache do not observe `runtimeOwnerDidChange`.

After an in-process account switch, the new owner's Focus page may therefore continue rendering the previous owner's in-memory rows. Its ordinary initial `refresh()` explicitly skips the local database load whenever `storage.sessions` is already non-empty, so the stale state can persist rather than merely flash. Home and notification suppression also read the same singleton status. The per-owner database files remain isolated; the leak is the surviving process memory and global cache around them.

### Decision

`finish the local adaptation with owner-safe Focus state transitions`

Confirmed: on every effective-owner change or sign-out, synchronously clear all visible/in-memory Focus sessions, current status/app, detected-app state, delay/cooldown state, loading ownership, and other owner-derived projections before any next-owner authenticated surface can render. Then load only the newly authorized owner's local Focus rows from that owner's retargeted GRDB database. Capture an owner/authorization generation around every asynchronous load, insert projection, refresh, delete, and clear operation, and reject a completion that returns after the owner changes.

Remove the process-wide Focus UserDefaults record cache under IR-029 rather than replacing it with another duplicate authority. Do not add an `ownerId` column merely to duplicate the existing per-owner database-directory boundary. Signing out or switching accounts must not delete the prior owner's database; their data remains in their own directory for a later authorized return. Preserve the same Focus analysis, page, status, history, and settings product behavior after the correct owner's state loads.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-666 - Small local retention boundary for Focus history

### Relationship to the existing cloud-to-local decision

This continues the same product pattern rather than redesigning Focus. The inherited Mac presentation loads only the most recent 30 days and no more than 500 Focus rows. The old cloud storage did not automatically delete everything outside that window; it merely remained a separate persistence authority. IR-029/030 already replace that cloud/duplicate authority with a small owner-local history, so the local database now needs an explicit boundary instead of accumulating records that the retained page never loads.

### Exact current behavior

`FocusStorage` asks owner-scoped GRDB for rows from the last 30 days with a limit of 500 and also trims its in-memory list to 500. Older or overflow rows can nevertheless remain indefinitely in `focus_sessions`, because the existing `deleteFocusSessionsOlderThan` helper has no caller and there is no row-count cleanup. Some rows may disappear incidentally when a linked screenshot is deleted, but that cascade is not a complete or intentional Focus-retention policy.

The legacy Firestore Focus store exposed paginated reads and individual deletion but no automatic 30-day or 500-row retention. The active inherited Mac path also uploaded duplicate Focus memories instead of using that legacy store. Therefore this decision preserves the Mac's existing visible history window while adapting persistence to the accepted local-only authority; it does not claim that cloud storage previously enforced the cleanup.

### Decision

`preserve the existing 30-day / 500-row Focus-history window and enforce it locally`

Confirmed: retain at most the newest 500 owner-scoped Focus rows and permanently remove any Focus row older than 30 days from the current owner's local GRDB database. Apply both limits as local maintenance after a successful Focus-row insert and when the current owner's Focus storage starts or refreshes, so long-running and returning installations converge on the same small boundary. Perform cleanup and the related insert/load work against the currently authorized owner's database, and fence asynchronous completion through the owner-generation rule in IR-665.

Keep the retained page's recent-history presentation, today's statistics, analysis behavior, and the individual **Delete** and **Clear All History** controls from IR-660. Do not add cloud retention, backend IDs, synchronization, a second cache, an archive, all-time browsing, or a user-configurable retention setting. This is the existing recent-history pattern made authoritative in local storage.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-669 - Local Insight-history loading boundary

### Relationship to the existing cloud-to-local decision

This preserves the inherited Insight-history pattern while moving its authority from cloud/duplicate storage to owner-local GRDB. It does not introduce a new retention or deletion policy.

### Exact current behavior

`InsightStorage` asks the backend for at most the newest 100 tagged Insight memories and keeps at most 100 items in its duplicate UserDefaults page cache. The page therefore works with a newest-100 window even though older records can remain stored by the backend. IR-034 already removes that backend authority and duplicate cache in favor of the tagged Insight records in local GRDB.

### Decision

`keep all Insights locally and continue loading the newest 100 on the page`

Confirmed: preserve the current newest-100 page-loading boundary, but read those records only from the currently authorized owner's local GRDB database. Keep older tagged Insight records stored locally even when they fall outside the page's loaded window. Do not automatically delete overflow records, impose a 100-record retention cap, or treat the page limit as a data-retention rule.

Keep the existing Insight page, search, category filters, read/unread state, dismiss/show-dismissed behavior, detail presentation, individual deletion, and clear-history controls retained by IR-034. Their authoritative local mutation and owner-transition behavior remain separate implementation details. Do not restore cloud reads, synchronization, backend IDs, or the duplicate UserDefaults array merely to preserve the newest-100 presentation pattern.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-670 - Owner-safe Insight state during account changes

### Relationship to the existing cloud-to-local decision

IR-669 decides how much Insight history the page loads. IR-670 separately decides whose history may occupy the shared in-memory page state. This preserves the inherited account-isolation pattern while replacing an authenticated cloud read with the current owner's local database.

### Exact current behavior

`InsightStorage` is one process-wide singleton. Its `insightHistory`, loading/error state, and shared `omi.advice.history` UserDefaults cache can survive an in-process sign-out or account switch. The current backend sync may eventually replace the list after another authenticated read, but the old owner's rows can remain visible while that asynchronous work runs. Removing cloud sync and the duplicate cache under IR-034 does not by itself make the singleton change owners.

### Decision

`clear the old in-memory Insight projection and load only the newly authorized owner's local history`

Confirmed: on every effective-owner change or sign-out, synchronously clear the displayed/in-memory Insight history, unread projection, loading ownership, error state, selection-derived state, and any other owner-derived page projection before a next-owner authenticated surface can render. Then load at most the newest 100 tagged Insight records from the newly authorized owner's local GRDB database under IR-669.

Capture the current owner/authorization generation around every asynchronous Insight load, refresh, insert projection, read, mark-all-read, dismiss, delete, and clear operation, and reject a completion that returns after the owner changes. Remove the global UserDefaults Insight array under IR-034 rather than partitioning that duplicate cache. Do not delete the prior owner's local database during sign-out or switching; their complete Insight history remains in their own database for a later authorized return.

Keep the same Insight page, filters, search, detail, read/dismiss/delete lifecycle, notification behavior, and newest-100 presentation after the correct owner's state loads. This is account isolation for the local adaptation, not a redesigned Insight workflow.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-671 - Authoritative local Clear All Insights

### Relationship to the existing pattern

The visible workflow and its promise remain unchanged: the user chooses **Clear All History**, confirms the destructive action, and expects their complete Insight history to be gone. The local adaptation changes only the persistence authority and repairs the inherited implementation's incomplete loaded-window deletion.

### Exact current behavior

The Insights page loads at most 100 records. `InsightStorage.clearAll` copies the IDs from that in-memory list, empties the duplicate UserDefaults cache, and issues one backend deletion per copied ID. If more than 100 Insight records exist, older records outside the loaded window are never included. A later refresh can therefore reveal old Insights after **Clear All History** claimed that all history was permanently removed.

### Decision

`keep Clear All History and make it delete every current-owner Insight locally`

Confirmed: retain the existing **Clear All History** control, wording, confirmation dialog, styling, and user workflow. After confirmation, delete every tagged Insight record in the currently authorized owner's local GRDB database in one authoritative local operation, including records older than the newest-100 page window in IR-669. Do not limit the operation to the currently loaded or filtered items.

Scope the deletion to Insight-tagged records only. Do not delete ordinary Memories, other locally stored product data, or another owner's database. On database failure, keep or restore the Insight list and present an actionable error rather than claiming that history was cleared. Remove the per-ID backend loop, UserDefaults mutation, cloud deletion, and swallowed-error behavior under IR-034.

This repairs the existing control's stated behavior while preserving its product pattern; it does not add a new Insight workflow.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-672 - Authoritative local deletion of one Insight

### Relationship to the existing pattern

The visible workflow remains unchanged: hover one Insight, choose **Delete**, confirm **Delete Insight**, and permanently remove only that selected Insight. The local adaptation replaces the backend as the mutation authority without redesigning the control.

### Exact current behavior

`InsightStorage.deleteInsight` removes the selected item from its in-memory list and duplicate UserDefaults cache immediately, then starts a backend-memory deletion. A backend failure is only logged. The page can therefore claim deletion even though the authoritative record was not deleted, and a later backend refresh can restore it.

### Decision

`keep individual Insight Delete and make the selected local record authoritative`

Confirmed: preserve the existing hover action, **Delete** label, **Delete Insight** confirmation dialog, Cancel action, styling, and user workflow. After confirmation, permanently delete exactly the selected tagged Insight record from the currently authorized owner's local GRDB database. Do not delete other Insights, ordinary Memories, or another owner's data.

Complete the authoritative local deletion before finalizing removal from the displayed projection, or restore the row if an optimistic presentation is used and the transaction fails. Present an actionable error on failure rather than silently claiming success. Remove duplicate UserDefaults mutation, backend-memory deletion, backend-ID routing, cloud refresh resurrection, and swallowed-error behavior under IR-034.

Keep search, filters, read/dismiss state, detail presentation, Clear All History from IR-671, and all other retained Insight behavior unchanged.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-673 - Authoritative local Insight dismissal

The visible workflow remains unchanged: the row's eye-slash action dismisses an Insight from the normal list, and the existing **Show Dismissed** toggle includes dismissed Insights again. The local adaptation changes only where the dismissed state is durably stored.

`InsightStorage.dismissInsight` changes the selected in-memory item and duplicate UserDefaults cache immediately, then starts a backend-memory read-status update with `isDismissed = true`. A backend failure is only logged, so the page may hide the Insight even though its authoritative dismissed state was not saved. A later backend refresh can reverse the apparent action.

### Decision

`keep Dismiss and Show Dismissed exactly as they behave, backed by local GRDB`

Confirmed: preserve the existing eye-slash hover action, no-confirmation dismissal workflow, normal-list hiding, **Show Dismissed** toggle, dismissed-row presentation, filtering, labels, styling, and behavior. Persist the selected tagged Insight record's dismissed flag only in the currently authorized owner's local GRDB database.

Complete the authoritative local update before finalizing the displayed projection, or restore the previous dismissed state if an optimistic presentation is used and the transaction fails. Present an actionable error rather than silently claiming success. Remove duplicate UserDefaults mutation, backend read-status updates, backend IDs, cloud refresh reversal, and swallowed-error behavior under IR-034.

Do not turn Dismiss into deletion, add a confirmation, automatically delete dismissed records, alter Show Dismissed, or affect ordinary Memories or another owner's data.

No product code has been changed.

The row tap calls `markAsRead` and then opens the detail sheet. `InsightStorage.markAsRead` changes the in-memory item and duplicate UserDefaults cache immediately, then starts a backend-memory read-status update. A backend failure is only logged, so the unread marker can disappear even though the authoritative state was not saved and a later backend refresh can reverse it.

### Decision

`keep open-and-mark-read exactly as it behaves, backed by local GRDB`

Confirmed: preserve the existing row selection, detail sheet, content, styling, unread emphasis, and automatic mark-read behavior. It must not mark other Insights read, dismiss or delete anything, or affect ordinary Memories or another owner's data.

The detail sheet must still open if the local read-state transaction fails. In that case, keep or restore the Insight's unread presentation and show an actionable error rather than pretending the read state was saved. Remove duplicate UserDefaults mutation, backend read-status updates, backend IDs, cloud refresh reversal, and swallowed-error behavior under IR-034.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-675 - Authoritative local Mark all read

### Relationship to the existing pattern

The visible workflow remains unchanged: when unread Insights exist, the page offers **Mark all read**, and selecting it removes the unread emphasis without dismissing or deleting Insight content. The local adaptation preserves that intended behavior while replacing the broken backend-saving sequence with one authoritative owner-local mutation.

### Exact current behavior

`InsightStorage.markAllAsRead` first changes every item in its loaded in-memory list to read and saves the duplicate UserDefaults cache. It then starts `markAllReadOnBackend`, but that function searches the already-modified list for unread IDs. It therefore finds none and sends no backend updates. The page looks correct temporarily, while a later backend reload can restore unread state. Records outside the newest-100 loaded window are not considered.

### Decision

`keep Mark all read as it is presented and persist its complete result locally`

Confirmed: preserve the existing **Mark all read** button, conditional visibility, label, placement, styling, and immediate user-facing meaning. When selected, mark every tagged Insight record belonging to the currently authorized owner as read in local GRDB, including dismissed Insights and older records outside the newest-100 page window. Active search, category, and dismissed filters must not narrow this all-history operation.

Do not dismiss, delete, rewrite, or otherwise alter Insight content. If the authoritative local transaction fails, keep or restore the previous unread states and present an actionable error rather than claiming success. Remove duplicate UserDefaults mutation, per-ID backend updates, the broken post-mutation unread-ID lookup, backend IDs, cloud refresh reversal, and swallowed-error behavior under IR-034.

This keeps the existing customer-visible pattern and makes its stated all-read result durable under local authority.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-683 - Customer-facing local Rewind screen-history workflow

### Relationship to existing decisions

IR-011 already deletes the shared-backend copy of Rewind activity while retaining local capture, OCR, video, SQLite indexing, and retrieval. The ordinary timeline loads sampled local frames for the selected day and refreshes today's view as new finalized frames become available.

Captured screenshots, OCR records, video chunks, and search indexes remain authoritative on the currently authorized Mac profile. The retained embedding service may compute vectors transiently through the managed boundary, but it does not turn the Rewind page or its history into a shared cloud product.

`keep the current customer-facing Rewind screen-history workflow with local authority`

Confirmed: preserve the existing Rewind overlay, `Command-Option-R` entrance, date-based history, search entry, grouped-results and timeline presentations, frame inspection, Settings entrance, and truthful Capture control as one customer-visible local product. Keep the current screen-history records, OCR, video, indexes, and retrieval authority local to the currently authorized Mac profile under IR-011/053.

## IR-684 - Rewind selected-day timeline and search boundary

### Exact current behavior

Rewind initializes its calendar selection to today. Choosing another date replaces the ordinary timeline with that calendar day's local screenshots. Entering a search term uses the same selected date as a hard boundary: both full-text OCR matching and semantic matching receive that day's start and end timestamps. Clearing the query returns to the ordinary timeline for the same selected day.

The selected date is visibly presented beside the search field. The current product does not offer an all-history query, a start/end range, a week/month aggregation, or a separate global-search mode from this page.

### Decision

`keep Rewind scoped to one selected calendar day at a time`

Confirmed: preserve today as the initial selection, the existing graphical date picker, and the rule that both ordinary timeline browsing and search operate only within the selected calendar day. Changing the date must reload or re-run the current query for that day; clearing search must return to that same day's ordinary timeline.

Do not add all-history, week/month, or arbitrary date-range search for the first release. Keep the selected date visible beside search so the scope remains understandable. This decision governs the date boundary only; frame sampling, search implementation, result presentation, and empty states remain separate children.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-685 - Rewind daily timeline sampling boundary

### Exact current behavior

Rewind can retain far more frames for one day than the page should mount at once. The ordinary selected-day load asks the local database for a target of 500 frames. If the day contains 500 or fewer records, it returns every record in chronological order. If the day contains more, it chooses approximately 500 records at even intervals across the complete day and orders those sampled frames from oldest to newest.

Sampling changes only the ordinary visible timeline projection. It does not delete the unsampled screenshots, OCR, video frames, or embeddings. Search queries the authoritative local indexes separately, so stored frames omitted from the ordinary 500-frame projection remain eligible to appear as matches.

### Decision

`keep the 500-frame evenly sampled daily timeline projection`

Confirmed: preserve every retained local Rewind record while limiting the ordinary selected-day timeline to at most 500 evenly distributed frames. Return all frames when the day contains no more than 500. Keep chronological navigation across the resulting projection and continue refreshing today's projection as finalized captures arrive.

Do not load every captured second into the visible timeline, delete records merely because they were not selected for the projection, or make ordinary timeline sampling limit search eligibility. Search result limits and presentation remain separate children.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-686 - Rewind combined text and semantic search

### Exact current behavior

After a 300-millisecond input debounce, Rewind searches the selected calendar day through two paths in parallel. Local SQLite full-text search matches expanded words across OCR content, app names, and window titles and returns at most 100 relevance-ordered screenshots. Semantic search transiently embeds the query through the managed embedding boundary retained by IR-053, compares it against locally stored screenshot vectors on the Mac, and returns at most 50 candidates.

Text matches remain first. Rewind appends only semantic-only candidates whose similarity is above 0.5 and whose screenshot ID is not already present. If query embedding or semantic comparison fails, that branch becomes an empty result while ordinary local full-text matches remain usable.

### Decision

`keep combined local text and local-vector semantic Rewind search`

Confirmed: preserve the debounced parallel search, 100-result full-text bound, 50-result semantic bound, 0.5 semantic inclusion threshold, text-first merge order, stable-ID duplicate removal, and selected-day boundary from IR-684. Continue using transient managed query embedding with local vector comparison and authority under IR-053.

Semantic-service failure must continue failing open to available local text results rather than blocking the complete Rewind search. Do not replace the combined search with semantic-only retrieval, upload authoritative Rewind history to create a cloud search product, or make the ordinary 500-frame timeline projection from IR-685 constrain search eligibility. Search result grouping and error presentation remain separate children.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-687 - Rewind nearby search-result grouping

### Exact current behavior

Search can return several captures of the same application and exact window only seconds apart. The result row uses one representative screenshot and displays the app, window title, time or time range, matching text snippet where available, thumbnail, number of screenshots, and group position. `keep the current same-context 30-second search-result grouping`

Do not flatten nearby near-duplicate frames into independent top-level rows, permanently collapse them into one stored record, or merge unrelated apps/windows merely because their text is similar. List/timeline presentation and navigation remain separate children.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-688 - Rewind search list and timeline presentations

When a nonblank query becomes active, Rewind defaults to a vertically scrollable grouped-results list. Each row gives the user enough app, window, time, snippet, thumbnail, and count context to select a useful moment without first opening every frame. `keep the grouped-results-first search workflow and both presentations`

Confirmed: preserve grouped List as the initial active-search presentation, row selection into that group's Timeline, the existing List/Timeline toggle, back and Escape return from a search timeline to the results list, and query clearing back to the ordinary selected-day timeline.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-689 - Reachable Rewind manual frame navigation

### Exact current behavior

The live Rewind page presents one large selected frame above a full-width timeline. The user can click or drag the timeline, scroll on the page, or press the left and right arrow keys to move through the active ordinary-day or selected-search-group projection. Navigation clamps at the first and last frame and displays the current index, total frame count, and compact timestamp.

Frame images load asynchronously. Each request carries a fresh identity and source token so a slower result from an earlier scrub position cannot replace the image for the user's newest selection. Search-results list mode reserves left/right navigation for the opened timeline rather than moving the list.

### Decision

`keep the reachable manual Rewind frame-navigation pattern`

Confirmed: preserve timeline click and drag, page scroll, left/right arrow navigation, bounded first/last behavior, current-position and timestamp presentation, and newest-request-only image application. Keep the same controls for the ordinary selected-day timeline and the timeline inside a selected search-result group.

Do not add autoplay, playback-speed controls, or a second full-screen player to the reachable page merely because dormant player code exists elsewhere. That unreachable code and selected-frame load failures remain separate children.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-690 - Rewind selected-frame load failure presentation

### Exact current behavior

When navigation selects another frame, Rewind updates the current index before the asynchronous image load finishes and keeps the last valid `currentImage` in memory. If the requested image loads, that image replaces the old one. If it fails, Rewind leaves the selected index in place, stops the loading state, and continues displaying the last successfully loaded image. The position/timestamp and search-overlay inputs can therefore describe the newly selected record while the visible image remains from the earlier record.

An active video chunk that is still being written is not deleted. A failed frame from an older chunk classified as corrupted schedules the existing chunk cleanup and timeline refresh; other failures are logged without adding a visible unavailable-frame state.

### Decision

`keep the current selected-frame failure behavior exactly as implemented`

Confirmed: when a newly selected Rewind frame cannot be loaded, preserve the selected index, current loading-state completion, last successfully displayed image, existing logging, active-chunk protection, and corrupted-old-chunk cleanup/refresh behavior exactly as they are. Do not add a **Frame unavailable** or still-saving presentation, clear the old image, automatically skip to another frame, realign the visible timestamp to the prior image, or otherwise repair this mismatch.

This is an explicit decision to retain the current presentation despite the possible image/index/timestamp mismatch. It does not change the normal successful frame-load or latest-request protection accepted under IR-689.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-692 - Unreachable alternate Rewind timeline and screenshot preview

### Exact current behavior

`RewindTimelineView.swift` contains an older alternate timeline with per-app colored activity markers, app-icon jumps, drag/scroll selection, and thumbnail hover previews. The same file contains a separate `ScreenshotPreviewView` with previous/next/close controls, search highlighting, visible extracted OCR text, selection, and a Copy action. ## IR-908 - Rewind quiet refresh of today's timeline

### Exact current behavior

After Rewind successfully initializes, its view model checks every three seconds for changes while the selected date is today. ## IR-909 - Rewind selected-day midnight boundary

### Exact current behavior

The reachable daily timeline, its quiet refresh, full-text search, and semantic-search candidate scan calculate a selected day's range from that day's start at midnight through the following day's midnight. Their database comparisons include both endpoints: the start is greater-than-or-equal and the end is less-than-or-equal.

Consequently, a screenshot whose timestamp is exactly the following midnight can qualify for both the preceding day and the new day. This is a narrow boundary case; timestamps away from that exact instant remain assigned to the expected selected day.

### Decision

`keep the inclusive next-midnight boundary exactly as implemented`

Confirmed: preserve the greater-than-or-equal start and less-than-or-equal following-midnight comparisons, including the possibility that an exact-midnight screenshot appears in both adjacent selected days. Do not change the end comparison to an exclusive boundary or otherwise normalize the daily range during the first-release adaptation.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-910 - Rewind position after newly captured screenshots arrive

### Exact current behavior

On the initial nonempty load, the reachable Rewind page selects the last screenshot in its oldest-first daily array, so it begins at the newest available frame. When a later refresh changes that array, the page looks up the ID of the screenshot at the user's previous index. If that screenshot still exists, Rewind changes the numeric index as needed to keep showing the same frame and does not reload or advance to newly appended captures.

If the prior frame is no longer present, such as after resampling or deletion, Rewind instead selects the last frame in the new array, resets the search-group index, and schedules that newest frame for display.

### Decision

`keep Rewind's current-position preservation exactly as implemented`

Confirmed: preserve initial selection of the newest frame, continued display of the same identified screenshot when later captures arrive, absence of automatic live-edge following, manual navigation to newer captures, and fallback to the newest available frame when the previous frame disappears exactly as they are.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-911 - Rewind statistics state with no reachable presentation

### Exact current behavior

`RewindViewModel` publishes a tuple containing total screenshot count, indexed screenshot count, and total Rewind storage size. After initial loading it asynchronously asks `RewindIndexer` for those values. It also listens for every new-frame notification, throttles the stream to at most one update every two seconds, and repeats the statistics request. The indexer counts database records and asks storage to calculate total disk use.

No reachable Rewind view reads or renders this published tuple. The public `refreshStats` helper also has no caller. These calculations therefore perform database and filesystem work without changing anything the customer can see.

### Decision

`keep the undisplayed Rewind statistics wiring exactly as implemented`

Confirmed: preserve the published statistics state, initial asynchronous calculation, throttled new-frame listener, repeated database and storage-size calculations, unused public refresh helper, and absence of a visible statistics presentation exactly as they are. Do not remove this wiring or add a new statistics UI during the first-release adaptation.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-922 - Production Local Agent HTTP API for other programs on the same Mac

### Exact current behavior

The production desktop app contains a second, optional entrance to local Omi tools that is separate from the managed Pi agent path. `LocalAgentAPIServer` binds an HTTP listener only to `127.0.0.1`, using port `47778` by default. Its unauthenticated health route identifies the running local service. Listing tools through `GET /v1/local/tools` and executing one through `POST /v1/local/tool` require a bearer token stored in the app's scoped macOS Keychain service. A persisted enabled flag causes `OmiApp` to start the listener again on later launches.

This HTTP server exposes a generated ten-tool `local-agent-api` projection and then dispatches ordinary calls into the same Swift `ChatToolExecutor` used behind retained agent behavior. It is therefore an additional access path for another trusted local program, not the managed Pi harness itself. Managed Pi uses `pi-mono-extension -> OMI_BRIDGE_PIPE -> ChatToolExecutor`; the generic `omi-tools-stdio` child-process path is a third, callerless path deleted under IR-015/S-05.

The enablement, token rotation, connection testing, and prompt-copy flows are coupled to the Memory Export / external-agent connector product already rejected under IR-047 and IR-015. The API-specific projection also includes `get_local_status` and historical `get_screenshot` wrappers that are not advertised to Pi. Pi separately retains its managed tool projection, including approved screen/context tools such as `capture_screen` and `get_work_context`.

### Decision

`delete external Local Agent HTTP access while preserving the managed Pi tool path`

Confirmed: remove `LocalAgentAPIServer`, `LocalAgentAPISettings`, the production `127.0.0.1:47778` listener, `/health`, `/v1/local/tools`, `/v1/local/tool`, persisted enablement and port state, scoped Keychain bearer-token lifecycle, app-launch startup, Memory Export connection setup/testing coupling, generated `local-agent-api` adapter projection, API-only wrappers, and tests/fixtures that exist only for this external HTTP surface.

Do not delete or replace the managed Pi harness, retained local Node runtime, packaged Pi extension, `OMI_BRIDGE_PIPE`, `AgentRuntimeProcess` authorization/relay path, `ChatToolExecutor`, or any tool capability retained by Pi merely because the deleted API also exposed or executed it. Delete the separate callerless `omi-tools-stdio` process under IR-015/S-05 without routing Pi through it. Do not convert the API-only wrappers into new Pi tools as part of this deletion. Keep shared loopback HTTP parsing needed by the separately retained test-only `DesktopAutomationBridge` on port 47777, relocating or renaming it if necessary rather than deleting that test safety boundary.

## IR-923 - Managed Pi background agents and visible Agent Pill lifecycle

### Exact current behavior

A background agent is a separate canonical agent session/run that can continue while the user remains in the main or floating conversation. The bundled local Node kernel owns execution and durable run truth. `AgentPillsManager` owns only the visible, owner-scoped projection shown through the floating bar and notch UI.

The lifecycle can spawn one visible run or a bounded batch, present queued/starting/running/done/stopped/failed state, stream progress, open the run as a conversation, show returned artifacts, stop the active run, and send a follow-up into the same canonical session. A follow-up arriving during active work first attempts to cancel the current run; early or temporarily blocked follow-ups are queued until the canonical session can accept them.

The Mac reconstructs pills from the local kernel after runtime readiness or restart, reconciles visible state against canonical session/run inspection, and materializes a terminal completion block into the exact local journal surface that produced the run. Account-owner fencing rejects stale spawn receipts and clears projections across owner changes. Finished pills can be dismissed manually, expire ten minutes after being viewed while not actively open, and are preferentially trimmed when the visible collection reaches its soft eight-pill cap. Completed output can include user-facing artifact projections.

IR-603 already deletes the separate cosmetic Claude title/acknowledgement request while preserving deterministic local titles and authoritative router-supplied metadata. IR-800 pins normal and background execution to managed Pi and deletes Claude ACP, Hermes, OpenClaw, directed-provider routing, and provider-specific Pill presentation. IR-028 separately deletes backend-owned workstream and task-attached cloud-agent continuity; that does not delete these finite local managed-Pi background runs.

### Decision

`keep the complete local managed-Pi background-agent and Agent Pill lifecycle`

Confirmed: preserve managed-Pi spawn and bounded batch spawn, canonical local session/run ownership, visible Agent Pills and all current statuses, progress and conversation projection, artifacts, Stop/cancellation, same-session follow-ups and their active-run interruption/queueing behavior, restart/runtime restoration, reconciliation, owner fencing, local terminal-journal materialization, manual dismissal, viewed-finished ten-minute expiry, and soft eight-pill trimming exactly as the retained architecture provides.

Delete provider-specific residue through IR-800 and the cosmetic title model call through IR-603. Do not restore cloud Agent VMs, remote workstreams, backend run authority, or alternate agent harnesses. Do not replace the retained Pill lifecycle with a new background-work system for v1.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-924 - Delivery of completed background-agent results into a live voice session

### Exact current behavior

The local kernel and Agent Pill can know that a background run finished while an already-live OpenAI Realtime or Gemini Live conversation remains unaware of that completion. `AgentCompletionVoiceDelivery`, started at app launch, observes agent-run projections for a new transition into terminal state on designated background surfaces and asks `DesktopCoordinatorService` for the canonical completion delta addressed to the realtime-voice surface.

The delta is bounded to at most five unseen completed runs from the previous hour. It is injected into the current provider session as untrusted context rather than a new user command or a synthetic assistant response. The voice model can mention the completion at its next natural turn boundary and answer follow-ups without the bridge independently speaking or taking output authority.

Delivery uses a per-surface seen-ID and completed-time checkpoint. The checkpoint advances only after the live provider session accepts the context. A failed or temporarily unavailable injection therefore remains eligible for retry. The service retries when a voice session connects, when a warm session opens an input window, or when another relevant terminal transition arrives. With no live voice session it does nothing and leaves eligible recent completion state unacknowledged.

The current trigger set includes `floating_bar`, `service`, and `workstream`. IR-028 rejects backend-owned workstream and task-attached cloud-agent continuity, while IR-923 retains local managed-Pi background runs and IR-061 retains both realtime voice providers.

### Decision

`keep bounded managed-Pi completion context in live voice and remove the rejected workstream trigger`

Confirmed: preserve terminal-transition observation for retained background surfaces, canonical local completion-delta reads, the previous-hour window, five-run bound, untrusted-context marking, no immediate synthetic response, delivery only into a live session, retry on provider readiness, and exactly-once checkpoint advancement only after successful injection. Keep the behavior compatible with both retained OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live sessions.

Remove `workstream` from the trigger set and delete any coupling that exists only for the rejected workstream product. Keep `service` only for genuinely retained local managed-Pi service runs. Do not add another model call, cloud completion store, immediate spoken interruption, or second completion authority.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-925 - Notch task-save receipts and conversation-end follow-up cards

### Exact current behavior

`NotchMomentsCoordinator` listens to the real transcription lifecycle and the incomplete-task projection, then routes two silent cards through the existing floating/notch notification path. It does not own notch geometry or realtime voice behavior.

While transcription is active, a newly appearing incomplete task can produce a live **“✓ Saved to Tasks — …”** receipt. The coordinator ignores ordinary backlog loads, requires a previously unseen task identity with a creation time no more than two minutes old, and deduplicates in-flight verification. Before claiming success it currently calls `APIClient.getActionItem`, requires the backend response to identify the same active task, and confirms that the task remains in the incomplete local projection. Failed confirmation suppresses the receipt. The card's Undo action deletes the most recently receipted task through `TasksStore`; Review opens the main Tasks page.

On the transition from transcribing to stopped, the coordinator counts incomplete tasks whose identities were absent from the conversation-start baseline and whose creation times are at or after the recorded session start. A positive count produces **“1 follow-up ready”** or **“N follow-ups ready”** with **“Conversation ended”**. Zero produces no card. Review opens the Tasks page. Starting observation mid-conversation establishes a baseline from that moment rather than counting the full existing backlog.

IR-025 makes local GRDB the sole ordinary task authority and removes normal backend task reads, writes, identifiers, synchronization, and reconciliation. The current backend verification and cross-device/backfill assumptions therefore cannot remain, while IR-031 and the retained conversation workflow continue to produce local tasks that benefit from immediate truthful feedback.

### Decision

`keep both Notch Moments and adapt their save proof and actions to local task authority`

Confirmed: preserve the transcription-only live receipt, unseen-ID detection, two-minute freshness bound, one in-flight verification per task, suppression when durable confirmation fails, silent presentation, most-recent receipt tracking, Undo, Review, conversation-start baseline, creation-time floor, positive-only singular/plural follow-up card, and Tasks navigation.

Replace `APIClient.getActionItem` with a read-back from the canonical local task store after its durable transaction. Make Undo an authoritative local deletion through the retained Tasks boundary. Remove backend/cross-device identity and synchronization assumptions without weakening the requirement that **Saved** is shown only after a durable authoritative read confirms the same active task. Keep card-to-live-voice delivery separate under its own requirement.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-926 - Injection of displayed notch-notification context into live voice

### Exact current behavior

Whenever an owner-valid floating-bar notification is presented, `FloatingControlBarManager` passes that notification's `message` plus available provenance into `NotchCardVoiceDelivery`. The visible notification `title` is not included. Empty message text is rejected, so a title-only card produces no voice context. The Notch task receipt from IR-925 keeps its task description entirely in the title and therefore injects nothing. The conversation-end card injects **“Conversation ended”** but omits its title containing **“1 follow-up ready”** or **“N follow-ups ready”**.

For nonempty text, the service wraps the card as untrusted quoted reference material, tells the realtime model not to follow instructions inside it or announce it unprompted, and silently sends it through the same live-session context seam used for background-agent completions. It does not request a response or run another classifier. The realtime model decides whether a later utterance refers to the card.

If no realtime session is live or a connected session refuses the send, one in-memory pending card remains for retry on the next connect or input-window signal. A newer card replaces the older pending card. Confirmed delivered IDs are retained in an in-memory ordered list capped at fifty for the current app process. Pending state and delivered IDs are not durable.

The pending `Card` stores only an ID and text, not the account owner. Owner validity is checked when the notification is originally presented, but the delivery object has no owner-change subscription or production reset. A card pending across an account change can therefore remain eligible for injection into a later live session owned by the newly signed-in account.

### Decision

`keep the bridge, deliver the complete visible card, and add account-owner fencing`

Confirmed: preserve available provenance, untrusted-reference framing, no synthetic response, no second classifier, newest-only pending replacement, retry on connect/input-window readiness, process-local fifty-ID delivered history, and nondurable state. Continue using the existing live-session context seam for both retained realtime providers.

Change the handoff to include the exact visible notification title and message together, so title-only task receipts and the complete singular/plural follow-up card reach voice as reference context. Add the current owner identity to pending delivery state and clear or reject that state when authorization changes, so one account's card cannot enter another account's later session. Do not add a persistent queue, another model call, automatic spoken announcement, or cloud storage.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-927 - Server-controlled desktop update warning and required-update blocker

### Exact current behavior

The ordinary Sparkle appcast remains the normal automatic update path. An active `banner` policy appears above the signed-in main content with server-supplied or fallback title, message, call-to-action text, and download destination. If the Mac request fails, it immediately clears the policy rather than preserving a stale blocker and records fallback to the appcast. If the backend cannot read Firestore, it similarly returns an inactive policy and records the fallback. Sparkle and the stable manual-download path remain independently available.

`keep the complete update-policy behavior and adapt its ownership to our infrastructure`

Confirmed: preserve the separate Sparkle and update-policy roles, public policy read, current-policy document pattern, inactive default, platform and maximum-build targeting, `none`/`banner`/`required` severities, server/fallback copy behavior, dismissible banner and policy-ID persistence, non-dismissible required overlay, download validation and stable fallback, launch/activation refresh, five-minute minimum interval, and fail-open clearing on Mac or backend failure.

## IR-928 - Automatic RAM-pressure remediation and extreme-memory app relaunch

### Exact current behavior

This requirement concerns temporary process RAM, not the customer's saved Memory records. `ResourceMonitor` starts during app launch, samples immediately and every thirty seconds, retains twenty recent samples, updates bounded resource/component diagnostics, and evaluates memory pressure through one episode tracker with hysteresis.

The default warning, critical, and extreme thresholds are 500 MB, 800 MB, and 3,000 MB. Warning and critical recovery boundaries are 450 MB and 720 MB. Warning breadcrumbs are limited to one per five minutes. A critical episode reports on entry and at most every fifteen minutes while sustained, while remediation can run on entry and again after five minutes if pressure persists. Fast growth above 50 MB per minute over five samples produces a diagnostic breadcrumb but no separate repair action.

Critical remediation clears queued assistant work, trims in-memory transcript segments through the AppState-owned closure after those segments have been persisted in SQLite, flushes the active Rewind video chunk, clears Focus-assistant pending work, and currently pauses `AgentSyncService` for sixty seconds before resuming it. It logs memory before and after and records Sentry diagnostics outside non-production builds.

At or above 3,000 MB in a production build, one automatic-restart attempt is armed for that app session. The monitor records a fatal Sentry event, waits three seconds, launches a new instance of the exact running bundle through `/usr/bin/open -n`, and terminates the old app only after that relaunch process starts successfully. A relaunch failure leaves the old app running and clears the one-shot flag so a later sample can retry. Non-production builds do not auto-restart.

IR-001 deletes the cloud Agent VM and its local-to-VM synchronization lifecycle. The `AgentSyncService` pause/resume action therefore has no surviving workload, while the remaining cleanup targets are retained local capture, transcript, Focus, and proactive systems.

### Decision

`keep automatic RAM remediation and extreme-memory relaunch while removing the rejected AgentSync step`

Confirmed: preserve launch/termination monitoring, thirty-second sampling, twenty-sample trend window, 500/800/3,000 MB thresholds, 450/720 MB hysteresis, warning/report/remediation cooldowns, growth diagnostics, component diagnostics, assistant pending-work clearing, persisted-transcript trimming, Rewind chunk flush, Focus pending-work clearing, before/after logging, bounded Sentry behavior, production-only one-shot extreme response, three-second reporting flush, relaunch of the exact bundle, termination only after successful relaunch start, and retry eligibility after relaunch failure.

Remove only the `AgentSyncService` pause, delayed resume, and related diagnostics/tests because the synchronized cloud Agent VM product is rejected. Do not add a replacement synchronization service, user confirmation prompt, different thresholds, or another restart mechanism during the first-release adaptation.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-929 - Runtime self-install from a DMG or App Translocation into `/Applications`

### Exact current behavior

This is a runtime first-launch gate, separate from the IR-892 release workflow that constructs, signs, notarizes, and publishes the DMG. Before databases, defaults, capture, agents, or ordinary background services start, `OmiApp` asks `AppInstaller` whether the exact running bundle is located under `/Volumes` or an App Translocation mount. Downloads, development checkouts, named test bundles in ordinary locations, and processes carrying the explicit skip environment variable are left in place.

For an unambiguous installer location, the destination is `/Applications/<current bundle filename>`. If a copy already exists, numeric build comparison prevents an equal or older DMG build from replacing it; the installed same/newer copy has quarantine cleared and is relaunched instead. A newer source first copies into a same-volume staging path and only then atomically replaces or moves into the destination, so a failed copy preserves the existing installed app.

After installation, the helper recursively clears the quarantine attribute because the user has already passed the first-open Gatekeeper check and leaving quarantine can translocate the installed copy again. It schedules a delayed `open` of the installed bundle, then terminates the current process so the single-instance lock is released first.

A shared UserDefaults counter permits at most two consecutive gate-triggered relaunch attempts. If installation fails or the relaunch loop persists, the helper leaves the current app running, shows manual move-to-Applications guidance, and resets the loop counter. A failure to schedule relaunch also leaves the current app alive.

### Decision

`keep and rebrand the guarded runtime self-install behavior`

Confirmed: preserve detection limited to mounted-volume and translocated paths, the harness escape hatch, `/Applications` destination, numeric no-downgrade comparison, launch of an installed same/newer build, copy-to-staging before atomic replacement, preservation of an existing install on failure, post-first-open quarantine clearing, delayed relaunch, termination only after relaunch scheduling succeeds, two-attempt loop guard, manual-install fallback, and fail-open running-in-place behavior.

Adapt the app names, user-facing guidance, logs where product identity appears, bundle filename expectations, skip-environment-variable identity, and focused tests to our product. Keep this runtime gate separate from IR-892's artifact construction/signing/notarization/publication responsibilities and do not introduce another installer framework.

No product code has been changed.

### Decision

`delete the complete standalone Remotion marketing-video project`

Confirmed: remove both compositions, every scene/component/style, public logo, README, Remotion/PostCSS/TypeScript/ESLint/Prettier configuration, package manifest, package lock, and project-specific ignore file beneath `desktop/macos/demo/`. Remove any newly discovered live reference that exists only to invoke this project.

Do not port or rebrand the stale videos for v1. Preserve their historical source through Git history. Future marketing material must be created from the finalized product and fact-checked disclosures under an explicitly owned website/marketing workflow rather than treated as a Mac runtime dependency.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-936 - Orphaned compiled Claude ACP bridge under `desktop/macos/acp-bridge/`

### Exact current behavior

`desktop/macos/acp-bridge/` contains only one 1,067-line generated JavaScript file, `dist/index.js`. It describes itself as a local bridge between Omi's JSON-lines protocol and the Agent Client Protocol used by `claude-code-acp`. Its intended flow spawns the external Claude ACP process, performs Claude authentication, manages ACP sessions, and relays Omi tool calls through a Unix socket.

This directory is not a complete runnable package or an independent retained agent system. It has no package manifest or source tree, and the generated file imports `session-manager.js`, `oauth-flow.js`, and `omi-tools-stdio.js`, none of which exists beside it. No production launcher or package path references this directory. The live non-Pi implementation instead remains in `desktop/macos/agent/src/adapters/acp.ts` and related adapter registry, policy, and tests.

IR-800 already selects managed Pi as the only normal-chat and background-agent harness and deletes Claude ACP, Hermes, OpenClaw, provider selection, customer-Claude authentication, and provider-specific residue. The standalone compiled directory is a forgotten generated child of that same rejected ACP path.

### Decision

`delete the orphaned compiled ACP bridge as an explicit IR-800 child`

Confirmed: remove `desktop/macos/acp-bridge/` completely together with the live Claude ACP adapter, activation and registry branches, Claude authentication, external-adapter policy, focused tests, configuration, packaging residue, and documentation already rejected by IR-800.

Preserve `desktop/macos/agent/` as the retained local Node runtime, its managed Pi adapter, packaged extension, `OMI_BRIDGE_PIPE` bridge, Swift `ChatToolExecutor`, tool authorization, local journal, and accepted normal-chat and background-agent behavior. Delete the callerless `omi-tools-stdio` process with the alternate-adapter plumbing under IR-015/S-05; do not delete or weaken Pi merely because the obsolete ACP bridge also relayed Omi tools.

No product code has been changed.

## IR-937 - Live packaged managed-Pi provider and tool extension under `desktop/macos/pi-mono-extension/`

### Exact current behavior

`desktop/macos/pi-mono-extension/` is a live package, unlike the orphaned ACP bridge in IR-936. The managed-Pi adapter resolves its `index.ts`, local and release build scripts copy it and its production dependencies into the app bundle, signed-artifact checks require it, and the focused agent harness runs its package tests.

The extension currently combines surviving and rejected behavior in one file. It registers Omi's OpenAI-compatible provider against `https://api.omi.me/v2`, advertises Omi Sonnet and Omi Opus, adds optional four-provider BYOK headers, forwards request-correlation and reasoning-lane metadata, registers the scoped Omi tool manifest over the private Unix-socket bridge, retains the rejected skill-search/load compatibility, classifies Pi's general shell/file calls through a dangerous-command denylist, and appends every tool call/result to `~/.omi/pi-mono-audit.log`. No other live Mac component reads that audit log.

Every boundary is already decided: IR-113/800 retain managed Pi and its managed-Claude proxy; IR-922/923 retain the private typed-tool route; IR-062 deletes product-wide BYOK; IR-605 pins normal Chat to Sonnet and removes Opus selection; IR-217 deletes Pi skill compatibility; IR-049 deletes broad shell/file execution and its exclusive denylist/audit surfaces; and IR-871/931 replace Omi's endpoint and local identity with this product's owned names.

### Decision

`retain and narrow the packaged managed-Pi extension according to prior decisions`

Confirmed: preserve the package, managed provider registration, one retained Sonnet-class route, authenticated request, safe request-correlation and reasoning-lane headers, scoped typed-tool registration and Unix-socket relay, packaging/signing wiring, focused package tests, and generic code genuinely required by those paths.

Delete four-provider BYOK environment/header propagation; Opus registration, aliases, and tests; rejected skill discovery/search/load registration; general shell/file built-in exposure; the broad-command and arbitrary-write denylist classifiers; the unconsumed broad-execution audit log and its `~/.omi` path; and exclusive fixtures/tests/docs. Replace Omi provider/model/endpoint/protocol-visible identity with the fork's owned identity while keeping internal transport compatibility only where a surviving caller requires it.

Do not delete the extension or replace managed Pi with ACP, Hermes, OpenClaw, direct customer keys, or a new harness. This is the source-level reconciliation of already-approved behavior, not a new agent architecture.

No product code has been changed.
